| Text tool, the edit ends with characters in it | `text.box {page, x, y, text}` and, for a drag, `width` and `height` (all in paper inches, the middle of the box); a click on a shape sends `shape.set_text` as the Pointer Tool's edit does |
| Text Block tool, a drag released | `text.block_move {id, dx, dy}`, `text.block_resize {id, x, y, width, height}` (the corner at (0, 0) of the block's frame and its sides along its axes), `text.block_rotate {id, by}`; the block drawn is read from `draw::text_block_place` |
| Home, Paragraph, Rotate Text | `text.block_rotate {id, by: 90}` for every shape selected (one `command.batch`, one undo step, for several) |

* Our rule (the style goes to the connectors selected and, with the page itself selected, to the default for new connectors). The window sends the connectors among the shapes selected (`ShapePlacement.one_d`), and the page's default when it finds none, including with shapes selected that are no connectors. Show Line Jumps is the page's and never a selected connector's. The marks on Right-Angle, Straight Lines and Curved Lines are the page's default and are shown only while no connector is selected: the engine has no reader for a selected connector's own style (`connector_path` answers for a path of lines only, and a curve is not one).
* Our rule (describe the reference application's galleries). The Themes strip shows the first three themes of `theme.list` and the arrow the whole list under a **Built-In** heading; the Variants strip shows the four variants of the page's theme. A theme or variant applies to the page on view and not to the first page. **A tile under the pointer is previewed** on the page (the page is drawn from a copy of the drawing with the theme applied, and nothing is edited); a tile's tooltip is its name. A right click on a tile of the Themes menu shows the two rows under the tiles (a context menu cannot open inside a menu in egui, as the card of a folded group found: `controls.rs`, `fold_card`). The **Colors** menu lists the four colour variants (`theme.variant {colors}`), because the engine cannot give a page the colours of another theme; Effects, Connectors, Embellishments, Create New Theme Colors and Apply Theme to New Shapes have no command behind them and are quiet.
* Our rule (no specification says when the dialog applies). The Page Setup dialog works on a draft and applies on OK; Cancel and Esc send nothing. A size typed as a custom size is in inches, and turning the orientation on the Page Size tab swaps the two typed sizes. A size typed on its own makes the page the way its sides say: the orientation command goes only if the orientation was chosen in the dialog. The dialog works on the page that was on view when it opened (or the one named); a refusal (a text that is not a number, a page taken away) is told in the dialog, which stays open. The Layout and Routing tab works (in "The page's routing settings"), so does the Alt Text tab (in "Alt text and the accessibility check"), and the Print Setup tab's print zoom, sheets, margins, centring and grid are drawn quiet with the values the page's cells hold (no command writes them).
* Our rule (the tab menu's Insert opens Page Setup on Page Properties). Insert makes the page first (`page.add {like}`), shows it, and opens Page Setup on it, so a Cancel keeps the page (Undo takes it away): the dialog cannot come before a page that does not exist.
* Our rule (describes the Page Properties tab and the Pages group). The tab has the Name box (at most 31 characters, as the box of a tab is, and refused in words when it is another page's name or "page" and digits), **Type** (Foreground or Background; Background is quiet, with a tooltip, for the only page that is not a background) and **Background** (None, and the drawing's background pages but the page itself and those that have it for their own background); OK sends `page.type` and `page.background` for what changed, in the one batch. **Background Page** adds a background page like the page on view and shows it, so that what is drawn on it is where the person is; **Duplicate This Page** and the tab menu's Duplicate copy a page and show the copy (a copy is the page on view in the window, whoever sent `page.duplicate`); **Blank Page** keeps the page on view. The tabs of background pages come after the others, set apart by a gap and a line, and are not dragged; the tooltip of one says it is a background page. The **Measurement units** box of the tab has no command and is not drawn.
* Our rule. The window reads the drawing again after any command that may grow a page (`shape.drop`, `shape.move`, `shape.align`, `shape.resize`, `shape.rotate`, `shape.flip`, `edit.paste`, `shape.duplicate`, `text.box`) when the page has Auto Size on. **A view of its own (one that is not Fit) follows a drawing that carried**: the distance a top-level shape the command did not name has moved is added to the middle of the view, so the shapes stay where they were on the screen. A view that follows Fit shows the whole page whatever it grows to. With no such shape (the first shape put on a page), the view stays.
* Our rule (no specification says whether the tool stays on). The Text tool is used up by the box it opens: the Pointer Tool is back while the person types, and the box is sent when the edit ends with characters in it (Esc, Ctrl+Enter or a click away), so a box left empty is never made. A click or a drag places the box on the grid, and Alt turns the grid off. While a new box is open there is no shape for the formatting controls to act on.
* Our rule ("moves, resizes and rotates the text area apart from the shape"). With the tool on, a click selects a shape (a top-level one) and draws its block: the rectangle, the pin it turns about, the eight handles of the block's own frame and a rotation handle above the edge that is the top of the text; the shape's own handles are not drawn. A drag of the block's body is a move (the block's middle goes to the grid), a drag of a handle a resize, and a drag of the rotation handle a turn in the steps of the shape's own rotation handle. Each is drawn from a preview while the button is down and sent once on release. The tool stays on until Esc or the Pointer Tool.

## Find and Replace

`edit.find` and `edit.replace` are Home > Editing > Find > Find... and Replace... (and "Replace text"). The window's two
dialogs run them (`crates/ui-egui/src/find_dialog.rs`, `window.find`); a program calls them straight, and neither opens a dialog. The engine is `crates/engine/src/draw/find/` (`pattern.rs` the pattern
and the search of one string, `walk.rs` the shapes in document order, `source.rs` the text of a shape that can be looked in, `replace.rs` the plan and the writes). The sibling Craft apps were searched
first: DeckCraft has `text.find` and `text.replace` (MIT or Apache-2.0), tied to its slides and paragraph runs, with no budget and a loop that is the pattern's length for each character of the text;
DesignCraft's is a regular-expression engine over its own compose crate; VectorCraft's `edit.findReplace` and WordCraft's `find_pattern.rs` work on their own text models (text objects, paragraphs
and styles). None runs on a ShapeSheet's text parts, rows and names, and none charges its work, so ours is written here and no code was copied (nothing is in `docs/provenance.md`); DeckCraft's whole-word rule (no letter, digit or
`_` beside the match) is the one adopted.

* **What matches.** `what` is literal text of 1 to 1,024 characters, with four special characters, the ones the Special list names: `^t` a tab, `^l` a manual line break (U+2028; a line feed
  ends a paragraph and is an ordinary character here), `^-` an optional hyphen (U+00AD), `^?` any one character, and `^^` is a caret (a caret before any other character is a caret). **The spelling of
  the four is ours** (the specification names the characters and not what is typed for them). A match is a run of characters that the pattern's equal one for one, so its length is the pattern's;
  matches never overlap. **Match case** compares the characters as stored, whatever caps formatting shows; without it a character equals its lower case when that is a single character.
  **Whole words** needs a match not to touch a word character, a letter, a digit or `_`, on either side, so `for` is in `for` and not in `forest`. Match character width and Match Kana type, which
  R19 lists for Japanese text, are **not here** (the window has no Regional option for Kana, which R19 says shows them).
* **Where it looks.** `in` is any of `text`, `shape_data`, `shape_name` and `user_cell` (the Shape text, Shape data, Shape name and User-defined cell), **`["text"]` by default** (R19 gives
  no defaults: ours). *Shape text* is what the shape's text block shows, a field's result in place (a date field is found by its date). *Shape name* is the shape's `Name`, or its `NameU` with no `Name`.
  *Shape data* and *user cell* are the `Value` cell of each row of the `Property` and `User` sections as the shape and its master together have it (the labels are not searched), so a row the
  master gives is found on each instance; a cell is a place when it holds text, and a number is found as its text. A match is told by its **place** (`text`, `shape_data`, `shape_name`, `user_cell`), its
  `row` for the last two, `start` and `end` in characters of the text the place shows, the shape's name and a `context` of twenty characters either side made safe to show. A shape that is a guide or is
  deleted from its master is not searched, and **a section of rows with more than 20,000 rows in a shape is not read** (its rows are charged, and the answer's `unread` counts such sections, so
  that nothing is dropped without being said).
* **Scope, order, Find Next.** `scope` is `selection` (the shapes in `ids` on `page`, and every member of a group among them), `page` (the page named, else the first that holds all of `ids`,
  else the first) or `all` (every page, in the document's order). The order is document order: pages in order, on a page a group before its members, and in a shape its name, its text, its shape data rows
  and its user rows. **`after: {page, id, place, row, offset}`** starts the list at the first match after the characters before `offset` in that place, and **`wrap`** (true by default) goes on from the
  start of the scope up to the place when the end is reached (`wrapped`); Find Next is `after` the end of the last match with a `limit` of 1. A place whose shape is not in the scope is no place: the
  list starts at the start. `limit` is 1 to 10,000 (100 by default) and `truncated` says there are more. `edit.find` is a query: it is not journaled and changes nothing.
* **Replace.** `edit.replace` replaces every match of the scope, or with **`at: {page, id, place, row, start, end}`** only that one, which must still be a match (the error says so in words
  and changes nothing). It is **one undo step** (`Replace All`, `Replace` for one) and none when nothing changed. A text is rewritten in **one pass** over its parts: the characters outside the matches
  stay in their runs, the new text joins the run of the match's first character, a match across runs takes the characters of the later runs out of them, and every marker and field stays.
  The ODF data of the text goes with it, as `shape.set_text`'s range does. A name's `Name` (and `NameU` when it was the same) takes the new name, which must be one a name may be
  (`diacraft_doc::check_text`). A cell is rewritten as it is kept: a quoted-string formula stays one with the new string, a constant stays a constant. **A match is left, and listed with why in
  `skipped` (the first 100, and `skipped_total` is exact), when** it touches what a field shows, when its cell is worked out by a formula, when a `GUARD` protects its cell, when the result is not allowed
  there (an empty name, a control character, a constant cell of text that would read as a number) or when the text would be more than 100,000 characters and longer than it was (a shorter text is always
  allowed; and the text of the whole replacement is within its budget). What reads a changed text or cell (`SHAPETEXT(TheText)`, a reference to a user cell) is worked out again for the page, once. `with` is checked as the text of a shape is (no control
  character but a tab and a line feed), and may be empty. The Replace dialog replaces **shape text** alone, as R20 lists no place; the command takes all four. **A shape on a locked layer is passed over**
  Every match of it is left with the reason that its shape is on a locked layer, and counted in `locked` as well as in `skipped_total`, whatever the scope (a page, the
  drawing, or a selection that holds a group, whose members go each by its own list); one match given by `at` on such a shape is refused in words, and `edit.find` still finds them. The Replace dialog's
  line says them apart (`Replaced 1 match. 2 matches on locked layers left.`).
* **What it costs.** Every search and every replacement is charged to one budget of **2^29 steps** (`MAX_FIND_STEPS`) before it is done, and refused in words past it (`the search is too large to
  finish`, with the way out): a step for each character passed or compared (a text that is plain and matches case goes by `str::find` and is charged a step for each byte), 8 for each shape passed, and
  400 for each row of shape data (counted over the shape, its master and the styles before any is merged), so a pattern and a text made to be slow (a thousand characters of `a` and a `b` against ten
  megabytes of `a`) cost what they are charged and no more. A listing is at most 10,000 matches and a Replace All at most 1,000,000 (every match counts, those that are left as well as those replaced); the contexts of a long text's matches are made in one pass over it. **A replacement writes at most 64 MiB of text in all** (`MAX_REWRITE_BYTES`): each text, name and cell is held to a text's longest, 100,000 characters, which is no cap on the drawing (76,000 shapes by a long `with` is 76,000 times that), and the process's memory budget is judged by `Session::edit_if` after the edit has made its copy, so the plan charges the bytes of every text it will make (an upper bound: the whole text a match is in, and `with` once for each match, and the plan's own) **before it makes it**, and is refused in words past the budget with nothing changed; `with` is at most 100,000 characters (a text's longest). `crates/engine/tests/it/find_cost.rs` runs 76,000 shapes by a 100,000-character `with`, as text and as shape data, and one text of 100,000 one-letter matches, each under `ulimit -v 3000000`;
  a walk goes no deeper than the model allows and visits at most a page's cap of shapes. `crates/engine/tests/it/find_cost.rs` counts it on a drawing of 76,000 shapes, a text of 10 MB, the worst pattern, 50,000
  matches in one text and a group 200 deep, and its ignored test times a search against a walk of the same drawing and against `str::matches`. **Measured** (development profile, a machine at a load of about 35, 2026-11-22): the text of 76,000 shapes in 13 ms (the same walk by hand 2.7 ms), the shape data of 76,000 shapes of three rows each in 0.55 s, a text of 10 MB in 1.1 ms for the plain case (`str::matches` 1.3 ms) and 40 ms folding case, and a refusal at the budget in 2.6 s; a row is charged 400 steps because it measured at about 2.5 microseconds against about 5 nanoseconds for a step.
* **The dialogs.** Home > Editing > Find has **Find...** and **Replace...** (the keys are Ctrl+F for Find, ours: the page names none for Find and gives Alt+H, FD, R for Replace, and Ctrl+H is
  Flip Horizontal, the specification's, so Replace has no key of its own). **Both are non-modal**: a floating window over the drawing area that does not shade the window or take its keys and
  pointer, with a close button, Escape in its box and `window.find {close: true}` to close it. Find what keeps the earlier searches (the button beside it), Special inserts the four characters, the scope is
  Selection (enabled when shapes are selected), Current page (the default) or All pages, the Find dialog has the four places and the options Match case and Find whole words only, a **Found in** line says
  where the match is (the text block, the shape name, the data row or the user-defined cell, with the shape and its page) and what a button did or why it could not, and **Find Next** runs `edit.find`
  from the match the dialog is at, then shows its page (`page.select`), selects its shape (`edit.select`) and moves the view to it when it is out of sight. **Replace** replaces the match the dialog is
  at and goes on to the next (with no match to be at it finds one first), **Replace All** is one `edit.replace`. Enter in Find what is Find Next. `window.find` (`mode`, `what`, `with`, `scope`, `in`,
  `match_case`, `whole_words`, `action`, `close`) opens it, sets its boxes and does what a button does, for a program; its state is `find` in the window state.
* **What is left.** Match character width and Match Kana type; replacing in names, shape data and user-defined cells is the command's and not the Replace dialog's; the data rows' labels and
  prompts are not searched; no regular expressions (the specification lists none); no Find in text being edited (a text box that is open is searched as the drawing holds it).

## Shape ids

* Our rule: a new shape or connector gets an `ID` above every `ID` the session has given on the page, above every `ID` in the page now,
  and above every `ID` in the file the drawing was read from or last saved to (`Session::id_floor`, a **high-water mark** per page). An `ID`
  that has been a shape's is therefore not given again in the session, though the shape was deleted or its drop undone: a formula that named it does not
  come to name another shape, and the writer does not meet a new shape where the file had a picture or a `Data1`, which it cannot write. A new
  drawing (`file.new`, `file.open`) starts the mark again. **A save keeps the mark too** (second): the baseline it replaces held the highest `ID` of the file the drawing was read
  from, and that goes into the mark first, so a shape of the file deleted before the save does not give its `ID` back to the next copy, drop or group (a `Sheet.<id>!` the delete left dangling would name it). The `draw` functions `drop_shape` and `add_connector` keep their earlier rule (the highest `ID`
  on the page plus 1); `drop_shape_above`, `add_connector_above` and `attach_connector_above` take the mark.
* The writer tells a shape by its `ID`, its `Type` and its master together, so a shape that has the `ID` of one taken out but is another thing is one
  removed and one added in the saved file, and not the old element edited.

## Saving and the file on the disk

* **A file changed on the disk is not replaced without `force`**. The session records the size and modified time of the file it read or
  wrote. `file.save`, and `file.save_as` onto the drawing's own file, compare them with the file as it is before they write. If they differ, something
  else has changed the file since: the command ends with `EngineError::ChangedOnDisk` (its words say so and name `force`, not the path), and
  writes nothing, and the drawing is as it was. `{"force": true}` saves anyway. A program gets the error; a window asks the person and, if the answer is to
  replace the file, runs the command again with `force`. A file that is no longer there is written again. Saving as another file is not compared: the
  check is for the drawing's own file.
* **A link is resolved when the drawing is opened**. A drawing opened through a link, or saved through a link to its own file, writes the
  file the link led to then, and not where the link points at save time. Both `file.save` and `file.save_as` judge the extension of the file that
  would be written (`.vsdx`, `.vsdm`, `.vssx`, `.vssm`, `.vstx` or `.vstm`, in any case): `file.save` of a file opened from a name with another
  extension is an error, and `file.save_as` names the kind of file.
* **The six types**. A file is a drawing, a stencil or a template, with macros allowed or not, by the content type of its document part and not by its extension; `file.save` keeps the type the package has, and `file.save_as` takes the type from the extension. **A template opens as a new drawing made from it** (`file.open` without `edit_template`): the document is the template's content, the session keeps **no file's bytes** (NP10: the model holds every part of the template, and the first save is written from it) and **no path**, so `file.save` is an error that says to use `file.save_as`, `file.status` says `has_file: false`, the drawing is unsaved from its first edit as one from `file.new` is, and the template on the disk is never written. The first file saved from it has times of its own (`created` and `modified`). `file.open {edit_template: true}` opens the template itself. A Save As between the types rewrites the document part's content type and keeps every other part; a drawing or template saved as a stencil keeps its pages and says so in `warnings`; a stencil saved as a drawing or a template gets an empty page part for each page that had none.
* **A row an instance holds of its own is saved with its type** (`crates/engine/tests/it/row_types.rs`). An instance holds a row of a `Geometry` section only where a cell differs from its master's: after `shape.size`, `shape.resize` or a size typed in a cell, the `X` or `Y` of the rows that name `Width` or `Height`, as `F="Inh"` with the new result as `V`. The row has its `IX` and **the `T` of the master's row** (`LineTo`, `MoveTo`, ...), as every `Geometry` row of the sample files has, in a VSDX file, in `.diacraft` saved as a VSDX type, and in the file a splice makes; a rectangle made 3 inches tall saves the rows `IX` 3 and 4 as `LineTo` with `Y` `Inh` and `V` 3. It is the same for a cell `sheet.set_cell` writes and one `shape.change` carries to the new master (`ReplaceCopyCells`). The rows a write makes in a `Geometry` section go in the order of their `IX`, which rise through it (the order of its rows is the order of its path, which a program that draws the rows as the file lists them draws): a resize in both ways saves rows 2, 3 and 4, not 3, 4 and 2. A `Connection` row is left as the master has it, since the files write none on a partial local row, and a row an earlier build saved with no `T` is kept as it is until a write reaches it (a save with no edit changes no byte of a file).
* **Macros are bytes**. The VBA project of a `.vsdm`, `.vssm` or `.vstm`, with its signature parts and their relationships, is kept as it is by every save, never run and never read. Saving a file that holds one as `.vsdx`, `.vssx` or `.vstx` ends with `EngineError::MacrosNotAllowed` (its words say what the two choices are) and writes nothing; `file.save_as {drop_macros: true}` leaves the project out of the new file, names its parts in `warnings`, and says how many in `macros_dropped`. The drawing in the session keeps its file, so the macro file is untouched. **The window asks**: the refusal of a Save As is the card "Leave the macros out?" in the engine's words, and Save without runs `file.save_as` again with `drop_macros`; a program that asks the same save gets the error and no card, as a command never asks. `file.save` keeps the type and is never refused for macros, and no command refuses a save for an embedded object, so there is no card for objects.
* **The root style of a VSDX file DiaCraft writes states what the renderer assumes** (ours; `crates/doc/src/root_text.rs`). The renderer reads a paragraph with no `HorzAlign` anywhere on its way as centred, a line with no `SpLine` as one and two tenths of a line, a tab with no `DefaultTabStop` as every half inch, and so on, and a reader of a file that finds no cell takes the default of the cell's kind, 0. The first check of the files DiaCraft wrote, in the reference application, found text DiaCraft centres left-aligned there, because the root style (style 0, `No Style`) held no `Paragraph` section (reported in words and not yet in the specifications: unverified). **A new drawing's root holds a `Paragraph` row 0** (12 of the 13 cells, each with the value the renderer assumes: `HorzAlign` 1, `SpLine` -1.2, `BulletFontSize` -1, the rest 0 or empty), **the nine cells of the text block** (`DefaultTabStop` 0.5 and `TextBkgnd`, `TextBkgndTrans` and `TextDirection` 0, beside the margins and `VerticalAlign` it already held) **and the cells of the first run's `Character` row 0** beyond its size and colour (`FontScale` 1, `ComplexScriptSize` -1 and the cells that are 0), and no face and no language (the font database's default and the document's own are no assumed value). `TextPosAfterBullet` and `ColorTrans` are left out: a reader takes a missing cell as 0, which is what is assumed, and an OpenDocument style has no attribute for either, while the rows the engine makes for a formatted run or paragraph hold every cell the row resolves to, the root's row 0 among them. **The `.odg` writer takes a `ComplexScriptSize` of -1 as no attribute** (it has none, and the root states it), and refuses another value as before. A drawing read from an `.odg` has the same root (the reader makes it from a new drawing's). `crates/render/tests/it/root_text.rs` holds the cells to the values the renderer assumes and says that stating them draws no pixel differently. **The model writer adds to a root that lacks them the cells whose absence a reader reads as another value than the assumed one, and only those** (`HorzAlign`, `SpLine`, `BulletFontSize`, `FontScale`, `ComplexScriptSize`, `DefaultTabStop`, and `Size` and `VerticalAlign` where missing), for a drawing that came from no VSDX file (a `.diacraft` file of an earlier build, an `.odg`): a Save As of one to a VSDX type. A cell the root holds, whatever it holds, is never changed, a section it deletes is not brought back, and the model the save hands back keeps the root the caller had (as it keeps the caller's font table), so that the next save into the file takes nothing out and the save's check finds nothing to say (`crates/vsdx/src/write/root.rs`, `crates/engine/tests/it/root_style_files.rs`). **A drawing that was read from a VSDX file keeps the root it has** in every save, the splice leaving the part's bytes as they are and the model writer writing the model's own root: what the file's root lacked, the file lacked. **One root is not a file's: DiaCraft's own earlier one** (`is_an_earlier_root`: the style `No Style` with no `Paragraph` section and a `Character` row 0 of a size and a colour alone, which every root of the census, with its whole `Paragraph` section, rules out for a file of another program). A drawing that holds it is DiaCraft's own whatever package data it holds, and the model writer states its cells as for a drawing that came from no file: a `.diacraft` file of an earlier build made from a template (which holds the package data of DiaCraft's own skeleton) and a VSDX file an earlier build wrote, opened and saved as a new file. A file an earlier build wrote, saved into itself, keeps the root it was written with (it still reads left-aligned in the reference application where DiaCraft centres, until it is saved as a new file).
* **A text row past the first is whole** (ours; `crates/doc/src/root_text.rs` `row_cells`, `complete_row_cells`, `complete_row_with`; `crates/engine/src/across/text_rows.rs`). A style holds row 0 alone, so a reader of a file takes a cell that a `Character` or `Paragraph` row of `IX` 1 or more lacks from the master's row of that `IX` and from nowhere else, and reads the default of the cell's kind, 0, where there is none; the renderer here draws such a cell with the value it assumes (the table). The reference application, opening files DiaCraft wrote, drew the title line of every org chart position as letters piled on one another (the master's `Character` row `IX` 1 held `Size` and `Style` alone, so its `FontScale` read 0 and its `Font` 0), and the runs of a language sample and of drawings converted from an `.odg` the same (reported in words and not yet in the specifications: unverified). Every row past the first in the files of the census holds all its cells, and asks a writer that adds a run to write the whole row. **A row DiaCraft makes past the first holds every cell the table states in its section** (12 in `Character`: `Size`, `Color`, `Style`, `Case`, `Pos`, `FontScale`, `Letterspace`, `DblUnderline`, `Overline`, `Strikethru`, `DoubleStrikethrough`, `ComplexScriptSize`; 12 in `Paragraph`: `Bullet`, `BulletFont`, `BulletFontSize`, `BulletStr`, `Flags`, `HorzAlign`, `IndFirst`, `IndLeft`, `IndRight`, `SpAfter`, `SpBefore`, `SpLine`), each it does not say with the value the renderer assumes, so a reader of the file and the renderer read one value and nothing is drawn differently here: the rows of the built-in masters past the first (the title of an org chart position, the second and third lines of the C4 masters and of the network labels) and the rows `text.format` writes whole. The table leaves out the face and the language (this program assumes none: a `Font` of 0 names no face), `ColorTrans` and `TextPosAfterBullet` (a reader takes them as 0, which is what is assumed). **A Save As to a VSDX type** (the model writer) **gives the copy it writes** each such cell a row past the first lacks and takes from nowhere else (a master's row of its `IX` or a style that holds it gives it), **for a drawing whose rows are DiaCraft's to state** (`root_text::rows_are_ours_to_state`, the test the root of a model written from nothing is given by too): one that came from no VSDX package (a new drawing, an `.odg`, a `.diacraft` file that holds no VSDX package: the rows an `.odg` reader makes, a run's row holding the face, the size and the weight its style says), or whose root is the one an earlier build made (`is_an_earlier_root`: the rows of that build, which no file of another program has a root like). **A drawing that came from a VSDX package with any other root holds the file's own rows, and every route writes them as they were read** (a Save As, a save through `.diacraft` and a save into the file alike): whatever a row of that file lacks, the program that wrote it left out, and a reader of the file takes it from the master's row of its `IX` as that program meant it. **The value a cell is given is what the drawing's own reading of the row says**: the table's, which is what the renderer assumes, and for the rows of an `.odg` what the format says: **a paragraph that states no alignment is left-aligned** (`HorzAlign` 0, `root_text::odf_row_value`), as the `.odg` says of it and as a program that reads a row with no `HorzAlign` takes it, and not the root's centre. **The held styles of an `.odg` stand beside the rows given cells** (`across::text_rows`, `restamp`): the automatic style each paragraph and run named is stamped again by the row it now stands on, and a group of cells the row was given which the style never stated holds a value of no attribute, so that the `.odg` written back from the VSDX file says what the source said (the faces, the sizes, the names of its styles, and no alignment, line height, colour or scale that it never stated). The drawing becomes what the file reads as; the drawing the person has is not changed by the save. **A row so completed is a row the `.odg` writer writes as the row it was** (the cells given to a bulleted paragraph, `BulletFontSize` -1 among them, left the paragraph with no style at all when the writer took the -1 for a size it could not write, so the space above and below and the justification of a list's paragraphs were lost on the way back from VSDX). Row 0 leans on the styles and is left as it is, as is a deleted row. **A save into a file leaves the rows a file holds as they are**: a file an older build wrote keeps its rows until it is saved as a new file, and a save with no edit is the same bytes.
* **A language cell of a VSDX file DiaCraft writes is the tag alone** (ours; `crates/vsdx/src/plain_languages.rs`). The sample files hold a language as a plain tag, `<Cell N="LangID" V="fr-FR"/>`, with no `F` and no `U`: all 75,418 `Character` cells of the samples and every `Shape Data` cell that holds a value, and none holds a number. A cell that holds a **string formula** (`"fr-FR"` typed in the formula bar: `F="&quot;fr-FR&quot;"`, `U="STR"`) gave the application that opens the file a text where the cell is a language, which it read as `#VALUE!` and replaced by a language of its own (observed there, in words and not yet in the specifications: unverified: `Char.LangID`, `Char.LangID[2]` and `Char.LangID[4]` read 8192 for `"en-US"`, `"fr-FR"` and `"tr-TR"`). **Every VSDX writer (a drawing never saved, the model writer, so a Save As from a `.diacraft` file or an `.odg`, and a save into a file) writes such a cell as the tag alone**, with the formula and the unit `STR` left out: the cells `LangID` and `DocLangID` under a sheet and the `LangID` of a `Character` or `Property` row. A tag needs no number (the files write `x-none` and `en-FI`, which no table of numbers lists), so none is written, and the drawing keeps the tag the person typed: DiaCraft reads it back from the file as the language of the run. **What is left as it is:** a formula that is no string (it reads another cell, it calls a function) is the person's and is written with its unit; a cell the file already holds (a save with no edit writes what it read, and an edit of another cell does not touch it, so an `V U F` cell an earlier build wrote stays until the cell is written again); a number a file holds (`1036`), which is read as the language its number pairs with (`diacraft_doc::lang`) and kept as written; an `Annotation` row's `LangID`, a number of the legacy files. The session's cell is not changed by a save: the formula the person typed stays in it, and `.diacraft` holds it whole; an `.odg` says the language in `fo:language` and `fo:country` as before. The engine hands the model writer the drawing with the cells so written, so that the check after the save finds nothing lost. Tests: `crates/vsdx/tests/it/language_cells.rs` and `crates/engine/tests/it/vsdx_language_cells.rs`.
* **The text of a `User` or `Field` row says `STR` in the VSDX files DiaCraft writes, whatever made the cell** (ours, beside; `crates/vsdx/src/string_units.rs`, `crates/doc/src/string_unit.rs`, `crates/engine/src/across/onto.rs`). Gave the unit to the cells a build makes. The release gate of 0.2.4 opened the files the command line wrote of the demo drawings in the reference application and found the cells that pass through a writer as the drawing holds them (reported in words and not yet in the specifications: unverified): the `Value` of the `User` rows of containers and swimlanes in the `.diacraft` files of 0.2.3 (`msvStructureType` with `V="Container"` and its string formula, `DiaCraftContainerStyle` and `DiaCraftSwimlane` with `V="frame"` or `V="phase"`: 25 cells in one drawing, 2 in each of two others), and the cached text of the `Field` rows of a VSDX file of 0.2.3 (`<Cell N="Value" V="web-01" F="Inh"/>`), which a save into the file kept as the file had it. The application said "an element in this file contains data that is invalid or inappropriate for the expected type of data" once for each: no `Type` cell in such a row says the value is a string, so the unit alone does. **What is given the unit** is the `Value` of a `User` or `Field` row that reads as a text (a number, an empty value, a colour, `Themed` and a cell that says a unit already are left as they are), **and no other cell**: a `Property` row's `Value` is typed by its `Type` (104,655 string rows of the sample files say no unit), and the cells of a text kind carry none in the files of the program that opens them (`Prop.Format`, `User.Prompt`, `Hyperlink.SubAddress`), so a file of another program that goes through `.diacraft` and back is not changed there, and a label or a prompt an earlier build wrote with no unit stays as it was. **A `Field` row whose own `Type` says its value is no string** (a date, a number, a duration, a currency or a list item: any `Type` but 0) **is typed by it, as a `Property` row is, and is left as it is**: a date field caches a date, the files hold `U` `DATE` and a date as text in it (gives it that where the text or the drawing's times say the date), and a text no date is read from, in a drawing that holds no time, stays as it was read and is no string. **Where:** a drawing never saved and the model writer (a Save As from a `.diacraft` file or an `.odg`) give it in the copy the writer is handed (`across::onto`, `Given::stringed`, counted for the save's adoption), **for a drawing whose units are DiaCraft's to state** (`diacraft_doc::units_are_ours_to_state`: it came from no VSDX package, or from one whose extended properties name DiaCraft, as the template-made drawings and the files of 0.2.3 do), and the drawing becomes the model the file reads as, so the next save into the file holds the units. **A drawing that came from the package of another program is that program's, and is written as it was read on this route as on the others** (the recheck of 0.2.4 found a file whose extended properties name another program, with a `User` row whose text says no unit, come out of the trip through `.diacraft` with `U="STR"`, a difference of the content in a file that was never ours: the content check of the trip counted one and its model check was false; one public file of the corpus was changed so); a package whose properties name no program is another program's. **A save into a file gives it only in a file DiaCraft wrote**, judged by the file's own `docProps/app.xml` (`Application`: a file an earlier build wrote, or one a save of ours has written), whether or not the drawing was edited, so a Save of such a file with no edit writes its pages and masters with the units; **a file another program wrote is written as it was read**, and one that DiaCraft saved after an edit names DiaCraft from then on. The drawing in the session is not changed by a save into a file. Tests: `crates/vsdx/tests/it/string_units.rs`, `crates/engine/tests/it/vsdx_string_units.rs`, `crates/engine/tests/it/vsdx_str_foreign.rs` and the unit tests of `crates/doc/src/string_unit.rs`.

## `.diacraft` files

`file.open` reads DiaCraft's own format, and `file.save` and `file.save_as` write it, so the window, the CLI and the MCP server reach it through those commands. The format is `docs/diacraft-format.md`, the package
is the `native` crate's (`diacraft_native`: `read`, `write`, `sniff`), and the engine's part is `crates/engine/src/nativefile`: what it keeps of the file, the memory a read and a save may use, the identifier ledger and the
content stamp. The window offers the format: its Save dialog lists the types the engine writes for the drawing, and its Open dialog lists DiaCraft drawings first. Which types a Save As writes is the engine's to say, and a frontend asks it with `Session::save_as_allows(extension)` (the save-path table asked without saving, so it answers what `file.save_as` would accept for a name of that type, and nothing for a `.fodg`, which no drawing is saved as) instead of keeping a table of its own; it is not a command, since it opens no dialog and changes nothing.

* The bytes decide, in this order. `file.open {path}` asks `diacraft_native::sniff` first (the first entry of the package is a stored `mimetype` that names a type of the format), then
  `diacraft_odg::sniff`, then the VSDX reader, **and neither of the others can claim a `.diacraft` file**. The kind the file says it is (a drawing, a stencil or a template) decides, and the extension only gets a warning: a
  `.diacraft` file called `a.vsdx` opens, and `file.warnings` says that it is called by another type's name. The answer is the document as `document.inspect` gives it, and `file: {variant: "diacraft" |
  "diacraft-stencil" | "diacraft-template", kind, format: "1.1", new_from_template, bytes, warnings: [..first 20..], warning_count, skipped_count, diacraft: {state: "absent"}}` (`format` is the version the file says;
  `skipped_count` is how many parts of a role this build does not know were kept as bytes). A file of a later major version is refused in words ("made by a newer DiaCraft (format 2.0)"); a damaged file or one past a
  limit is refused in words with the class and no path or text of the file; **damage confined to pictures, themes and kept parts does not refuse the file**: it opens and `warnings` counts what was lost. A file that cannot
  be opened leaves the open drawing as it was. A theme's colours and fonts are not in the file: they are read from its bytes at the open, as an `.odg`'s are (`odgfile::read_themes`).
* The memory is the process's. A read is given what is left of the process's budget beside `held`, everything the process holds (the open drawing and its file, the open
  stencils, every other session), as a reservation (below), and never more than `nativefile::open::READ_BUDGET`, the smaller of the process's budget (the VSDX reader's `diacraft_vsdx::MAX_MEMORY`, which every read reserves from) and the package's own `diacraft_native::MAX_MEMORY` (the package's is the larger, so the process's is the one a read is held to). A save is given `Limits::for_save(held)` (the figure the process holds in all, the model once, less the codec's own room for the tree of the child in hand, `save_child_items`, the tables of its check and the bytes of a part, out of the package's `diacraft_native::MAX_MEMORY`; the tree of a part is held to the items that fit). **The model is counted once**: the drawing's file holds the model the open read
  and its bytes, the session holds what it has grown by, and a save keeps no second model (the baseline shares what the drawing holds). A refusal for memory beside what is held says so in words that give the numbers
  (`not enough memory beside what is open`, `OpenProblem::OutOfMemory`, with the budget the read is held to named, `READ_BUDGET`: `HeldMemory::words_of`; a save's refusal names the package's own figure, which its room is taken from), and a file too large for the whole budget is told as it is told alone; **a `.diacraft` read holds the same reservation of what is left of the budget as a VSDX read does** (`file.open`, a template path and `stencil.open` take it, the first two waiting for a read that is running and a stencil taking a slice and waiting for none; the read is held to what was reserved, and never to more than `READ_BUDGET`), and its refusal says that a file is being read when one is; **the room is taken before the file is loaded**: the size of the file is looked at first (a path that names nothing, a folder or a pipe is refused at once, without opening it and without waiting for a read that is running), the reservation is taken, a file larger than the room it holds is refused from its size, in words (`out_of_memory` beside what is held, `too_big` when it is more than the whole budget alone) and not a byte of it is read, and the file is then loaded held to that room, so two large opens at the same moment no longer load two files beside a budget one of them holds; the children of `tests/it/native_memory.rs` (a file of 340 MB open alone,
  the same beside a hold of 1.9 GB and a template of 340 MB started from beside it (`file.new` of a `.diacraft-template` path), a save beside 2.3 GB, two sessions, and a drawing of 30,000 shapes read from a VSDX file, edited everywhere and saved, with a file of 150 MB read beside it; and `read_room.rs`: a file of 900 MB beside a read that holds the budget is never loaded by any of the four ways a file is read, and two opens of 900 MB at the same moment load one file at a time) run under `ulimit -v 3000000` and **assert their outcome**: a file beside a hold that leaves it no room is refused in words that say it is for memory (`out_of_memory`, `not enough memory beside what is open`) and opens once the hold is given back, and the others open; none is an abort.
* Two save paths, decided by the drawing's working file; the design's 4.1. `OpenFile::format()` is `diacraft`, `vsdx` or `odg` (`None` for a new drawing and one made from a template), and
  `file.save_as` **switches the working file** to the file it writes (Calls 15 and 16: `file.save` then writes it, in its own format, silently). `save_path` is a pure function of the working file and what the name says:
  a `.diacraft` drawing is saved as `.diacraft` (any of the three kinds) or as a VSDX type, **from the model alone** (the VSDX model writer, with no file to splice into, and the
  thumbnail, `Application` and `modified` kept when the content stamp says the drawing is the one its VSDX file held, and written as an edited save writes them when it is not or when there is no
  stamp), a VSDX drawing as a VSDX type by the splice writer as before or as `.diacraft`, an `.odg` as an `.odg` by the splice writer as before or as `.diacraft` (the model holds what the `.odg` holds, so the file loses none of it, and the package data and the named data of the file as it is now go with the drawing, `with_file_package_data`), and a new drawing as
  `.diacraft` or, from the model alone, a VSDX type. **A `.diacraft` drawing and a new one are saved as an `.odg` (a drawing) or an `.otg` (a template) from the model alone** (which lifted
  Call 18's refusal of them: `diacraft_odg::write_with(doc, None, ..)`, the model writer, makes the package, the kind of document the name says always asked for): the engine's own shapes are handed over flattened to what a shape of an
  `.odg` is, as a save into a file hands over its new ones (a shape that holds ODF data is in the file's form already and is left as it is), the copies taking at most a third of what a save may hold; a drawing started from a built-in
  template holds the VSDX package data of DiaCraft's own skeleton, which is no person's and which no `.odg` says, and is given to the writer without it (`odgfile/skeleton.rs`: only data that is exactly a built-in template's); **the thumbnail
  and the generator follow the content stamp** and never the dirty flag: while the drawing is the content its `.odg` held (a visit through `.diacraft`) the writer writes them as the model holds them and no picture is
  rendered, and otherwise, and for a drawing that was never read from a file, the generator is DiaCraft's and the first page is rendered for the thumbnail (at most 256 pixels). The file written becomes the drawing's own (an `.odg` with the
  index the writer gave), so a later `file.save` splices into it and an unchanged drawing is no edit; the answer is the `.odg` save's, `{bytes, variant: "odg" | "otg", kind: "drawing" | "template", form: "package", edited, macros_dropped: 0,
  dirty: false, warnings, warning_count, notes, carried, checked}` (`carried`; `checked`: the check after a save). **Refused in words, before anything is made or by the writer, and with nothing written:** a **stencil as an `.odg` or an `.otg`** (OpenDocument has no stencil format), and what the `.odg` cannot say that is a drawing's own, a background page (a master page that holds shapes) added to the drawing
  (the words say what is missing, that nothing was written and that a `.diacraft` file or a VSDX type holds the drawing; a VSDX file's package data and the drawing window's settings ride inside the file), and a
  **`.fodg`, which no Save As writes** (the words point to the `.odg` package). `file.save` of a `.diacraft` file writes a `.diacraft` file of the kind it has whatever the file is called, and **never turns a file into another format by its name**: whatever the table says, a name of another format than the file's (a VSDX package called `a.odg`, `a.otg` or `a.diacraft`, an `.odg` called `a.diacraft` or `a.vsdx`) is refused with the words of the file's own format (the name must end in its type, `file.save_as` is the way), so the guard holds once the writers across the formats are there. A name that is no type is refused listing the types. The link, folder,
  changed-on-disk (`ChangedOnDisk`, `force`) and atomic-replacement rules of the other types hold, and every save is made whole in memory and goes through `craft-atomic`.
  The answer is `{bytes, variant, kind, format, macros_dropped: 0, dirty: false, copied, warnings, warning_count, carried, checked}` (`carried`, empty for a `.diacraft` file; `checked`: the check after a save, made when the drawing came from a file of another format or a template file of one): `variant` is the extension written (`diacraft`, `diacraft-stencil` or `diacraft-template`) and
  `copied` how many entries of the package were copied as they were from the file the drawing was read from or last saved as. **A save that changed nothing writes the file it read**, and one that changed a page rewrites that
  page's part and the picture of the first page and copies the rest (**a page of more than 5,000 shapes has no picture, and a stencil has none**: a picture of 256 pixels of thousands of shapes is a blur, and the render of 20,000 shapes was 83 ms of their save; a package that holds none to copy gets one made); the same drawing gives the same bytes after a reopen (`native_reopen.rs`, with the clock pinned).
* Saves across the VSDX and OpenDocument formats; the design's sections 5.1, 5.6 and 6. **`file.save_as` writes the crossings**: a drawing opened from a VSDX file as an `.odg` or an `.otg` (`SavePath::OdgModel`), and a drawing opened from an `.odg` as one of the six VSDX types (`SavePath::VsdxModel`), each **by the model writer of the target**, with no file to splice into; `file.save` never changes a file's format by its name. **What the target cannot say rides in its carrier**, and **the result says what in `carried`: `{classes: [..], document_level, macros, objects, signatures_stale}`**, a structured field and never a warning, which every save answers (empty for a save into a file and for a save as `.diacraft`). The classes are plain words: "line ends", "gradients", "hatches", "glue directions", "layer settings", "style names", "document properties", "settings", "macro project", "embedded objects", "window settings" and "unknown parts", and "dash patterns", "fill images", "page layouts", "package details", "digital signatures", "shape data", "page data", "style data" and "document data" for what the design's list does not name; where the writer carried something that no finer class names, the class is "document data", so nothing is carried unnamed. The note's words are the design's 5.6, exactly, in `diacraft_engine::across::words(target, &carried)` (the window and any program word the field with it). **Options, never requirements:** `drop_macros` leaves the macro project out where the type cannot hold it or the file is of the other format (a macro project of either language goes into a VSDX file of a macro-enabled type only, Call 17: a save to `.vsdx`, `.vssx` or `.vstx` without `drop_macros` is `MacrosNotAllowed`, in words that name the macro-enabled types), and `drop_objects` leaves the embedded objects of the other format out of the file: **what is left of a shape that showed one is its picture** (the spec's question Q3, answered as the design says: its shape shows its replacement picture in both cases), and the drawing keeps them, so a `.diacraft` saved afterwards holds them. **The drawing after a save across to VSDX** adopts the model the file reads as (`Session::adopt_saved`, no undo step), when that holds everything it did (every item of carried data came back, and the options left nothing out): the file is the drawing's own, and a second Save As across in the same session is no longer refused ("a change to the picture of a shape"). **A picture an `.odg` held gets the cells of its box** when it is saved as VSDX (`ImgOffsetX`, `ImgOffsetY`, `ImgWidth` as `Width*1` and `ImgHeight` as `Height*1`: the picture fills the shape), because a `Foreign` shape is drawn by other programs only with them. **The style sheets of a VSDX drawing are carried by the `.odg` model writer** (the concern 1): the root's cells and names, and the links, names and cells of the others, ride in the document file as entries of `style` (`root`, `line-style`, `fill-style`, `text-style`), and what the root's element held rides in an item; a style sheet whose ID is not its place among the style sheets (a VSDX file's numbering has gaps) is carried too (the `id` of its entry), and two style sheets of one ID are refused in words. **What the engine still says it loses**: the links of a VSDX drawing's shapes to its style sheets, which the flattened shape does not carry (the `.odg` holds each shape's own values), in a warning in words; and the two `KINDS` rows (the text formatting a style sheet gives, the link to the Theme style), as before. The warnings no longer carry the note: `SaveNote::Carried` and the signature note are the field's. The VSDX writer says what it carried (`Written::carried`: items, parts, a macro project, objects), and the page's own item no longer goes stale after the trip (its stamp leaves out the `PageContents` and `Rel` entries the writer always makes). A VSDX drawing that holds masters is saved as an `.odg` with each instance written as the shape it shows: the flattened copy holds the text a shape shows through its master (a shape with no `Text` of its own shows its master's), the rows of `Character`, `Paragraph`, `Tabs` and `Field` that text names (the master's, with the shape's own cells laid over them), the cells that place the text block when it is not the whole shape, and the picture of a `Foreign` instance, so another program sees ordinary shapes; the link to the master stays and the master rides in DiaCraft's document file. A core property that an application writes as an empty element (a VSDX file's empty `dc:subject`, `cp:keywords` and the like) no longer refuses the save: the document item carries it. Still refused in words: a style sheet with no `Name`, a background page, a picture the `.odg` reader does not draw. **The save after a Save As, with no edit, is no edit**: a drawing saved as an `.odg` from the model (from a VSDX file, a built-in template or a new drawing) is the drawing's own file, and a `file.save` with no edit between gives the file's own bytes (`edited: false`). The splice is given what the model writer was: the drawing without DiaCraft's own skeleton when the first save left it out, and without what the Save As was asked to leave out (`drop_objects` gives each object's picture, `drop_macros` keeps the macro project out of DiaCraft's document file), on every save into the file; the version of the program a VSDX file names (`AppVersion`) is no field of an `.odg` and is not compared; and the model writer's index holds the drawing's own pages as the pages saved. Tests: `crates/engine/tests/it/odg_resave.rs`, `crates/odg/tests/it/model_resave.rs`. **What a Save As leaves out stays out of every save into the file it wrote, in every pair of formats** ("a Save As option holds for every later save into the file it wrote"). The drawing keeps what was left out (a `.diacraft` saved after it holds the object and the macro project, also after a Save As to an `.odg`, whose package data put on the drawing no longer takes the parts the file lacks). A VSDX file written from the model with `drop_objects` or `drop_macros` (from an `.odg`, a `.diacraft` drawing or a new one) records what it was asked to leave out (`OpenFile::asked`, the union of the Save As that wrote it and every later one into it), and the drawing becomes what the file reads as with what was left out put back on it (`across/dropped.rs`: the shapes that showed an object of an `.odg` and the macro and object parts), when every item the file carries came back and the check after the save found no difference. Each save into the file gives the writer the drawing as the Save As gave it (the objects as their pictures, `across::onto::given`; the macro parts out of a type that holds none) and compares it with a baseline made the same way, not with what the file reads as: a save with no edit is no edit with the same bytes, a move of a shape (the one that showed an object too) is written, and neither the objects nor the macro project come back into the file. A VSDX type that cannot hold macros gets `drop_macros` at each save into it, and a macro-enabled type holds the project whatever was asked, as it did. A Save As from an `.odg` to another `.odg` takes the two options: when the drawing carries a macro project or objects of another format (a VBA project or VSDX objects riding in DiaCraft's folder) the file is written from the model, as a Save As of a VSDX file to an `.odg` is, which leaves them out (a drawing the `.odg` model writer refuses, one that holds the style sheets of a VSDX file, is refused in words, nothing written); with nothing of the other format to leave out it is a splice, as before. **Closed:** an `.odg` that natively holds a VSDX file's object (written as an object frame) saved again with no edit is no edit, and an edit writes the object once: the file records that the model writer took the VSDX embedding out of what rides (`LeftOut::carried_objects`), and each save into it is given the drawing without it (`diacraft_odg::without_carried_objects`). A `.diacraft` drawing that holds an `.odg`'s frames, saved as a VSDX type with nothing left out, becomes what the file reads as, as a drawing read from an `.odg` does (`across::adopts_by_working_file`: the writer was given pictures an `.odg` held; a drawing that holds none and a VSDX drawing never do), so its next Save is no edit and an edit is written. A VSDX file whose page sheet has a `User` section before its `Layer` section, saved as `.odg`, is no edit on the next Save: the sections of a sheet are compared by name. **Closed:** an object of an `.odg` (or of a `.diacraft` drawing) saved as a VSDX type is held once by every save into the file, an edit too: the writer says which parts it wrote as embeddings (`diacraft_vsdx::Written::natively`), the file remembers them (`OpenFile::natively`), and each save into it gives the writer the drawing and its baseline without them (`across::natively::without_parts`), so the object's file does not ride in DiaCraft's part beside the embedding; the drawing keeps it. A drawing made from an `.otg` template that holds `.odg` frames has no working file, and the same gate takes it (the writer was given pictures an `.odg` held), so its next Save after a Save As to a VSDX type is no edit and an edit is written; a blank drawing's saves are unchanged. **Closed by ** (random chains of two to six saves in one session, from every kind of drawing, through every type a Save As writes, with and without its options and with edits between: `crates/engine/tests/it/resave_sweep.rs`): a picture the drawing holds by its bytes (inserted from a file, or read from an earlier file) is the picture its VSDX file names by a row of its own, so the Save after a Save As to a VSDX type is no edit and a move of the picture is written, and an embedded object is the same by its relationship and its picture's bytes; a picture inserted into a drawing whose file is a VSDX type is written by the Save, as a new page's picture is (a row of the page part to a part that holds it), on a blank page too, where it was saved with no `Rel` and lost; a Save with no edit into a file the session wrote keeps the program's name a model writer kept (the unedited visit); a Save As to `.diacraft`, or to another `.odg` from the model, of a drawing that stands on the `.odg` it was read from makes the drawing the model written, and a drawing whose `.odg` the session wrote from its own model takes no package data from it; the baseline of a VSDX save holds the parts the file holds (not a macro project it left out, the embedding and not the object's file it was made from), so a Save As from a `.vssx` to a `.vssm` writes the drawing's macro project and a drawing that becomes its file's model holds its objects' embeddings; a Save As that left something out puts back only what the drawing it was given held; a patch that leaves a part's bytes as they were is no edit; the user-defined fields of an `.odg` in a VSDX file are no change of its custom properties (the vector); and the entries of DiaCraft's folder in an `.odg` are what its document file names. Tests: `crates/engine/tests/it/resave_sweep.rs` (the chains, and one test for each class), `crates/vsdx/tests/it/new_pictures.rs`, `crates/engine/tests/it/drop_resave.rs` (every pair of formats, with a Save As that leaves nothing out; the object held once in every VSDX type after two edits, and by a second file written from the first; a template drawing's saves; a blank drawing's saves), `crates/engine/src/across/dropped.rs`, `crates/engine/src/across/natively.rs`, `crates/odg/tests/it/model_ole.rs`, `crates/vsdx/tests/it/objects.rs`.
* `file.check_compatibility`; plan 0.3 PL8; File › Info, label "Check Compatibility", no shortcut. **What a save would carry and lose, made in memory and not written.** A save is two halves (`cmd/file.rs`, `Made`): **making** the file (the target judged, the drawing given to the writer, the file written in memory and read back, the check and `carried` made of what was read back), which reads the session and changes nothing in it, and **committing** it (the write through `craft-atomic`, then the session told the drawing is saved: the working file, the dirty flag, the adoption of the model the file reads as, the identifier ledger and the baselines). `file.save` and `file.save_as` are both halves, and this command is the first. Its params are `file.save_as`'s, `{path, drop_macros, drop_objects, force}`, and `path` may be left out to mean the drawing's own file as `file.save` saves it (then `drop_macros` and `drop_objects`, which a Save has no choice of, are `BadParams`). → `{writer, format, variant, carried, checked, bytes}`: `writer` is `diacraft`, `vsdx_model`, `vsdx_splice`, `odg_model` or `odg_splice`; `format` is `diacraft`, `vsdx` or `odg`; `variant` is the extension of the type that would be written; `carried`, `checked` and `bytes` are the fields the save's result holds, `checked` being `null` where the save is not checked (a splice into the drawing's own format, a `.diacraft` written from a `.diacraft` drawing or a new one) and `carried` empty for a splice. **It fails as the save would**: the same kind of error in the same words, naming this command (a macro project the type cannot hold, `MacrosNotAllowed`; a file changed on the disk, `ChangedOnDisk`, past which `force` goes; a link; a `.fodg`; a stencil to `.odg`; a name that is no type; a drawing with no file; the save's memory gate; any refusal of a writer). **It is a query**: no undo step and no journal entry, and `file.status`, the dirty flag, the history, the working file, the identifier ledger and every baseline are as they were, and no file is made or replaced. (Only a cache that the next save fills the same way may be filled: the pending content stamp, worked out when a model writer asks whether the drawing is as it was read.) **Its cost is the save's less the disk**: the writer and the reader each run once, which a test counts (`diacraft_engine::file::saves_made` and the comparisons of the check), so that a window that asks before a Save As through a model writer costs that save twice. A save that follows a dry run writes the same bytes and answers the same: a property over the chains, each run in twin sessions (`crates/engine/tests/it/save_check_before.rs`). Programs are never asked: `file.save_as` is unchanged. The window's card with Continue and Cancel is.
* A new drawing is a `.diacraft` drawing; NP10. **A new drawing keeps its model and no file's bytes**, whether `file.new` made it blank or from a built-in template, or `file.new {template: path}` or `file.open` made it from a template file (`.diacraft-template`, `.vstx` or `.vstm`): `Session::source()` is `None`, the session holds the model alone, and the package a template was read from is let go before the drawing is made. The model it starts with is exactly what it was (`native_default::a_new_drawings_model_is_exactly_as_before` pins the content stamp of the blank drawing and of each built-in template, with the property times cleared, and page 1's `ID` is 1), and it holds every part its template's package held, as bytes. The drawing has no file: `file.save` says to use `file.save_as`, `file.status` is `{has_file: false, format: null, variant: null, kind: null}`, and **its first save is `.diacraft`** (the window sets its default extension itself): a Save As to a `.diacraft` name writes the package from the model and copies nothing. **A Save As to a VSDX type writes the file from the model** (`SavePath::VsdxModel`, the VSDX model writer with no file to splice into, as for a `.diacraft` drawing): its `created` and `modified` are the save's (`WriteOptions::new_copy`), the thumbnail is left out and `Application` is DiaCraft (there is no content stamp to say the drawing is as a file held it), and the lists of page and master names in `docProps/app.xml` are made from the model where the template's cannot be told (the one group a built-in template has names its one page: a drawing that has gained pages and masters would otherwise get the lists left as they were, and a warning). A blank drawing, which holds nothing of a package, is written from the writer's skeleton as before. **A drawing opened from a `.vsdx` keeps being saved as a `.vsdx` by the splice writer, silently** (Call 16): no note names `.diacraft`, and a Save As to another VSDX type splices into the file's own parts. A drawing opened from an `.odg` is saved as `.diacraft`. A `.diacraft` drawing or a new one is saved as an `.odg`. A VSDX drawing is saved as an `.odg` and an `.odg` as a VSDX type which lifted the last two refusals that named `.diacraft` as the way out. Tests: `crates/engine/tests/it/native_default.rs`, and `model_writer.rs` of the VSDX crate for the lists.
* A deleted shape's `ID` is not given again, also after a reopen; the design's 4.6. `state.xml` keeps, for each page, the highest shape `ID` ever given on it: the session's mark (`Session::id_floor`,
  which holds the file's own and every `ID` the session gave) is written, and a `.diacraft` open raises the session's marks to the file's (`Session::seed_ledger`). **A ledger raises a mark and never lowers one**: a row below the
  highest `ID` of its page reads as that `ID`, a row for a page the drawing lacks is ignored (a hundred thousand of them seed nothing), and a mark of 4,294,967,295 opens and ends the page's `ID`s in "no shape ids are left on the page".
* The content stamp; the design's 4.4. `Session::content_stamp()` is the fingerprint of the model's canonical encoding **as it was when the drawing was read from a foreign file** (a VSDX one), or as the
  `.diacraft` file says it (`state.xml`). A VSDX file arms it as pending at the open, and **it is made when it is first needed, not at the open and not at a save** (the pass was a third of the open's time, and a save of a VSDX file that nothing asks the stamp of would pay for it; the first save of a drawing of 20,000 shapes was 30 to 50% slower when it did). **The pending stamp keeps the document the drawing was read as** (a clone of the `Arc` taken at the open: no pass and no copy), and the stamp is made from that document, once, by a Save As to `.diacraft` and by `Session::content_unchanged()` of a drawing that is no longer that document; the document is let go of when the stamp is made. **The save of a VSDX file and `mark_saved` make no pass**, and a drawing edited after the open still reads as edited after any number of splice saves, because the stamp does not depend on the baseline a save replaces. **The kept document is memory the session holds beside the drawing**: the session's count includes it as a document that what lets go of a step never frees, the allocations it shares with the drawing and the history counted once, and the process is told of it with the rest of the session's hold; an edit that would be refused with it counted makes the stamp (which lets go of it) and is judged again, so a drawing is not refused an edit because it was read from a foreign file and saved. Whether the pass fits (`stamp_fits`) is asked when it is made, beside what the process holds then. It is one encoding pass in all for a
  foreign file, a part at a time, counted in `Session::stamp_work()`; it is carried by every save and by a Save As to `.diacraft`, and moved by no edit or undo. **A named VSDX file arms it and nothing else does**: a template
  opened as a new drawing and a new drawing saved as VSDX are not read from a foreign file, and a `.diacraft` file keeps its own in `state.xml`. `Session::content_unchanged()` compares it with the fingerprint of the content now (**one pass each time it is asked**, and none while the stamp is pending and the drawing is the very document the stamp keeps, which is `Some(true)`): `Some(true)` when they are equal (an edit that is undone makes them equal again),
  `Some(false)` when they differ, `None` for a drawing that never came from a foreign file (a new one, one made from a template, a `.diacraft` file with none) and for content that could not be fingerprinted
  (the pass is not made when it would not fit beside what the process holds, and the codec's budget refuses a model it cannot encode; **`None` reads as edited**, and the open does not depend on it). **The decision never asks the dirty flag**, which does not
  survive a reopen: a drawing edited after it was read from a VSDX file and saved as `.diacraft` is clean in the session that opens that, and `content_unchanged()` says `Some(false)`. The model writers write
  the bookkeeping the foreign file had while it is `Some(true)`, and an edited save's otherwise.
* Templates and stencils. A `.diacraft-template` **opens as a new, unnamed drawing** (`file.open` without `edit_template`; `file.new {template: path}` takes one too): the model carries everything, the
  session keeps no file's bytes and the template's identifier ledger still stands (spec 2.7), `file.save` says to use `file.save_as`, and the template on the disk is never written; the stencils it names are open, as for a VSDX template. `file.open {edit_template: true}` opens the
  template itself, and a save writes `.diacraft-template` with the built-in stencils open at that moment. A `.diacraft-stencil` opens as a drawing with `file.open`, and `stencil.open {path}` reads it as a
  stencil (a `.diacraft` drawing or template is refused in words by its content, not its name).
* `file.status` answers `{dirty, has_file, format, variant, kind}`: `format` is `diacraft`, `vsdx` or `odg`, `variant` the extension of the type the file was read as or last saved as (`diacraft`,
  `diacraft-stencil`, `diacraft-template`, the six VSDX types or `odg`) and `kind` `drawing`, `stencil` or `template`; the last three are `null` for a drawing with no file of a type (a new one, one made from a template).
* `Session::pin_clock(Some(seconds))` pins the clock every save reads the time from (`Session::now`): the VSDX writer's modified time comes from the caller, so a test that compares two saves byte for byte
  pins it. `None` reads the system's clock again.
* **The command line.** `diacraft-cli export` reads a `.diacraft` file by `diacraft_engine::nativefile::read_native`, the one way a `.diacraft` file is opened; `run --cmd file.open` and `--cmd file.save_as` reach the same commands.

## `.odg` files

`file.open` reads an OpenDocument drawing, `file.save` and `file.save_as` write one, and the window, the CLI and the MCP server reach them through those
commands. The writer is the `odg` crate's splice writer, which changes only what an
edit touched, in the file's own bytes.

* The file's own type decides, as for the six VSDX types. `file.open {path}` sniffs the package (`diacraft_odg::sniff`: the manifest's root row, else
  `mimetype`) and reads an `.odg` with the `odg` crate's reader; any other file goes to the VSDX reader as before. The answer is the document as `document.inspect` gives it, and
  `file: {variant: "odg", kind: "drawing", form: "package" | "flat", new_from_template: false, bytes, warnings: [..first 20..], warning_count, skipped_count, diacraft: {state: "absent"}}` (`form` and the flat file); `skipped_count` is
  what the reader kept in the file's bytes without modelling it. **The first of `warnings` says what the drawing does not hold**, when there is any: the line `What DiaCraft does not hold of this file: a save into the file keeps it, and a copy saved as another file (.diacraft or another format), or a new drawing made from it, is without it`, then a line for each class with its count: shapes of kinds kept only as placeholders (a dimension line, a callout, a form control, a 3-D scene), shapes in hyperlinks that a copy writes over the shapes that were over them, font declarations that repeat a name, style properties no copy writes (a default tab distance), and pieces of the file's markup that no part of the drawing holds. A file that does not open leaves the open document as it was, in words that hold neither the path nor the
  file's text. **A drawing template (`.otg`) opens as a new drawing made from it** (`.otg` is a format to open and save and no built-in template): `file` says `variant: "otg"`, `kind: "template"`, `new_from_template: true`, the drawing keeps no file's bytes (NP10) and has no file until `file.save_as` gives it one, and with `edit_template: true` the template file itself opens (the session keeps its bytes and its index, and a save writes a template). `file.new {template: path}` starts from an `.otg` too, a drawing is refused as "not a template", and the flat form of a template is refused in words. **An `.odg` read from a file has its content stamp pending**, so that a drawing that visits `.diacraft` and comes back unedited keeps the thumbnail and the generator it was read with. The session keeps the file's bytes and the `ShapeIndex` that maps each shape of the
  model to its element (`OpenFile::odg`, behind an `Arc`, so the session's snapshots stay cheap).
* A drawing is saved in its own format. `file.save` writes an `.odg` drawing to its file and `file.save_as` takes the type from the extension, but **an `.odg`
  is saved as an `.odg` and no other type, and a drawing of another type (a VSDX file, a template, a new drawing) is never saved as an `.odg`**: that is refused in words before
  anything is made (superseded: the model writer saves them). The link, extension, folder and changed-on-disk rules of the other types hold
  (`ChangedOnDisk`, `force`, a link refused unless it leads to the drawing's own file). The answer is `{bytes, variant: "odg", kind, form, edited, macros_dropped: 0, dirty: false, warnings:
  [..first 20..], warning_count, notes, carried, checked}` (`notes`; `carried`, empty for a save into the file; `checked`: `null` for a save into the file, which is not checked in 0.2) (there are no `parts`: the writer keeps every part it does not edit, and `edited` says whether it changed any). **The type a drawing is saved as is the type it was read as** (what the package is, `OpenFile::extension`: `odg`, or the VSDX type), not what its file is called, so an `.odg` called `a.vsdx` or `a.dat` is saved as an `.odg` and a VSDX file called `v.odg` as a VSDX one; Save As in the window starts with a name of that type, so the dialog offers it, and gives a name typed with no extension that type. `file.save` of a VSDX drawing whose file is called `.odg` is a failure that says to use `file.save_as`, not a bad parameter.
* **A flat OpenDocument drawing** (`.fodg`: one XML document whose root is the office namespace's `document`) **is read by every route, saved back as a flat file by Save, and saved by Save As as a `.diacraft` file, an `.odg` or `.otg` package or a VSDX type** (never as a `.fodg`). `file.open` tells it by its content (`diacraft_odg::sniff`, so the name decides nothing: a flat file called `a.odg` or `a`, and a package called `a.fodg`, are what they are) and reads it as the package that holds the same elements, so the model is the package twin's: the same pages, shapes in the same order, frames, looks, texts and glue, and the same picture of each page, and every edit the engine has gives the same drawing from either. `file` says `form: "flat"` (`"package"` for an `.odg`) and gives **first, among `warnings`, a note of what Save does with it** (Save writes it back as a flat file, and Save As writes it as a .diacraft file or an .odg package), and `OpenFile::is_flat` says it from the file's own bytes. The Open dialog lists `.fodg`. **`file.save` writes the drawing back as a flat file, in place, whatever the file is called** (a flat drawing is saved as a flat drawing; the file's own form is kept, as for a `.vsdx` and an `.odg`): unedited it is the file's own bytes and `edited: false`; an edit is spliced into the one document (what the edit did not touch is the file's own markup, byte for byte, and the generator says who saved it); the answer is the `.odg` save's with `form: "flat"`; no thumbnail is rendered, since a flat file has none; a second save is no edit; the changed-on-disk check and `force` hold as for any file. **What the flat writer does not write is a refused save in words**: a change of the document's masters (a shape dropped from a stencil brings its master), themes, colours or cells, a page added, taken away, moved or renamed; the words end with the way out of a flat file (`Undo the change (edit.undo) to save, or use Save As to save the drawing as a .diacraft file, which holds it: a drawing opened from a flat file is saved only as a flat file by Save.`), and the file and the drawing are as they were. **`file.save_as` is available for a drawing that came from a flat file** (had its `enabled` say no, with one reason, so that `engine.commands` listed it disabled, MCP's `enabled_only` left it out and the window greyed it out): its `enabled` is that of any drawing (a document is open), and it writes the drawing **from the model** by the name it is given, because a flat file is no package to splice into: a `.diacraft` file (the model reads back equal), an `.odg` or an `.otg` by the model writer (`SavePath::OdgModel`, as for a `.diacraft` drawing), or a VSDX type across the formats. The flat file is left as it was, the file written becomes the drawing's own, and `file.save` writes it from then on. What a flat file holds in its own form comes with the drawing: its `office:meta` and `office:settings` are held by the reader as a package's `meta.xml` and `settings.xml` are, a picture it holds inline is written as an entry of `Pictures/` under the writer's own name, and its content stamp is pending as a package's is, so that a visit through `.diacraft` gives the `.odg` the drawing is saved as directly. A flat file called `a.odg` saved by Save As over its own name is a package from then on. What the flat file holds in the markup of its containers that no field reads (`office:scripts` and the like) is not held, so a Save As does not carry it (`docs/gaps.md`, F23). Save As to a `.fodg` is refused for it as for any drawing: **`file.save_as` of any drawing to a `.fodg` is refused** (`BadParams`) in words that say Save As does not offer it, judged on the file that would be written; a `file.save` of a package that a person called `.fodg` is refused by its name as before (`the file name must end in .odg`).
