* A page whose sheet names no paper, or a paper the table has no size for (a user-defined one, `32767`), prints on US Letter, and `paper.assumed` says so. `PrintPageOrientation` 1 and 2 are upright and sideways; absent, 0 (as the printer is set) or any other number holds the sheet the way the page's own size is.
* `page.orientation` swaps `PageWidth` and `PageHeight` if the page is not that way already and sets `PrintPageOrientation`: a landscape page whose paper is held upright (264 pages of the census) is turned on its paper, which is a change, though its size is right. The shapes stay where they are.
* A change of drawing scale keeps the page's size **on paper**, so `PageWidth` and `PageHeight` are worked out again (a Letter page at 1/4 in = 1 ft is 528 by 408 drawing units, not 11 by 8.5), and the shapes' cells are not touched: they print at a new size.
  `PageScale` and `DrawingScale` are written with all their digits (`V` in inches, `U` the unit chosen: `IN`, `FT`, `MM`, ...), since they are divided by each other for every length of the page. A scale of the list is read back as that scale by its ratio (`scale.preset`). The scale lists (architectural, civil engineering, metric, mechanical engineering) are ours.
  A ratio of 1:1 given as a custom scale is `DrawingScaleType` 0. The two lengths are more than 0 and at most a billion inches, the ratio is from 0.001 to 1,000,000 drawing units to a paper inch, and the page may not be more than 1,000,000 drawing units on a side (`MAX_COORD`).
* `DrawingSizeType` (2 a standard size, 5 metric, 6 ANSI engineering, 7 ANSI architectural for a named size; 3 for a custom size at 1:1 and 4 for one on a scaled page) and `DrawingScaleType` (the family of the scale; 3 custom) are written as the labels they are (nothing draws by them).
  `DrawingResizeType` 0 defers to `DrawingSizeType`, so a page that has the 0 is first given the 1 or 2 that its state comes to, and writing the label never turns Auto Size on or off.
* Auto Size is on when `DrawingResizeType` is 1, or is 0 and `DrawingSizeType` is 0 or absent, and off when it is 2 or any other number. **A page that has no `DrawingResizeType` at all, as the pages of a new drawing, has it off**
  (`Page.AutoSize` says off is the default). The same D10 notes that the census holds a 1 on 72 pages in 100; that 1 means "on" is the specification's word, not something this project could check, and `auto_size_on` (`draw/page_setup.rs`) is the one place to change.
  `page.auto_size` writes 1 or 2; turning on a page that is on already (by the 0 and 0 of the rule) is no change.
* Auto Size. With Auto Size on, a shape put or moved past the page's edge makes the page grow by **whole sheets of its printer paper**: one sheet is the paper (`PaperKind`, held the way `PrintPageOrientation` says) on paper, which is `paper.width` by `paper.height` times the page's drawing units to a paper inch;
  on each side that the shape's box passes (its four corners carried through its turn and its groups) the page gains `ceil(overshoot / sheet)` sheets, so the page is then the number of sheets it was plus those. A box that only touches the edge does not make it grow. A page whose `PrintPageOrientation` is not set (as a new drawing's) has its sheet held the way the page is, and **the first growth writes `PrintPageOrientation`**, so that the sheets do not turn when the page grows taller than wide (11 by 8.5 becomes 11 by 17). Holds: Letter paper, a shape dragged past the right edge, the page extends past its old edge and the paper stays Letter.
  Page breaks (the View tab) are the window's: `page.setup`'s `sheets` and `paper` give where they fall. **A page does not grow past 10,000 inches on paper or 1,000,000 drawing units on a side**: a shape that would need more is left off the page, and the command succeeds.
* A page's origin is its lower-left corner, so a growth on the **left or the bottom** moves the origin: every top-level shape is carried by the growth (a group takes its members), the way a paste or a group carries shapes (`draw/lift.rs`), so the drawing is not changed:
  no route is made again, a glued end follows its shape, a cell that reads a pose is worked out again, and the shape that made the page grow ends inside it (a shape put at x -0.2 on an 11-inch page ends at x 10.8 on a page of 22). A page of **more than 20,000 top-level shapes** (`MAX_SHIFT_SHAPES`; the work of a carry is linear in them) is not carried, so it does not grow on the left or the bottom (the shape stays off the page) and still grows on the right and the top.
* The hook looks at the shapes the command named or made, and no others: a shape that was past the edge before is left, and the page does not grow for it. Turning Auto Size on grows nothing.
* **Where it hooks** (`draw::fit_page`, inside the command's own edit, so the growth is part of its one undo step): `shape.drop` (and a drop from a stencil file) after the instance is added, `swimlane.create`, `swimlane.insert`, `swimlane.insert_phase`, `swimlane.resize` and `swimlane.orientation` and the drops of a Swimlane, a Separator, a Pool and a Lane after the structure is laid out, for the whole structure and not only the part made, `shape.move` and `shape.align` after the move, `shape.resize` and `shape.size` after the resize, `shape.set_end` and `shape.set_length` after the end moves, `shape.rotate` and `shape.flip` after the turn or flip,
  `edit.paste` and `shape.duplicate` after the copies are placed, and `connector.autoconnect` after the new shape is made, moved beside the other and connected (a growth on the left or the bottom carries the new shape and its connector with everything else, and the answer's `x` and `y` are read after it). `shape.delete`, `edit.cut`, `shape.group`, `shape.ungroup`, `shape.pin` (the shape draws where it did) and the other connector commands do not grow the page. The answer of a command does not say that the page grew: read `page.setup`. **A growth that cannot be made** (the page's size or a shape's pin is protected by `GUARD`, a number is out of range) is dropped and the command goes on without it, since refusing a drop for a shape elsewhere that cannot move would be worse than a shape off the page.
* ("a page name has at most 31 characters"; the spec does not say what happens past 31, and V5 says the dialog limits or refuses it, so DiaCraft does both). **A command that gives a page a name refuses one of more than 31 characters**, counted as characters and not bytes: `page.rename`, `page.add` (a background page too) and, in the copy `page.duplicate` makes, the name of the page cut short to leave room for its number. The refusal is in words ("a page name must be at most 31 characters"), is made before anything is written, and leaves no undo step and no journal entry. The box of a page's tab and the Name box of Page Setup take no more than 31 characters as they are typed. **A name a file holds stays as it is, however long** (the model holds up to 255 characters, `diacraft_doc::MAX_NAME_CHARS`): a reader does not cut it, a save writes it back as it is, and an edit that does not name the page leaves it; the cap is the rule of the commands that name a page (`diacraft_doc::check_given_page_name`), and the model's own audit and the readers' `Document::add_page` still take the longer name. A rename of such a page to its own name is a command that names a page, and is refused.
* Our rule (found by opening the files DiaCraft writes in the reference application, which renames a page called "page" and digits, such as an `.odg`'s `page1`, and a repeated page name, and gives the renamed page's `Name` and `NameU` different numbers; the specifications give no rule for how names are compared, so they are compared without regard to case, the safe reading). **No two pages of a drawing have one name, and no page is named "page" and digits.** (1) **The commands that give a page a name** (`page.add`, a background page too, `page.rename`, the copy `page.duplicate` makes and the renumbering `page.move` does) refuse a name another page has, compared without regard to case, and a name that is `page` in any case followed by the digits 0 to 9 and nothing more (`page1`, `PAGE12`; `Page-1`, `Page 1`, `page1a` and `pages1` are other names). The refusal is in words ("another page has this name", "a page name must not be \"page\" and digits"), is made before anything is written, and leaves no undo step and no journal entry; a page may be given its own name again, in another case too; a renumbering that would give a page a name another page keeps (a background page's, or a name a person gave) is refused whole, with nothing renamed. A page added with no name is called `Page-N` for its `ID` N or for the next N whose name no page has, a background page `VBackground-N` for the first N no page has, and a copy the name of its source and `-N` for the first N no page has the name of, each looked for among the names and the universal names (`NameU`) of the pages, without regard to case (`Document::add_page`, `Document::default_page_name`). (2) **The VSDX writers write names the reference application keeps** (`diacraft_vsdx::keep_page_names`, used by the writer of a drawing never saved, the model writer and a save into a file for a page it writes): a page whose `Name` is `page` and digits or repeats another page's, or whose `NameU` is or does, is given the default form `Page-N` for the lowest N that no page has, the same in `Name` and `NameU` (when only the `NameU` is the trouble, a new `NameU` and the name a person gave kept), and the save says so in its warnings, by the page's place in the list and its new name and with no name of the drawing in it, and how many formulas followed the page. **A page the writer renames is named by DiaCraft and not by the person, so no formula may read `#REF!` for it:** every formula that names the page by the name it had (`Pages[page1]!`, by its `NameU` or its `Name`, a name in quotes or with blanks, or by a number, `Pages[2]`, a page by its `NameU`) is rewritten to name the page by its new name, in a shape, a member of a group, a page's sheet, a master and its shapes, a style and the document's sheet, the bytes of the formula kept but the bytes between the brackets (`diacraft_formula::page_index_spans`, `crates/vsdx/src/page_follow.rs`), and the cell keeps its value, unit and the rest; a formula that still finds the page by what it says is left as it is, and so are a string that holds the text and a name that finds no page. A Save As to a VSDX type then works out the cells that give a page's name (`PAGENAME()`) and the fields that show it, as `page.rename` does, so that the file holds what the drawing is and the drawing becomes what the file reads as; **a field that shows anything else (a page number, a page count, a date, the file's name) keeps the text the file held**, as it does when no page is renamed (the rename is the writer's, and no person edited the drawing). `page.rename` by the person is not changed: it leaves the formulas that name the old name reading `#REF!`. **The links to such a page by its name follow it too**: the `SubAddress` of a `Hyperlink` row with no `Address` (a link of this drawing), when it is plain text that names the page (`page1`, or `page1/Shape`, the page found by its name as a click finds it, the first page with the name, and after that by its universal name, as the formulas do), is written with the page's new name, the blanks round it and the text after the slash kept, in a shape, a master, a page's sheet and the rest; the `SubAddress` of a link with an address (a web address's fragment) is left; and **an `.odg`'s own page link**, which the model keeps as markup and a VSDX file carries in DiaCraft's part (a `text:a` round some text or a `draw:a` round a shape, an `xlink:href` of exactly `#<page>`), is written `#<new name>` (`crates/vsdx/src/page_follow.rs`, `page_hrefs.rs`), so that the file read again, and an `.odg` made from it, hold a link that finds its page. The save's warning says how many links followed. A link by name that a person leaves behind a `page.rename`, and the links of the `.odg` writer, which keeps the names, are not changed. The first page of a name keeps it, and a page renamed never takes a name that a page after it keeps. A save into a file leaves a page row the file holds as it is: a name a file has is kept as the reader keeps it, and a save with no edit writes what it read. A Save As to a VSDX type of a drawing read from an `.odg` or a `.diacraft` file is handed the drawing so named, so that the check after the save finds the pages the same and the drawing becomes what the file reads as. (3) **The `.odg` and `.diacraft` writers keep the names as they are**, and a name a file holds stays as the reader gives it: an `.odg` names its pages `page1`, `page2` (and may give two pages one name), a `.diacraft` file holds the names of the drawing it was saved from, and a draw.io file's page names are made different by the reader with regard to case, so two names that differ only in case come in as they are. The model still takes any name from a reader (`Document::add_page` with a name, `Document::rename_page`); the rule is the commands' and the VSDX writers'. A name made of the page's own number, an `.odg`'s, is therefore refused by the commands and renamed in a VSDX file, and the `.odg` writer still refuses in words two pages under one name.
* Our rule (the tabs show the pages that are not backgrounds before the backgrounds). **A command that is not given a page works on the first page that is not a background, and on the first page there is when every page is one** (`Document::first_foreground_page`). A file lists its background pages first and a drawing a session makes keeps them so, so the first page of the model is a background page in any drawing that has one, which a drawing opened on and the window works on is not: `file.export` and `diacraft-cli export` and `convert` draw the first page that is not a background (`--page N` stays the page's place in the drawing as the file lists it, so `--page 1` is the background), `insert.picture` puts the picture on it, `guide.list` lists its guides, `text.field_choices` and `edit.paste` (when the page the shapes were copied from is gone) take it, and so do the commands that were already told so (the setup, layer, theme, container, relayout, swimlane and org chart commands, `page.duplicate`). **The pages that hold a shape are looked for in the order of the tabs**, the pages that are not backgrounds first: a command about shapes that is not given a page works on the first page that holds all of them, and a shape's `ID` is its page's own, so a background page and another may both have a shape 1 and the search takes the one a person works on. A command that names a page by its `ID` takes that page, a background page too, and a command that works on every page (`scope` all, a save, a search of every page) is not a default and is not changed; `theme.variant` and `theme.preview` over every page say the theme of the first of them that is not a background. The round trip tool's salted edit (`roundtrip --edit`, `--move`) acts on the first shape of the first page that has one, as it always did: it is a test of the file, not of the drawing a person works on.
* `page.delete` takes a page out with its shapes. **A drawing keeps one page that is not a background** (a drawing of backgrounds only has no page to open); the last such page is refused. A page that named the deleted one as its background (`BackPage`) names none after it (the answer's `unassigned` says how many, and Undo puts them back with the page). Nothing else is rewritten. The page's `ID` may be given again by a later `page.add` (`Document::add_page` takes the highest `ID` plus one), and the writer takes a page of the same `ID` for the page it replaced.
* `page.move` puts a page at a place among the **pages that are not backgrounds**, counted from 0 as the tabs show them ("foreground tabs stay left of background tabs, and background tabs cannot be moved"); a background is refused, and every background keeps its place in the list. With `renumber` every such page with a default name (`Page-` and a number) is named for the place it has now: `Page-1` for the first, `Page-2` for the second; a name a person gave is left alone, and `NameU` is not touched. A move to the place the page has, with nothing to rename, is no undo step.
* Our rule ("a copy of the page on view, with its shapes, for separate editing"). A copy of a page is the page whole: its page cells (so its layers, its size and its scale), its shapes with their ids, its connects and the background page it names. It has an `ID` of its own, one past the highest, and is named for its source and `-2` (`Page-1-2`), or the first number from 2 that no page has taken: no specification gives the name, and a name too long to take the number is cut short, so that the copy's name has at most 31 characters (the source keeps the name its file gave it, however long). It stands **right after its source** in the list, and the copy of a background page is a background page. The page's shapes are shared with the source until one of them is written to, so a copy costs what a page costs once it is changed. **What belongs to the place the page had in its package is left behind**: its part, its relationship, the `Rel` its row held, the unknown markup of its OpenDocument page element and every attribute of the relationships namespace among what its slot keeps (counted in `Page::leave_package` and `refs::leave_package_for_copy`, as a master that leaves its package is), and the file the drawing is saved into gives the copy a part of its own. **A picture or an object that a file names by a relationship of its page's part is copied with the page**: the part a save makes for the copy, through either VSDX writer, has a row for every picture, embedded object and other part its shapes name, leading to the part the source's row leads to, so the two pages share one part and nothing is copied; a shape keeps the id it names when the new part has no row of it, and is given another only when two of its shapes name one id for two parts (`vsdx/src/write/page_rows.rs`). So does every relationship id of a shape's kept markup, such as the `ForeignData` of a shape whose `Type` is not `Foreign`, which the reader keeps whole and does not read (`page_rows/kept.rs`). A copy whose source is taken out, in the same save or a later one, keeps them. A picture with no relationship, one that came from another format, is copied as the source holds it, and the save gives it a part of its own made from the model's bytes. (The clipboard still pastes a shape with a picture of a file only on the page it was copied from.) A drawing of 1,000 pages cannot have another, and says so. **A cell that reads the page it is on (`PAGENAME()`, `PAGENUMBER()`) keeps the value it had until the cell is next worked out**, as a renamed page's does.
* Our rule, gap F40; the specifications say a formula names a page by its `NameU` and give no rule for what a rename, a copy or a delete does to the formulas that name the page, so this reading is ours and unverified. **A command that changes the pages** (`page.add`, `page.duplicate`, `page.rename`, `page.delete`, `page.move` with or without `renumber`, `page.type`, `page.background`) **works out, in the same undo step, every cell whose formula names a page it gave another reading**: a name or a number that found a page and now finds another or none, or none and now finds one (the first page of the list that has a name is the one found, so a move or a renumbering changes it too), and the names of a page that was renamed, added or taken away. The text of the formula is not rewritten: a cell that named a page that is gone reads `#REF!` with its last good value, and reads the page again when a page has the name. A cell that names no page but reads the list (`PAGENAME()`, `PAGENUMBER()`, `PAGECOUNT()`, `BKGPAGENAME()`) is worked out after any such change, **except that a page that is only renamed changes the names and not the order of the pages**: `PAGENAME()` and `BKGPAGENAME()` are worked out and `PAGENUMBER()` and `PAGECOUNT()` are not, so the value one of them holds is kept (a page added, taken away, moved or made a background, or given another background, works out all four). The cells that read what changed follow, on any page, in the one commit, and the connectors glued to the shapes that moved are routed again; a change that gave no name another reading (a page's setup) works out nothing, and one nothing reads costs the comparison of the pages and, the first time in a drawing, the listing of its sheets. The work shares the evaluator's 20 million steps; a change it does not cover is refused in words (`the cells that read pages are too large to work out again after this change to the pages ... nothing was changed`). Undo, redo and a save and a reopen give the pages as they were.
* Our rule where noted. A page of Type Background is a page with `Background` on, and any page may name one background page of its own, a background page too. `page.add {background: true}` names the page `VBackground-N` for the first number from 1 that no page has taken, copies the setup of the page `like` names, and puts it **before the first page that is not a background**, as a file lists them; the tabs show the backgrounds after the other pages whatever the order of the list. **A page names only a background page, never itself and never a page that names it back** (MS-VSDX forbids a `BackPage` that names a foreground page, and a loop is one the renderer stops at; `page.background` refuses each in words). `page.type` makes a page a background page (it goes where an added one does) or a page that is not (it goes after every other page, and the pages that named it name none after it, counted in `unassigned`); **a drawing keeps one page that is not a background**, so the last is not made one. Each is no undo step when the page has the type or the background already. `Background` and `BackPage` kept in `raw` in a spelling the model does not write back (`Background="true"`, `BackPage="007"`) are taken out of `raw` with the change, because a writer lets a kept spelling win. A foreground page draws over the shapes of its background and the pointer meets only the shapes of the page on view (the renderer paints the farthest background first). **Saving:** VSDX and `.diacraft` hold the type, the assignment and the order (`Background`, `BackPage`; `background`, `back-page`); **a VSDX file lists the background pages first** (in each of the 70 corpus files that hold both kinds, every background page comes before every foreground one): a drawing a session makes is in that order already, and the writers that make the pages index from the model (a new drawing, a save from a `.diacraft` or `.odg` drawing, and every Save As to a VSDX type) put a drawing that is not in it so, each page keeping its `ID`, name, `BackPage` and content and each kind its order, and the drawing in the session becomes what the file holds (no undo step); **a plain Save into the file the drawing was opened from keeps the order the file has**, as it changes only what was edited, and a page `page.move` took to another place is written to that place; `.diacraft` keeps the model's order, as it keeps the whole model; **the window a writer makes (a new drawing's, and the windows part a drawing gets when its window settings are set) opens the first page that is not a background, and the document settings' `TopPage` names it**, where the first page of the list is a background page (a drawing of backgrounds only opens its first page). **Opening**: the window opens the first page that is not a background whatever order the file lists the pages in and whatever page its own window and `TopPage` name (a file an earlier build wrote names a background page there), and its tabs put the background pages after the others, set apart; a drawing opened from an `.odg` takes a copied page, and **a background page added to it is refused at the save in words** (`odg/src/write/structure.rs`: a background is a master page that holds shapes, and a new one is not written into the file), with the way out (Undo, or Save As `.diacraft`).

**For the window (the Design tab's Page Setup group and the dialog's page tabs).** Size: `page.presets` gives the gallery (group by `group`); the current choice is `page.setup`'s `size.id`; More Page Sizes is the dialog's page-size tab (pre-defined: `page.size {preset}`; custom: `page.size {width, height}`).
Orientation: two items for `page.orientation`, the current one `page.setup`'s `orientation` (the page's, which is what the button shows). Auto Size: a toggle, pressed when `auto_size`, sending `page.auto_size {on: !auto_size}`. The dialog's Print Setup tab: `paper` (`page.presets` `papers`, `page.paper {kind}`) and its way round; Drawing Scale: `scales` and the custom form; Page Properties: the name is `page.rename`, the Type `page.type` and the Background `page.background`.
The page tabs: `page.add {like}` for the plus control, `page.duplicate {id}` for Duplicate, `page.add {background: true, like}` for Background Page, `page.delete {id}`, `page.move {id, to, renumber}` for dragging a tab and for the Reorder Pages dialog. A window that draws page breaks reads `paper` and `sheets`. The Rust side is `diacraft_engine::draw::{read_setup, paper::{SIZES, PAPERS, SCALES}}`.
Not here, and not hidden by a control that would send them: Fit to Drawing (P1), resizing the page by dragging its edge (P1), keeping the page and the printer paper apart as a user choice (P1; `page.paper` sets the paper, and the size commands set it when the size is a paper), print margins and centring.

## Themes

Applying a theme to a page or to every page, taking it off, and its variants: the engine side of the Design tab's Themes and Variants galleries. The rows are the checklist's "Themes"
(Apply a theme: P0; Apply a theme to one page or all, Theme variants: P1); the format is the VSDX theme part and the cells are the theme cells (the scheme and variation cells, the Quick Style cells).
Code: `crates/engine/src/theme/` (`catalogue.rs`, the five themes; `kit.rs`, the lists they are made of; `style.rs`, the `Theme` style; `apply.rs`, applying; `masters.rs`, the masters a theme reaches an instance through), `cmd/theme.rs`, and the writer's side in
`crates/vsdx` (`theme_write.rs`, a definition made into a theme part; `write/themes.rs`, the part added to, rewritten in and taken out of a package). The reference app was never taken apart: every rule below is **ours**
and is listed in the report of the task for the check list. **The themes are originals** (`docs/provenance.md`): names, colours, typefaces and lists are our own.
`page` is optional and is the first page that is not a background; `scope` is `page` (the default) or `all` (every page of the drawing, backgrounds too: "pages in one file can differ").

| Command | Parameters | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `theme.list` (query) | `page`?; works with no document | `{themes: [{id, name, scheme, in_drawing, colours: {dark1, light1, dark2, light2, accents: [6], hyperlink, followed_hyperlink, background}, fonts: {heading, body}, variants: [{index, name, monotone, colours: [7]}]}], variants: [names], page}`: the Themes gallery (`colours` as `#rrggbb`; `variants` are the four of that theme, `monotone` marking the single-hue one), and the theme the page has: `page: {page, theme, colors, styles, selection: [{cell, value}]}` with `theme` an id of the list, `none`, or `custom` (a number of a theme the file brought), `colors` and `styles` the variants picked; null with no document |
| `theme.apply` | `theme` (an id of `theme.list`, or `none`), `variant`? (0 to 3, default 0), `scope`?, `page`? | `{theme, variant, scope, pages, changed_pages, shapes_linked, cells_rewritten, theme_added, style_added, locked}`: the pages worked on and those that changed, how many times a shape began to follow the `Theme` style, how many scheme cells of shapes were given the page's numbers, whether the theme's part and the style were added (the style also when a `Theme` style with no cell, which another program's save of an `.odg` leaves, was filled in), and how many shapes on a locked layer were passed over (no link and no cell is written into them) |
| `theme.variant` | `variant`, or `colors` and/or `styles` (each 0 to 3); `scope`?, `page`? | as `theme.apply`, for the theme the page has (an id or `custom`): `variant` picks the colours and the styles together, `colors` and `styles` one of them. A page with no theme is a failure (with `scope` `all` the pages that have none are left out, and it is a failure only when none has) |

Each is one undo step (all the pages of `scope` all together, the part and the style with it), and one that would change nothing (a theme and variant a page has, with every shape following it) is no undo step and does not make the drawing unsaved.
A call that fails (a page that is not there, a drawing at the cap of themes) changes nothing.

* A theme of the catalogue joins the drawing's themes (`Document::themes`) when no part carries its number (`ThemeIndex` is found by `schemeEnum`, never by a part's place). A part the drawing already holds under that number is used as it is, whoever made it. The part is named
  `theme<n>.xml` for the least `n` no theme of the model has (a neutral name: a later change gave up the folder of a VSDX package's path, which the document file of an `.odg` wrote as it was and so named the product in a file of another format; a VSDX package is the same bytes, the writer naming a part it adds itself); **the writer names it again** when it adds it to a package (the least `n` no part has) and a model that holds the same bytes under another name is the same part (`write/themes.rs`), so a
  save of a drawing that was saved does not take a part out and put it back. A drawing holds at most `MAX_THEMES` (256) parts and `MAX_THEME_BYTES` (4 MiB) of them, as many as the reader keeps: past that the command fails and a save refuses.
* The five components of a theme carry **one number**, 1001 (Tidepool), 1002 (Fernwood), 1003 (Cinderglow), 1004 (Inkstone) and 1005 (Plumline), as the pages of real files hold one number in all five cells. Real parts carry 33 to 60, so a
  drawing that holds both never selects the wrong part. Whether the reference app takes a number that no theme of its own has is not known.
* `ThemeIndex`, `ColorSchemeIndex`, `EffectSchemeIndex`, `ConnectorSchemeIndex` and `FontSchemeIndex` of the **page sheet** take the theme's number, and `VariationColorIndex` and `VariationStyleIndex` the variant's place (0 to 3, zero-based). **No theme** writes 0 to all seven, which sends every themed cell
  back to the root style; the part and the style stay in the drawing. A page that holds none of the cells and is given none is not written to.
* The style a shape follows to take the theme's values is the one named `Theme`, made when the drawing has none (the first free `ID`, based on the root style through all three links, **or, in a drawing opened from an `.odg` whose file has a style named `standard` (LibreOffice's default drawing style, the parent of every shape's own style in the files it writes), based on that style, so that a program that draws the style as an empty common style draws the shapes that follow it with the drawing's face and not its own defaults (a serif, in LibreOffice); a file with no such style, a new drawing's blank package among them, gets the style on the root and an `.odg` that names no parent for it**) and used as it is when it has one. It holds what a file's does: the call `THEMEVAL()` with the marker `Themed` in each line,
  fill, shadow and gradient cell the theme answers, the ten rows of `FillGradient`, `Color` and `Font` of `Character` row 0, 65534 in the scheme cells (which sends a shape to its page) and the Quick Style cells. **The Quick Style numbers are ours**: 100 in the four matrices and in the fill, line and shadow colours
  (the first style of the page's style variant and the first colour of its colour variant, which is what makes a variant one click), 0 in the font colour (`dk1`). A shape of type `Shape` (to any depth of groups; a group, a guide and a picture are left alone) whose line, fill or text family has **no style or the root style**, of its own and from the master shape it stands for (a master that links a style gives its instances that style, and a link of the instance would outrank it), follows `Theme` for that family, **an instance through the master's shape it stands for** (the master's shape is linked and the instance keeps no link of its own). A shape with a style of its own keeps it, and
  **a cell a person set stays set**: a fill chosen with `shape.format` is not changed by a theme ("standard colours stay put").
* A theme reaches an instance through its master; the owner's ruling of 2026-11-27 "Link masters to the theme"; observed in the reference application on the project's test PC: the files it writes link their masters' shapes to the `Theme` style and leave the instances with none. In its check of the earlier build every instance of the seventeen notation connector masters read `BeginArrow` 0, `EndArrow` 0, `LinePattern` 1 and `FillPattern` 1 from `THEMEVAL()` after `theme.apply`, a solid line with no ends: the instance was linked to the style itself, and the application reads an instance's own link before its master's cells of that family. **So a theme links the master's shape an instance stands for** (the master's first top-level shape, and for a member of an instance the shape its `MasterShape` names) to the `Theme` style for each family that has no style or the root, of the instance's own and the master shape's, **and the instance keeps no link of its own**: a link to the root, or to the `Theme` style (an instance an earlier build linked itself), is taken off. `theme.apply`, a shape put on a page that has a theme and a theme colour or a Quick Style do it (`crates/engine/src/theme/masters.rs`). **A shape with no master** (a box the tools draw, a text box, a connector of `connector.add`) links the style itself, as before. **One master serves every page:** the style's cells are worked out on the instance, and their scheme cells hold 65534, which reads the instance's own page, so pages of two themes or two variants share a master, and on a page with no theme its instances read the root's cells; no master is copied. **A master is left as it is where linking it would change a shape the theme does not reach**: an instance that reads the family through it (no link of its own for the family) on a locked layer of the page, on another page that selects a theme the instance does not follow, or under a sheet of its own that selects one. The instances the theme reaches then link the style themselves, as before, so nothing draws otherwise than it did. That is found by one walk of the drawing, made only when a master's shape is still to be linked (a drop of a master the theme reaches already makes none, counted), of at most 4,000,000 shapes (past them no master is linked by the command). **A shape read from an `.odg`** follows the theme by links of its own, as before (the file holds no master another program reads, and its automatic style's parent is its link), and a save to VSDX takes off the copy a link of such a shape that is its master shape's (`across/onto.rs`: the `.odg` reader gives an instance the parent its style names, and the master in DiaCraft's document file links the same style). **"No theme" and `theme.variant`** write no link, and the masters stay linked as the shapes' own links did. **Undo and redo** take a master's links back and forward with the rest of the command's step. A file's own masters and instances are as the file has them until a theme is applied. **The files:** the model writer, the splice (which patches the master's part at the shape's start tag and leaves the page part as it was) and a Save As from a `.diacraft` and from an `.odg` drawing write the master's shape linked to the `Theme` style and the instance with no `LineStyle`, `FillStyle` or `TextStyle`; an unedited save is the file's bytes (`crates/engine/tests/it/theme_master_links.rs`, which also draws every master of the catalogue under each theme against the drawing as the earlier rule linked it, pixel for pixel, and pages of two themes and of none). That the application then reads the master's line ends, pattern and fill with the theme's line colour is our reading, unverified until its check of this build.
* Our rule. With no theme selected a cell holding the marker reads the root style's cell of its name; **where the root holds no such cell** (a new drawing's root holds no `BeginArrowSize` or `EndArrowSize`, where every file's root holds every line cell), `THEMEVAL()` gives no value (`#N/A`) and each reader takes its own default, as for a cell found nowhere: so a shape that follows the `Theme` style on a page with no theme draws as a shape that follows no style does. The 0 drew the smallest line end there, where the readers' default is the medium one: "No theme" after a theme drew a connector's ends small, and so would the instances of a master a theme linked for another page. A call that names its property (`THEMEVAL("ConnectorEndSize")`) gives the root's cell or the default, as before. **That is for the cells every root holds**: those directly under the sheet and row `IX` 0 of `FillGradient` and `LineGradient`. **A stop row past the first** (`IX` 1 and up) is no such cell, since a root holds row 0 and no more: it reads the root's cell of its own row where the root holds that row, and where it holds none **the cell's own default**, 0 for a transparency and a position and black for a colour ("other rows have no root value"), never the root's row 0 and never `#N/A`, with the root's section there or not (the first form of the rule gave every stop row past the first `#N/A` on a page with no theme).
* A shape that holds a scheme cell of its own with a plain whole number (not 65534, not 65535, not a formula) takes the number the page now selects (a new theme rewrites it on the shapes), unless the `Lock...` cell that matches is set on the shape or inherited by it (`LockThemeIndex` for `ThemeIndex`, `LockThemeColors` for `ColorSchemeIndex` and `VariationColorIndex`,
  `LockThemeEffects` for `EffectSchemeIndex` and `VariationStyleIndex`, `LockThemeConnectors` and `LockThemeFonts`: our reading, says only that they keep a new theme from changing the number; **and `LockVariation` for both variant cells** (a variant chosen for the page, or the variant of a theme applied, skips a shape that holds it even when the colour and effect locks are off, and a colour or effect lock alone still holds its own variant cell)). A cell the page does not change is not written.
* "Apply theme to new shapes": on by default. A shape put on a page that selects a theme follows the `Theme` style as the shapes of `theme.apply` do (an instance through its master's shape), in the same undo step: `shape.drop` from a built-in stencil and from a stencil file (the instance and the members it lists), `text.box` (the box keeps the no fill and no line it is made with, and its text is the theme's colour and face),
  `connector.add`, and the shape and connector of `connector.autoconnect`. Nothing is done when the page selects no theme, or the drawing has no `Theme` style (a page of a file that selects a theme and holds none is left as the file has it). A shape that a paste or a duplicate makes keeps the links its source had; there is no option to turn it off. **A colour that the shape's master gives by a formula of `THEMEVAL`** (a C4 element's accent) **is the theme's as the shape is linked** (`theme/new_colours.rs`): the cells of the master's shape, and of the members the instance lists, whose formula calls `THEMEVAL` are worked out for the instance, each in the one evaluator with the default budget (at most 256 shapes and 64 cells of each master shape), and a result that differs from the master's cached colour is held on the instance as `Inh`. Without it a shape dropped into a themed page showed the colour the master was built with, which has no theme, until something recalculated it; a budget that runs out refuses the drop in words and the document is as it was.
  **In an `.odg`** the shape's three links to the `Theme` style (its own or, for an instance on a page that selects a theme, its master shape's) are saved: its own automatic style names `Theme` as its parent, and the cells the shape has from that style and from no cell of its own or of its master's are not written as constants, so that the file a session of its own opens holds the shape on the style and `theme.variant` moves it. A program that draws the style as an empty common style draws such a shape from the style's own chain (the file's default graphic style, or its own defaults) and not with the theme's colours, as it draws the shapes of the file that follow the theme; a shape whose three links are not all that style is saved on the root with its look as constants and the save says the link is not written.
* The **whole page** is worked out again after a change (`calc`'s `affected.rs`: what `THEMEVAL` reads of the sheet's theme cells is not followed, and a caller whose edit changes them asks for the page, `Changes::whole_page`). A cell holding the marker is not written by a recalculation (`commit.rs`): the renderer asks the theme each time it draws, so the new theme shows at once.
  A cell that holds a number under a theme formula, as a file from another application has, is written with what the theme gives now; and so is every other formula of the page whose result differs from the number the file saved (that is what a whole-page recalculation is, and why a theme on a foreign page may write more than a move does). **The connectors glued to the shapes the pass resized are routed again** (a theme that gives the text another face makes a compartment wrap another way, and the class is taller).
  **An instance is given a cell it inherits and does not hold only where the theme changed what the cell works out to on it** (the Recalculation item): an instance that follows its master's style keeps every cell as its file left it, and one the theme reaches (by links of its own or through its master's shape) holds, `Inh` with the theme's value, the cells its master's theme formulas now give it another value for than its master's, which is how it shows the theme.
* Each theme has **four colour variants** and **four style variants**: the colour variants are the accents in their own order, one place on, one hue in seven tones (`monotone`: every variant colour is the first) and three places on, the seventh colour of each being the theme's second dark colour; the style variants are
  Original (a pale fill with the colour's outline, a dark fill with white text, a plain colour, white with a heavy outline), Gradient (soft gradients and a soft shadow), Outline (white or pale, thick outlines, no shadow) and Raised (the first variant's fills with a deeper shadow). **The variants pick lines 1 to 3 only** (`kit.rs`): a connector's list holds three
  entries and an entry past a list reads the no-theme table. The theme's `Look` gives each its character: Tidepool and Plumline round corners (`vt:lineEx` `rndg`) and use wide soft shadows, Cinderglow heavy lines and hard shadows, Inkstone fine lines and no shadow, Fernwood thin lines.
* Fonts are open families (Liberation Sans and Serif, DejaVu Sans and Serif): a face is named in a drawing and never embedded (the check list, "No font embedding"), and none is a face the project may not ship. `THEMEVAL` answers `Font` with the theme's body face (`a:minorFont`); the heading face is in the part and is read by nothing.
* A theme part is written as the samples' are: `a:theme` with `a:themeElements` (`a:clrScheme`, `a:fontScheme`, `a:fmtScheme`), `a:objectDefaults` and `a:extraClrSchemeLst`, every extension of R7 under its URI with the `vt:` namespace declared by the child, a declaration with `standalone="yes"`, six entries in each list of the effect scheme and three in
  the connector scheme's, one more `vt:lineStyle` than lines, four variants of each kind. A part written reads back as the definition it was made from (`tests/it/theme_write.rs`, a generated test over any definition), and no colour, modifier or list the reader would cut is written.
* As amended, one outside report of the reference app's reading, unverified. A package may list a theme part in its content types and leave out the relationship that names it. When the document part has **no theme relationship at all**, the reader takes as the drawing's themes the parts whose content type is the theme's (in the order of their names), and failing that the part `theme/theme1.xml` beside the document part, and only a part that reads as an `a:theme`: any other part stays an unknown part, held as the bytes it is. The report says each (`theme_without_relationship`). A document part that has a theme relationship is read as it always was, a part beside the one it names staying unknown. A save that changes no theme keeps the file's own way (the part, its content type and the document part's relationships are the original's), and so does one that only rewrites the part's bytes; a save that gives the document another theme relationship (a theme added beside the part) gives the part one too, since the reader looks at content types only where there is none; the model writers always write a relationship. A saved file reads with the themes the drawing had.
* As amended, one outside report, unverified. A cell with a formula and **no value saved anywhere on the way to it** (a style's `THEMEVAL()` with no `V` beside it, a shape's formula alone) is worked out where it is read, on the sheet that asked, with the cells it reads worked out as well (`Evaluator::evaluate_worked_out`), and not read as a default (the root style's white fill and black line). **Every reader that draws or shows a cell reads it so**: the renderer (every cell of a shape's frame, look and text, and the cells of the rows of its geometry, so the picture, the PNG, SVG and PDF exports and the print agree), `shape.formatting` and the planners of the format commands (a Quick Style leaves alone a cell that follows the theme by a call of `THEMEVAL` and no saved value, as it does one that holds the marker, and a scheme cell that works out to the page's; a colour turns off a gradient that a formula with no saved value turns on and keeps a pattern one works out to; a run cell that holds a formula is no plain number), the ShapeSheet window and `sheet.cell` (the value shown is what the formula works out to, in the unit the cell shows in, and an error shows as the error) and the copy an `.odg` save makes of a shape the file does not hold (the writer reads values). The cell is not written: a save adds no `V` to a cell that had none (the answers are kept beside the model, never in it). A cell with a saved value, `Themed` or not, stands as saved. A result that is no value (an error, a function the evaluator lacks) leaves the cell as it was read before; a cycle of such cells is cut. **The work is bounded and paid once.** The steps for these cells are a budget of their own beside the themed cells' (a frame: 32,000,000, a part to each share of a walk shared out among threads; a read of a window of the ShapeSheet: 1,000,000; the formatting commands, `shape.formatting` and an `.odg` save: 32,000,000 for the command, and **one for the whole gallery of Quick Styles**, which lends it to the readers of its 46 tiles in turn), and cells past them read as they did before, the frame saying so (`UnsavedUnanswered`, "cells left at their defaults"). **The answers are kept from one frame to the next** (`WorkedCache`): the window's drawer makes a cache for each document value it draws, held with the document, and the frames of that value (a pan, a zoom, the rough picture and the full one) work out only what an earlier frame did not, in at most 64,000,000 steps and 400,000 answers in all; an edit makes a new document value and the next frame is drawn with a cache of its own, so no answer is ever out of date and nothing is kept for a document that is gone. A page of 30,000 shapes that follow a style of such cells is drawn themed whole, and its second frame works nothing out (counted tests). **The readers that edit and pick read it so too** (a follow-up of public issue 14): the commands' reader (`draw/read.rs`: `shape.placement` (Size & Position), `shape.move`, `shape.resize` and every command that reads a shape's pin, size, turn, flips, ends or connection points), the snap's reads (the box, the handles, the connection points, the outline of a shape and the line of a guide), the shape operations, the pen and the connection edges (a row's `X` of `Width` and no value is the width), a shape's text block, the table of layers (`layer.list`, and the layers the pointer's scene passes over: a layer whose `Visible` is `0` by a formula and no value is hidden, one whose `Lock` is `1` is locked), the window's scene (`ui-egui`'s `Scene`: a shape's frame, its geometry rows, its ends, its `SelectMode` and its connection points, so a click, a rubber band and a drag find a shape pinned, sized or turned by a formula where it is drawn) and the group's `IsTextEditTarget` (`=FALSE` sends the text to the member on top). **A shape pinned at `=1+1` with no `V` is picked, moved, snapped to and shown at 2 inches**, where it was read at the origin. The cell is not written: a move writes the cell it moves, as a value, and nothing else gains a `V`. **A result that is no value is read by one rule in every reader**: a formula that gives none (an error, a function the evaluator lacks, steps that ran out, a formula that needed more than a part of them) leaves the cell reading as a cell that holds no value anywhere on the way, which is **the root style's value for a shape's cell that the root style holds** and the reader's own default for any other (`Resolver::root_standin`, which the renderer, the formatting controls and the commands' `Worked` all call, so that a cell is not drawn one way and picked, moved or reported another; give such a cell the default of its kind and unit, which differs from this only for a cell the root style holds a value of; this follows the renderer's reading, which is the specification's for a `THEMEVAL` the theme cannot answer, and assumed for any other formula). A number a reader wants is not read from a text, a colour or `#N/A`, and nothing stands in for those: `#N/A` is the answer "no value", as the theme gives it for a stop past its list. **The work is paid once for a reader and bounded for all the readers of one operation** (`draw/worked.rs`, `Worked`): a reader makes one evaluator when it meets the first such cell and keeps it, with its answers, for its life, so a cell is worked out once for a reader and the lists of the page's shapes are built once, not for each cell (the cost of a hang on a page of thousands of shapes); the scene is kept for a revision and reads at most 5,000 shapes, the snap's page is kept for a revision and its index reads at most 10,000, so **a click, a rubber band or a frame of a drag works out no cell**, and a query a drag sends (`snap.at`) works out the cells of the few shapes it looks at (counted: six on a page of 10,000) and no page. The steps are one budget for all the readers of an operation: 8,000,000 for a command in all (the session enters a new budget for each top-level command, a batch sharing its own) and for a scene's build and the connection points it reads later, taken by a reader 50,000 at a time and given back when it ends, so a reader made while another is alive still finds some; a formula that needs more than 50,000 is given up on (read as saved, and not tried again by that reader), and a reader that gives up on four stops working cells out; the evaluator's memory is capped (about 160,000 cells), and one that fills it is let go of and made again, and a reader keeps 400,000 answers at the most (past them the rest is read as saved); **cells past the steps read as saved, nothing fails and nothing hangs** (counted tests, with a timed twin that is ignored). A print draws its sheets with one cache of what they work out for the document (`print::pdf`), so a page of twenty sheets works each cell out once and spends the document's steps in all; an export of a page, a PNG, an SVG or a PDF, and the thumbnail an `.odg` save makes, draw one frame, whose 32,000,000 steps are their whole budget. **The readers of what is not a place or a size read it so too**: shape data (every cell of a row: label, type, value, format, prompt, the two flags, the language), the picture a field shows (the row's `Format`), hyperlinks (address, description and the three flags), the cells of a container (its type, style and role), a stencil's master (the size and kind its listing shows, the size and the pin a drop is made from and the page scales that decide whether a drop is scaled), the rows of a connector's route (`X` and `Y`, so a route a file leaves the values out of is a route to edit), a layer's colour (`RGB(255,0,0)` is that colour, and a number an index of the table) and a shape's `LayerMember` list (the page's walk of lists, the lock test of a command and the write of a list), a geometry row's constructor text (`PolylineTo`'s `A` and `NURBSTo`'s `E`: the text the formula gives), a selection by role, a shape operation's container test, the accessibility check's hyperlinks and the connection points of an outline's edges. **A reader keeps at most 64 KiB of one answer's text and 16 MiB of text in all** (a text past the first is no answer and is read by the rule above; past the second the reader works no more cells out), with counted tests for a page of 30,000 shapes, a page that runs the steps out, a cycle of cells and a text too long to keep. **Not yet read this way** (listed in `docs/gaps.md`, F4): `Locks::of` and the callers of `shape_layers` that have no address of the shape (the lock test of Find and Replace, the layers dialog, routing's obstacles), the window's page settings for its grid and rulers, Find's search of computed text and the theme's lock test.

**What it costs** (`tests/it/theme_cost.rs`, `theme_file.rs`: counted, not timed, as `diacraft_calc::work` and `diacraft_vsdx::work` count; the page of 500 shapes and 300 connectors). The first `theme.apply` on the 800 shapes (2,400 links) is **one commit of 204,347 steps, the steps of the recalculation of the whole page as it was**: a theme works the page out once and no more;
the same theme again works out nothing; another theme, `theme.variant` and "no theme" are one commit each. A page of 10,000 shapes that each hold five scheme cells and a lock is one commit of 520,000 steps, and the locks are looked up through **one resolver for the page** (a unit test counts the resolvers made). A drawing with 255 themes costs an apply and a variant two commits and the list none; a hostile part of 200 sixteen-modifier fills, a variant and a removal 2 commits of 91 steps. The writer pairs themes by hashing: each theme's bytes at most twice, whatever the parts share (counted).
What the fixture lacks: it holds no groups, no master whose shapes hold theme formulas and no number cached under one, so the recalculation writes nothing; a foreign page writes what its theme cells' readers now give. A page of more than `MAX_THEMED_SHAPES` (200,000) shapes to change is refused whole.

**For the window (the Design tab's Themes and Variants galleries).** Themes: one item for each theme of `theme.list` (its `colours` give the thumbnail: the accents on the dark and light colours, the `fonts` the sample text), preceded by "No Theme" (`theme.apply {theme: "none"}`); the current one is `page.theme`, which the gallery marks (`custom` for a theme the file brought, which no item
marks). The gallery's menu chooses the page or every page: `scope` `page` or `all`. Variants: the four of the current theme, `variants[i].colours` the thumbnail and `name` the tooltip, sending `theme.variant {variant: i}`; the current one is `page.colors` (with `page.styles`: `colors` and `styles` can differ after a `colors` or `styles` call, and then no variant is marked). A theme applied is shown at once, the renderer asking the theme each time it draws.
Not here, and not hidden by a control that would send them (Quick Styles are `shape.quick_style`): swapping the colours, effects, connectors or fonts of a theme for another's (P1 and P2), "Remove Theme" from chosen shapes (P1), a paste or a duplicate (it keeps the links its source had) and an option to turn "Apply theme to new shapes" off (P1), "Stop a theme reaching a shape" as a control (the locks are read, not set), the theme's background colour (P2), and custom themes (P2).

## Transparency, patterns, gradients, shadows and Quick Styles

The fill's and line's transparency, the pattern fill, the cap and compound type of a line, the gradient of a fill or a line, the shadow, and the Quick Styles of the Home tab's
Shape Styles group. The renderer drew all of these from the cells before; these commands
and the Format Shape pane write them. Code: `crates/engine/src/formatting/` (`shape_cells.rs`, `effects.rs`, `quick.rs`), `cmd/effects.rs`, and in the window `format_fx.rs`, `panes/format_fx.rs`
and `ribbon/quick_styles.rs`. The reference app was never taken apart: every rule below is **ours** where it says so, and is listed in the report of the
task for the check list.

| Command | Parameters | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `shape.format` (more parameters) | `fill_transparency`, `line_transparency` (percent, 0 to 100), `fill_pattern` (1 solid, 2 to 24 hatches and stipples), `fill_background` (`#RRGGBB`), `line_cap` (`round`, `flat`, `square`), `compound` (`single`, `double`, `thick_thin`, `thin_thick`, `triple`) | `{page, formatted}`, as before |
| `shape.gradient` | `ids`, `page`?, `target`? (`fill`, the default, or `line`), `on`?, `kind`? (`linear`, `radial`, `rectangular`, `path`) with `origin`?, or `direction`? (0 to 13), `angle`? (degrees), `rotate_with_shape`?, `stops`? (2 to 10 of `{position, color, transparency?}`) | `{page, target, formatted}` |
| `shape.shadow` | `ids`, `page`?, `on`?, `preset`? (`none`, `bottom_right`, `bottom`, `bottom_left`, `right`, `center`, `left`, `top_right`, `top`, `top_left`), `color`?, `transparency`?, `size`?, `blur`?, `angle`?, `distance`? | `{page, formatted}` |
| `shape.quick_style` | `ids`, `page`?, `row` (1 to 6) with `column` (1 to 7), or `variant` (0 to 3) | `{page, formatted, matrix, colour}` |
| `shape.quick_styles` (query) | `ids`, `page`? | `{page, current: {matrix, colour}, variants: [tile], styles: [tile]}`: the gallery for the first shape, each `tile` `{variant | row and column, matrix, colour, fill, line, weight, fill_transparency, gradient, shadow}` as the shape looks in that style |

Each is one undo step, and a call that would change nothing is none and does not make the drawing unsaved. `shape.formatting` also answers, for each shape, `fill_pattern`, `fill_transparency`,
`fill_background` (`null` unless the fill is a hatch or stipple), `line_transparency`, `line_cap`, `compound`, `gradient` and `line_gradient` (`null` or `{direction, kind, origin, angle, rotate_with_shape,
stops: [{position, color, transparency}]}`) and `shadow` (`null` or `{color, transparency, size, blur, angle, distance, kind}`).

* A transparency is a share on the half-percent steps files hold (a writer rounds to the nearest 0.005): 35.3 percent is 0.355. It writes `FillForegndTrans` and `LineColorTrans`; beside a
  hatch or stipple also `FillBkgndTrans` (the ground has its own); and with a gradient on, **the `GradientStopColorTrans` of every stop** of the section the gradient is in ("for one transparency over the whole shape,
  set the same number on every stop"), which is what the pane's slider does when it shows a transparency for a gradient's stop. A refusal names the key and "from 0 to 100 percent".
* Our rule. `fill_pattern` writes `FillPattern` and, where the shape had a gradient on, turns it off (`FillGradientEnabled` 0, its rows stay), because a pattern does not paint under a gradient.
  The gradients 25 to 40 of the old way are `shape.gradient`'s, and refused here in words. `fill_background` is the colour between the marks (`FillBkgnd`); the colour of the marks is `fill`.
* `line_cap` is what files draw: `round` 0, `flat` 1 (the number MS-VSDX names square draws a flat end) and `square` 2 (the number it names extended draws the projecting square).
* Our rule. A gradient turned on makes the shape paint a fill (or a line) at all: `FillPattern` 0 becomes 1, and `LinePattern` 0 becomes 1, because a pattern 0 paints nothing whatever else is set. **A member reached through a group that draws none keeps none**, and a fill gradient leaves a member filled with its own line colour.
  Our rule: turned on with no stops it keeps the ones the shape has, or, when it has none, is made of two, the colour the shape has now and a lighter one (white, or a grey for a colour that is nearly white).
  Any gradient setting turns it on unless `on` is false, which writes 0 where it was on and leaves the rows. A shape the gradient is not on is left as it is by `on: false`.
* The stops are written **in position order from `IX` 0** as `GradientStopColor`, `GradientStopColorTrans` and `GradientStopPosition`; a row of the style or the master that the new list does not
  reach is **deleted here** (`Del`: a shape that follows the `Theme` style, which holds ten rows, keeps no stop it was not given), and a row the shape had deleted is brought back when a list needs it. Two to ten stops:
  a refusal says "from 2 to 10 stops". The layout is `kind` with `origin`, which `FillGradientDir`'s table gives, or `direction` itself; `angle` is degrees clockwise from the right as seen on the page, written
  in radians; `rotate_with_shape` is a fill's `RotateGradientWithShape`. `target: line` is the same for `LineGradientEnabled`, `LineGradientDir`, `LineGradientAngle` and the rows of `LineGradient`.
* The controls read a gradient section (the shape's, its master's and its styles' rows together) **only when it has at most 256 rows**, counted before any row is merged (`Resolver::effective_rows_within`: a file may hold a hundred thousand rows of stops, counts ten), and read a longer one as a section with no stops, so a gradient fill of such a shape shows the two fill colours; the picture draws its first ten rows. A command that writes a gradient writes the stops it is given from `IX` 0 and deletes at most the rows 3 to 9 the shape or its style holds. A Quick Style on 4,096 shapes that follow the `Theme` style and a gradient and a shadow on 4,096 shapes are each one pass and **one commit** (`formatfx_cost.rs`: counted, not timed), and one that would change nothing commits nothing.
* Our rule (leaves the sense open). The pane's Distance (points) and Angle (degrees) are the shadow's offset in polar form: the angle is **clockwise from the right as seen
  on the page**, so 90 is straight down. A theme's own `ShadowDirection` is DrawingML's bearing, clockwise from the right, and `ShapeShdwOffsetX` agrees with the distance times its cosine and `ShapeShdwOffsetY` with
  the negated distance times its sine, so what a theme gives and what the pane shows agree. The offset is paper inches along the page's axes with y up; the blur is paper inches.
* Our rule. Any shadow setting turns the shadow on, unless `on` is false (`ShdwPattern` 0; the other cells stay). A shadow that is off is made whole
  from the starting one (ours: black, 60 percent clear, the size of the shape, blurred 4 points, 4 points away at 45 degrees) with what is given; one that is on has **only what is given written**, so a
  shadow that follows its theme keeps following it for the rest. A shadow of the page's default (`ShapeShdwType` 0) is given the shape's own type 1 with its offsets and size as it shows them. (ours;   the galleries' contents are `named` only):
  the ten presets are `none` and the starting shadow in each of the eight directions and `center` (no distance, blurred 8 points).
* Our rule. A Quick Style is **two numbers**: an entry of the theme's lists, `QuickStyleLineMatrix`, `QuickStyleFillMatrix` and `QuickStyleEffectsMatrix`, and a colour,
  `QuickStyleLineColor`, `QuickStyleFillColor` and `QuickStyleShadowColor`. The gallery is the reference's two grids: four **Variant Styles**, entry 100 to 103 (the first to fourth of the page's style variant) in colour 100, and
  the **Theme Styles**, six rows of seven, row `r` column `c` being entry `r` in colour `99 + c` (the seven colours of the page's colour variant). The font cells are not written.
* Our rule. A shape without members, inside the shapes named, follows the page's `Theme` style for a family that has no style of its own or the root style, as `theme.apply` makes it (an instance through its master's shape); the six cells
  are written; and every cell of the line, fill and shadow families (and the ten stop rows of the fill gradient, and the scheme cells that send a shape to its page, 65534) **that does not read the theme's marker is written as
  the call `THEMEVAL()` with the marker as its value**, as the shapes of files the reference application saved hold them: **choosing a style replaces the colour a person set**, and a shape with a style of its own takes its fill
  from the theme. A shape that follows the `Theme` style has nothing but the six cells written. A page with no theme, or a drawing with no `Theme` style, is a failure in words ("apply a theme first (Design, Themes)").
  At most 4,096 shapes (the shapes inside the groups named counted): past it the command is refused in words and changes nothing. A connector's list holds three entries, so a row past 3 reads the no-theme table.
  **A member reached through a group keeps the line or fill it does not draw** (its `LinePattern` or `FillPattern` cell is not written as `THEMEVAL()`), and one filled with its own line colour keeps its fill cells.
* `shape.quick_styles` gives each tile what the first shape selected **looks like in a copy of the document** with that style put on it (the same planning as `shape.quick_style`, no recalculation: a cell
  that holds the marker is asked of the theme as it is read), so a tile shows what a press makes, and the drawing is not changed (a test compares the session before and after). It is 46 copies of a document, which is a handful of
  pointers each, and 46 readings of one shape.
* Our rule. **What is not painted is not shown** by `shape.formatting`: a shape that paints no fill reads no fill transparency, ground or gradient, one that draws no line no line transparency, cap, compound type or
  gradient, and one that paints neither no shadow. So the look of a text box does not change in a theme variant for what the picture does not draw. A fill of the old way, `FillPattern` 25 to 40, reads as the gradient it
  stands for.
* **Files.** The cells ride in VSDX and `.diacraft` as they are. In an `.odg` the opacity of a fill and a line is `draw:opacity` and `svg:stroke-opacity`, a solid fill and a stroke are native, and **what the ODF styles do not hold
  natively here is carried in DiaCraft's namespaced extension and named in the save note** (`tests/it/formatfx_files.rs` saves each of the effects in the three formats and reads them back as they were).
* (with Q3 answered by measure). **An `.odg` says a gradient, a hatch, a stipple and a shadow in ODF's own markup**, for a new drawing and a new shape of a file (the
  model writer and the splice) and for a gradient or a shadow set on a shape of a file, and the cells ride in DiaCraft's data beside it, so the drawing reads back as it was (`crates/engine/tests/it/odg_fx.rs`: each of the 14 layouts,
  the 24 patterns and three shadows, from a new drawing and into a file; `crates/odg/tests/it/fx_native.rs`, and a property test over random looks). **A gradient** is a `draw:gradient` of DiaCraft's own in `office:styles`,
  named by its layout, its angle and its stops (`DiaCraft_20_gradient_20_...`), so the element is made from the name: `draw:angle` is 90 degrees less the cell's angle (LibreOffice 26.8.2.2 turns it counterclockwise from a
  start at the top, and reads a number with no unit as degrees), the colours of a radial or rectangular gradient run from the outer edge in (the last stop is `draw:start-color`), the stops beyond two or not at 0 and 1 are
  `loext:gradient-stop` children (the one form LibreOffice reads: it reads no `svg:linearGradient`), the path layout (13) is written as the rectangular one from the centre, and a layout from a corner or the middle of an edge has
  its stops at twice or 1.58 times their places, since LibreOffice ends such a gradient at half the distance to the far corner. **A hatch** (patterns 2 to 7, 13 to 16 and 19 to 23) is a `draw:hatch` named by the pattern and the
  colour of its marks, over the ground of `draw:fill-color` (`draw:rotation` and `draw:distance` follow the lines the renderer draws; LibreOffice draws every hatch line hairline thin, so the heavy bars of 13 to 16 are lighter
  there); **a stipple** (8 to 12, 17, 18 and 24), which the renderer draws as one flat mixture of its two colours, is that colour. **A shadow** is `draw:shadow`, its colour, `draw:shadow-opacity` (the complement of the share),
  its offsets (y runs down in the file and up in the cell) and `loext:shadow-blur` of four thirds of the cell's blur (DiaCraft's deviation is the blur over 1.5 and LibreOffice's about half its blur). **What ODF has no form
  for stays in the data:** a stop's transparency, a shadow's size and any type but 1, `RotateGradientWithShape`, a line's gradient, the exact angle, a cap and a compound line. **Another program's gradients, hatches and shadows
  stay as they are.** A hatch or a stipple set on a shape of a file is not written as a display form (the shape's fill stays the marks' colour) until the file is saved from the model.
* **For the window.** The Format Shape pane's Fill has **No fill, Solid fill, Gradient fill and Pattern fill**, and under the kind the shapes have: the colour and a transparency (a number box in percent over a slider); for a
  gradient the layout, the angle or the place it starts from, a bar with a handle for each stop, Add stop, Remove stop, and the colour, position and transparency of the stop selected, and Rotate with shape; for a pattern the grid of
  the 23 patterns (our own artwork: lines, grids and dots), the colour of the marks, the colour between them and the transparency. **Line** has No line, Solid line and Gradient line, the colour, transparency, width, compound type, dash
  type, cap type, rounding and ends. **Effects** has the Shadow group: Presets, Color, Transparency, Size, Blur, Angle and Distance, quiet while the shapes have no shadow; Reflection, Glow, Soft Edges, Bevel and 3-D Rotation stay
  quiet. The window's commands are `format.gradient` (also the edits of one stop: `stop`, `stop_color`, `line_stop_color`, `stop_position`, `stop_transparency`, `add_stop`, `remove_stop`, which send the whole list of stops),
  `format.shadow` (also `shadow_color`) and `format.quickStyle`, each the engine's command with the shapes selected on the page on view. Our rule: **a slider that is dragged shows its value on the page as it
  goes and is one undo step**: each frame of the drag takes back the step the last frame made and makes it again with the new value, while the drawing is as the last frame left it. Home's Quick Styles opens the two grids (the
  tile the first shape has is marked; no live preview: it would be an edit); Fill has Gradient, Pattern and Transparency submenus and Line a Transparency one, and Effects, Shadow has the ten presets and Shadow Options... (the
  Effects tab). **The Format Painter carries the transparency, the pattern, the cap, the compound type, the gradients and the shadow**, and a source with no shadow takes the shadow away from the shape painted, in the same undo step.

## Templates

Starting a drawing from a template, the stencils the template opens, and the list File > New shows. **In the window** (`new_page.rs`) File > New has the headings Personal, Templates and Sample Diagrams: Templates holds the Blank drawing tile and a tile for each template of `template.list`, each showing its name and its category over a picture the window draws from the template's `page` and `theme` (a sheet of the page's proportions with a plain picture of its category, in the first accents of its theme), and its description is the tooltip; a press asks about unsaved changes as Ctrl+N does (`save::Then::Template`) and runs `file.new {template: id}`; Sample Diagrams says there are none (the engine has no samples) and Personal is quiet (the window has no folder of the person's own templates); there is no detail dialog and no Metric or US choice at the start. The rows are (Start a drawing from a template, Template opens its stencils,
Basic Flowchart template, Basic Diagram template: P0; Template sets page scale, size and orientation, Browse templates by category, Save a drawing as a custom template, Start a drawing from a custom template: P1). The format is
a `.vstx` is a drawing under the template content type; the file holds no flag saying it opens as a new document, so the command layer decides and (the
windows part). Code: `crates/engine/src/template/` (`catalogue.rs`, the eighteen registered templates and the ones listed; `build.rs`, a template made into a document and the bytes of a `.vstx`; `names.rs`, the list in DiaCraft's part that names a template's stencils),
`cmd/template.rs` and `cmd/file.rs`. The reference app was never taken apart: every rule below is **ours**. **The templates are originals** (`docs/provenance.md`): four descriptions in code, no file
from another application, nothing traced.

| Command | Parameters | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `template.list` (query) | none; works with no document | `{templates: [{id, name, category, description, page: {size, size_name, orientation, width, height}, theme: {id, name, variant} or null, stencils: [{id, name}]}], categories}`: the templates in the order File > New lists them (`basic_diagram`, `basic_flowchart`, `cross_functional_flowchart`: its page holds three lanes and three phases, and `organization_chart`: its page holds an Executive, and `gane_sarson`; the templates of the second stencil batch follow as their stencils ship), the page each starts (inches), the theme it applies, and the built-in stencils it opens, first shown first. There is no thumbnail: a template's page is empty or holds only what it seeds, and the window draws its card from `page`, `theme` and `stencils` |
| `file.new` | `template`? (an id of `template.list`, in any case, or the name, or the **path** of a template file, `.diacraft-template`, `.vstx` or `.vstm`) | the new document as `document.inspect`; with a template also `template` (`{id, name, builtin: true}`, or `{id: null, name: null, builtin: false}` for a file), `stencils: {open: [ids], ignored}` (the built-in stencils now open, and how many names in the template were not opened), `warnings`, and for a file `file: {variant, kind, bytes, warning_count, skipped_count}`. A blank drawing when `template` is left out, answered as it always was, with the stencils open by default open |
| `file.open` | (as before) | of a template file: the same drawing and the same stencils as `file.new {template: path}` (`stencils: {open, ignored}` is in the answer, for a template only); with `edit_template: true` the file itself, with the stencils it names open. A file that is not a template has every built-in stencil open |

* A built-in template is held in code and written on demand; ours. A template is a `TemplateSpec`: a page size (an id of `page.presets`), an orientation, a theme of the catalogue with its variant (or none), and
  the built-in stencils it opens. `template::build` makes a new drawing (the root style and one page, "Page-1"), gives the page its size and turn by the page setup rules, applies the theme by the theme rules (so the theme's
  part, the `Theme` style and the page's selector cells are in it), writes the list that names its stencils (into DiaCraft's part), and has the one writer (`diacraft_vsdx::write_with`) make the **`.vstx` bytes**, with no times, so the same bytes
  each time. **A built-in template is then read from those bytes by the reader, as a template file is**: there is no second path, and what a test of the built-in templates shows is what any template file does. They are not
  files shipped with the app because the web build has no folder to read them from, and an asset file would need a provenance row and a place to be found. Basic Diagram: Letter, landscape, no theme, the Basic Shapes and Arrow Shapes stencils.
  Basic Flowchart: Letter, portrait, the theme Fernwood, the Basic Flowchart stencil and then the Basic Shapes. Cross-Functional Flowchart: Letter, landscape, no theme, the Cross-Functional Flowchart Shapes, the Basic Flowchart and the Basic Shapes, and three lanes and three phases on its page, and its page has Auto Size on. Organization Chart: Letter, landscape, no theme, the Organization Chart Shapes and then the Basic Shapes, and an Executive on its page. Data Flow Model (Gane-Sarson): Letter, landscape, no theme, the Gane-Sarson shapes and then the Basic Shapes, a blank page. All five are drawn one to one. Each costs the same whatever drawing it replaces (see "What it costs").
* A template starts a new unsaved drawing; the rule for `file.open`. The document is the template's content, with its page setup, styles and theme; the session keeps **no file's bytes and no
  path** (NP10: the model holds every part of the template), so `file.save` says to use `file.save_as` and the first save is `.diacraft` or, as a VSDX type, written from the model; the drawing is **clean until it is edited**, has no undo step, and is untitled. A template that
  cannot be started (a name that is not a template and is not a path, a drawing or a stencil in its place, a file that cannot be read, one past a limit of the reader) is refused in words and **leaves the open drawing, its
  history and the stencils as they were**. `template` is judged as an id first (in any case, with spaces and hyphens as underscores, or the template's name), and anything else is a path (a word with no `/`, `\` or `.` in it is
  told it is no template, and is not read as a file; `template::is_path` is that rule, and the engine and the window both use it). A path is read as `file.open` reads one (the one reading path, A2 and A5 of the gaps). **`file.new` and `file.open` inside a batch are refused before any work** (each checks first: no template is made and no file is read; a test counts the commits, steps and resolvers and finds none, and the file that would have said something of its own is not looked at). **The window reads a template file on a thread**, as it reads a file to open: `engine.execute file.new {template: path}` on the control channel is answered when the reading ends (`docs/control-protocol.md`), and the window's `new_from_template_file` does the same for a control of its own; a template that is an id is made at once.
* How a template names the stencils it opens; ours; moved into DiaCraft's part. The specs give the format one record of open stencils, the stencil windows of the windows part, whose
