A chart of 100,000 positions, a manager with 3,000 reports (counted: the page is walked a handful of times and no shape is found by a search from its top), a chain 9,000 deep (no recursion) and a ring of positions each managing the next are each laid out or refused in words (`draw/relayout/org_hostile.rs`; `crates/layout/tests/it/org.rs` for the layout itself, a chain of 100,000 and a manager with 10,000 reports). **The window asks `orgchart.info` once for each revision of the drawing, page and selection.**
* **What the window does** (`crates/ui-egui/src/org_ui.rs`). The **Org Chart tab** shows after View (and Developer) and before Help while the drawing holds a position, and goes, with the ribbon back on its first tab, when it does not. **Layout** is a menu of the six layouts (the one the page holds is marked); **Re-Layout** lays the chart out again; **Arrange Subordinates** is a menu of the four arrangements for the position selected (its own is marked); **Insert Picture, Picture...** shows the file chooser Insert, Pictures uses and puts the file on the position selected; **Change Picture** does the same; **Delete Picture** and **Hide Picture** (a check box that shows the state) work on it. They send `window.orgChartDo {op, value?, path?}`, which adds the page on view and the position selected (`select a position of the org chart first` when none is, `select one position` when several are) and sends the engine's command. A position dropped from the Shapes window onto its manager is `shape.drop` at the pointer, and the chart reflows in the drop's step. **The tab's other controls are not built** (below).
* **Files.** The positions, the data, the marker, the links (the glue), the page's `PlaceStyle` and a manager's `ShapePlaceStyle` are cells and rows, and the picture is `ForeignData` of the shape, so **`.diacraft`** and **VSDX** (the model writer, and a save into the file) hold them and read them back, and the check after a save names no class (`crates/engine/tests/it/orgchart_files.rs`). **An `.odg`** holds the positions, their data (in DiaCraft's own data), their text (the two fields are written as the text they show, and a save into a file says so in a warning), the layout cells and the links, from the model writer and by Save As from a `.diacraft` file; the check names only what any connector between two shapes loses in an `.odg` (its formulas, its route and the formatting of its label, a class for each connector, the same for plain rectangles). **Two things an `.odg` does not hold, said in words and never dropped silently:** a position **with a picture** is not written (an `.odg` has no place for the text of a picture frame: "saving does not yet write this change: a text on a picture or an object frame ... Nothing was written ... save it as .diacraft, or as a VSDX type"; delete the picture, or save as `.diacraft` or VSDX), and a save **into** an opened `.odg` after a layout (which glues the connectors again) is refused with "a connector glued or glued anew (a connection is written by a later task)", which Save As `.diacraft` gets round.
* **What is left.** From the tab: Fit to Page, Synchronize and its copies, Move Further and Closer, Move, Move Left and Right, Show/Hide Subordinates, Change Style, the height and width of the shapes, Position Type, the data display options and Organization Data (Import, Export, Compare) are named controls and do nothing (P2 rows, except the wizard). **The Organization Chart Wizard from a data file** (a P1 row) is not built. It would take: a dialog that asks for a delimited text file (comma or tab) or an Excel workbook, a reader for them, a choice of the columns that hold Name, a unique ID and Reports To (and the others to show), a pass that makes a position for each row with its Shape Data, a link for each Reports To (a blank one is the top, `orgchart.link` for the rest), one `orgchart.layout`, and the sample file; the engine has the rest (the whole table would be one undo step, bounded as the layout is: 20,000 positions). Team frames and dotted-line reports (a Team Frame is a container), pictures from a folder, a chart over several pages and the fields shown on the shapes are not built. A position cannot be dragged onto a manager from the page (`orgchart.link` does it), the gallery has no pictures of the layouts (a menu of six rows), the right-click menu has no Arrange Subordinates row, and the placement is DiaCraft's own.

## The ShapeSheet (SHEETWIN)

Developer, Shape Design, **Show ShapeSheet** and the ShapeSheet window. The design is the ShapeSheet window's; this section is what is built, and built the **queries**: a program reads a sheet with the commands below, and the
window reads the same sheet through the same module (`diacraft_engine::sheetview`, which the window calls on the session's document, while the queries are JSON over its functions: a JSON answer
for each scroll of a section of 31,273 rows would be waste). Built the **writes of a cell**, `sheet.set_cell` and `sheet.set_cells`, the **rows and sections**, `sheet.add_row`, `sheet.delete_row`, `sheet.add_section` and `sheet.delete_section`, and the window's editing that sends the writes of a cell. The reference app was
never taken apart: a rule marked **ours** is DiaCraft's own and a row in the check list.

| Command | Parameters | Answer and effect |
|---|---|---|
| `sheet.read` (query) | the sheet, `sections`?, `from`?, `count`?, `all`? | `{sheet, name, sections, lines_total, from, lines, more}`: the sections the sheet shows, in the window's order, and `count` of its lines from line `from`. `sheet` names the sheet back (`{kind, page, master, style, id}`, the keys that apply), `name` is its title (`Process.4, Page-1`, `Page-1`, `Document`, `Heading (style)`, `Box (master)`); a section is `{section, label, ix, kind ("cells" or "rows"), first_line, lines, rows, columns, can_add_rows, can_delete}` (and `unlisted` when rows are not listed), a line `{line, section, kind, row, cells}` (`kind` is `header`, `cell`, `titles`, `row` or `note`; a row `{key, label, type, origin}`) and a cell `{ref, name, col, formula, value, unit, shown, error, origin, from, guarded, parsed, worked_out, truncated}`. `count` is from 1 to 2000 (default 200), `from` a whole number, `sections` at most 256 names, `all` the groups the rules leave out. Nothing is written, worked out or journaled |
| `sheet.cell` (query) | the sheet, `cell` | one cell whole, the answer of a read's cell with no text cut and `{sheet, kind, class, listed, default, chain}`: what the cell holds (`scalar`, `length`, `angle`, `days`, `color`, `text`, `font`, `point`), which sheets it is looked for on (`class`: `shape-only`, `style-any`, `fill-family`, `line-family`, `text-family`, `page-sheet`, `style-flag`, `style-local`, `unlisted`), whether the catalogue lists it, what it reads where it is found nowhere (`default: {value, shown, formula}`) and `chain`, the sheets it is looked for on, nearest first, each `{source ("local", "master" or "style"), id, name, family, holds}` |
| `sheet.sections` (query) | the sheet | `{sheet, name, present, can_add, can_delete}`: what Insert Section and Delete Section offer. `present` is each section the sheet shows `{section, label, ix, kind}`; `can_add` each section that can be inserted on this kind of sheet and that the sheet has not `{section, label, variant}` (a Geometry section can be added again, as `Ellipse` and `InfiniteLine` too: `variant`); `can_delete` each section that can go `{section, label, ix}`, Shape Transform never |
| `sheet.evaluate` (query) | the sheet, `formula`, `cell`? | `{sheet, value, unit, shown, error, parse_error, budget_exhausted, worked_out, steps}`: a text worked out on the sheet **as the formula of the cell would be**, with nothing written (the revision, the history and the journal are as they were). The text is cut as a write cuts it (white space at its ends and one leading `=`), at most 65536 bytes; a bare number takes the unit `cell` holds; a parse error is `{kind, offset, words}` with the byte `offset` in the text as given (`unexpected_end` for `1+`, `expected_operand` for `1+*2`), an error the formula works out to is `error` (`#DIV/0!`), and the work is held to 200000 steps of the evaluator (`budget_exhausted`) |
| `sheet.set_cell` | the sheet, `cell`, `formula`, `force`? | `{sheet, cell, changed, formula, value, unit, shown, error, origin, worked_out, recalculated}`: writes the cell as the formula bar does, **one undo step** (`Edit formula`, or `Clear formula` for an empty text) **and none when the cell already holds the text** (`changed: false`), the cell as `sheet.cell` gives it after the write, and `recalculated: {cells, listed, more}`, the cells that changed besides this one (`listed` at most 256, each `{sheet, cell}`, `more` when there are others), and, when the recalculation dropped `SETF` calls past the caps, `setf_dropped` and a note. The text is the formula as the window's bar takes it (below); a refusal is in words and changes nothing |
| `sheet.set_cells` | `writes`, the sheet params? | `{written, unchanged, results, recalculated}`: **at most 4,096 writes** `{cell, formula, force?}` in **one undo step** (`Edit formulas`), **all or nothing**, one recalculation of each page touched, at the end. A write names its own sheet by any of `id`, `page`, `master`, `style` or `document` (all of its sheet, none of the call's), else takes the call's; `written` counts the writes that changed a cell, `unchanged` those that left it as it was, `results` is the first 256 writes' answers (each as above, with no `recalculated`). A refused write refuses the call and is named in the words (`write 2: the cell Height is guarded by GUARD(): send force: true to replace it`) |
| `sheet.add_row` | the sheet, `section`, `after`? or `before`?, `name`?, `type`? | `{sheet, section, label, row, type, cells, renumbered, note}`: adds one row to a section the sheet has, **one undo step** (`Insert row`). `section` is as `sheet.read` names it (`Geometry1`, `Scratch`, `User`, `Prop`, `Connections`, `Controls`, `Hyperlink`, `Actions`, `SmartTags`, `FillGradientStops`, `LineGradientStops`) or by its label (`Shape Data`, `Connection Points`), in any letter case; `after` and `before` (not both) name a row by its name, read as a formula reads it (below), or by its number as a reference spells it, and the row goes at the end with neither; `name` names a row of a named section and `type` a Geometry row's one of fifteen (`LineTo` by default). `row` is the new row's number or name and `label` how a reference spells it (`3`, `Prop.Row_2`), `cells` the cells the row holds as `sheet.read` gives them, `note` says a gradient's row past the tenth stop is ignored, and `renumbered {rows, sections, formulas, connects, copied: {rows, cells}, work}` is what an insert in the middle numbered again and the rows an instance took as its own first (and the copy below) |
| `sheet.delete_row` | the sheet, `section`, `row` | `{sheet, section, label, row, how, renumbered}`: deletes one row, **one undo step** (`Delete row`); `row` is the row's name, read as a formula reads it (below), or its number as a reference spells it. `how` is `removed` (a row the sheet holds and no master or style gives, taken out, with the numbers after it closed up where the section is the sheet's own) or `marked` (a row a master or a style gives, dropped by a local `Del` row) |
| `sheet.add_section` | the sheet, `section`, `variant`? | `{sheet, section, label, ix, rows, cells, renumbered}`: adds a section, **one undo step** (`Insert section`): `section` is one `sheet.sections` lists in `can_add`; `Geometry` takes the next number and holds a `MoveTo` and a `LineTo`, or with `variant` `Ellipse` or `InfiniteLine` that one row. `rows` are the keys of the rows the section holds, `cells` the cells of Text Transform or Layer Membership |
| `sheet.delete_section` | the sheet, `section` | `{sheet, section, label, ix, how, removed_cells, renumbered}`: deletes a section, **one undo step** (`Delete section`), one `sheet.sections` lists in `can_delete`: Shape Transform never |

**The sheet** is named by the params every `sheet.*` command takes: `id` (with `page`: that page, else the first page that holds it, a group's member too), `page` alone (the page's sheet), `master` and `id` (the master's shape), `master` alone (its page sheet), `style` or `document: true`. Any other mix is refused in the words **give one sheet: id (with page), page, master (with id), style or document**, and a sheet that is not there in words that name it (`the drawing has no page 7`, `page 1 has no shape 99`, `master 2 has no shape 99`); a shape marked deleted (`Del`) is not there.

**The cell** is named by **the reference a formula uses for it, with no sheet before it**: `Width`, `Geometry1.X2`, `Geometry1.NoFill`, `Scratch.A1`, `Prop.Cost`, `Prop.Cost.Label`, `User.Total.Prompt`, by the formula parser and `diacraft_calc::cell_address`. A leading `=`, a sheet in the reference (`Sheet.4!Width`) and a text that is no one reference are refused in words. **A row's name matches without regard to letter case** (below): `Prop.COST` is the row `Cost`, which `cell_address` cannot know, having no document, and the command spells (`diacraft_engine::sheetview::respell`). **So does the name of a cell directly under the sheet that the catalogue lists** (below): `WIDTH` and `width` are `Width`, which `cell_address` spells, the catalogue being no document's. `ref` in a read gives each cell's reference back, `null` where none can be spelled.

**The window** (`crates/ui-egui/src/sheet/`) **reads** a sheet through `diacraft_engine::sheetview` on the session's document and **writes a cell only through `sheet.set_cell`** ("Editing in the window" below) **and adds and deletes rows and sections only through `sheet.add_row`, `sheet.delete_row`, `sheet.add_section` and `sheet.delete_section`** ("Rows and sections in the window"): it holds its tabs, its folds, its selection and its editor itself. Its commands are the window's (listed by `engine.commands` beside the engine's, and reached by the control channel and the command line as the others are); a command that acts on an open sheet is refused with the words **no ShapeSheet is open** while none is.

| Window command | Parameters | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `window.shapesheet` | `of`?, `id`?, `page`?, `style`?, `master`? | Opens a sheet in a tab of the sheet area, or brings forward the tab that shows it (no two tabs show one sheet; at most 32, the 33rd taking the place of the one used least recently), and gives it the focus. `of` is `shape`, `page`, `document`, `style` or `master`; without it the sheet of the first shape selected, else of the page on view. The sheet is named as `sheet.*` names one (the engine's words, `page 1 has no shape 99`, `the drawing has no style 9`), a shape of no page with `id` alone being looked for on the page on view first. From the window: Developer, Shape Design, Show ShapeSheet (its big part, and Shape, Page and Document in its menu), the right-click menu of a shape and of the page while the Developer tab is on, and Drawing Explorer's drawing row, styles and masters (a master's first top-level shape) |
| `window.sheetTab`, `window.sheetClose` | `tab` | Brings a tab on top, or closes it (the tab on top when `tab` is left out): `tab` is a place from 0 or the title. The area goes with the last tab, and the bar with it |
| `window.sheetDock` | `at` | `below` (the default: 45% of the middle band, 160 points at least, the drawing keeping 120), `beside` (at the right of the drawing, shown below while the band is narrower than 640 points) or `fill` (the whole band, with a tab of the drawing at the left of the sheet tabs that goes back to the dock the area had before) |
| `window.sheetView` | `formulas`?, `values`? | The View group's two toggles: both on at first, and at least one stays on (`at least one of Formulas and Values stays on`) |
| `window.sheetSections` | `shown`? | Show Sections: the sections named are shown and the others hidden; without `shown` every section shows. The tab's own state, not saved |
| `window.sheetCollapse` | `section`, `open`? | Folds a section to its header or opens it; without `open` it turns the other way |
| `window.sheetSelect` | `cell`?, or `section`, `row`?, `cell`? | Selects a cell by its reference as `sheet.read` gives it (`Geometry1.X2`, `Prop.Cost.Value`) or by section, row and cell, or a whole row, and brings it on view: a hidden section is refused, a folded one is opened, and it is refused while an edit is open (`an edit is open: commit or cancel it first`) |
| `window.sheetEdit` | `text`?, `commit`?, `cancel`? | Drives the editor as a person would: `text` begins an edit on the selected cell or replaces the text of the one open, `commit` commits it (one `sheet.set_cell` with `force: true`, the selection stays), `cancel` gives it up; the answer's `sheet.last` says what the engine answered, and a refused text keeps the edit open with its fault marked in `sheet.edit.fault` |
| `window.sheetInsertRow` | `at`? | Inserts a row in the section of the selected cell or row with one `sheet.add_row`: `at` is `after` (the default, the Rows group's Insert) or `before` (the right-click menu's Insert Row) the selected row, and with a header, or a cell of a section's own, selected the row goes at the end. The new row is selected and the footer says what was numbered again. Refused in words where the window knows the engine would refuse (`select a cell or a row of a section of rows first`, the rows the text makes) and where the engine does (`add the row at the end`); the refusal is in the footer and in `sheet.last` too |
| `window.sheetDeleteRow` | none | Deletes the selected row, or the row of the selected cell, with one `sheet.delete_row`; the selection stays where the row was |
| `window.sheetInsertSection` | `sections`?, `close`? | Without `sections` opens the **Insert Section card**: a box for every section some sheet takes (the sections of rows, Text Transform, Layer Membership, Geometry and its Ellipse and Infinite Line kinds), in the window's order; what `sheet.sections` offers in `can_add` is on offer and the others are greyed (the sheet has it already, or it belongs to another kind of sheet). OK adds the ticked boxes with **one `command.batch` of `sheet.add_section`** (one undo step), and a refusal is said in the card, which stays. With `sections` (labels as `can_add` lists them: `Scratch`, `Shape Data`, `Geometry`, `Ellipse`, `Infinite Line`) it adds those with no card; `close: true` closes the card |
| `window.sheetDeleteSection` | none | Deletes the section of the selected cell with one `sheet.delete_section`; refused for Shape Transform and the sections the engine's rules keep (`Shape Transform cannot be inserted or deleted: a shape always has one`) |
| `window.sheetEditFormula` | `text`?, `commit`?, `close`? | The **Edit Formula card** (Ctrl+E): a text area of several lines on the selected cell's formula, OK and Cancel. It is **another place the one edit of the cell is held in**, as the bar is: `text` puts a text in it (and opens it), `commit` is OK (one `sheet.set_cell` with `force: true`; a refused text keeps the card open with the fault marked and the engine's words), `close` is Cancel (an edit the card began is given up; one it moved into goes back to the cell's editor with the text it had) |
| `window.sheetAddRow` | `section` | The Editing group's **Shape Data**, **Link** and **Shape Action**: a row at the end of the section `Prop`, `Hyperlink` or `Actions` of the sheet on top (one `sheet.add_row`), and the section is made first, with its one row, by `sheet.add_section` when the sheet has none. The control of Shape Action is greyed until a cell or a row of the Actions section is selected |

**The window state** (`ui.inspect`, and the answer of each of these commands) has a `sheet` key: `{open, focus, dock, shownDock, formulas, values, active, tabs: [{title, sheet, gone}], sections: [{name, label, open, shown}], lines, first, visible, selected, bar, painted, work, card, ops}` (`card` and `ops` are in "Rows and sections in the window"). `work` counts what the sheets have done since the window began (`outlines` made, `rows` those walks visited, `cells` resolved, `lines` read), which the tests hold a cost to; `painted` is what the last frame drew of each cell box (the ink of its formula and of its value by the name of its token, the dot, and the two texts), for the tests.

* Design 5.1 to 5.3. The area is docked with the drawing: a bottom panel (the drawing's page tabs stay directly under the drawing), a right panel left of the task panes, or the whole middle band in place of the drawing and its page tabs. **The formula bar** is a panel of its own under the ribbon body and over everything else, so that the whole window shifts once when the first sheet opens and once when the last closes; it holds the selected cell's reference name, the cancel and accept buttons before the text (greyed while no edit is open, and working while one is), the formula whole (a formula the reading cut at 4,096 characters is read whole with `sheet.cell`, once for each revision and selection) and its value. **The sheet has the focus** from a press in the area or the bar until a press in the drawing (a press in the ribbon, a menu or a popup changes nothing, as the ShapeSheet Design tab's own controls are in the ribbon); the tab shows while it does.
* **In the window**. With Formulas and Values on, a cell box shows the formula at the left and the value at the right; **the value is left out when it reads as the formula does, told by the number and not by the text** (`2.5 in` and `2.5000 in`, a text in its quotation marks, `TRUE`), and never for an error, a formula that did not parse or one the evaluator cannot work out. With one toggle on a box shows that one: the formula (a plain value with at most four decimals, the zeros cut) at the left, the value (four decimals, the zeros kept) at the right. A box is cut with an ellipsis and whole in its tooltip, which says where the cell comes from (**Own**, **From the master Process (ID 3)**, **From the style Normal**, **Default: not in the drawing**) and what an error means (`#DIV/0!`: Division by zero).
* **And the colours** (design 5.6, 5.7). A cell the sheet holds is drawn in `sheet_local` with a small dot at its left edge, so that the difference does not rest on colour; an inherited cell in the text colour, a cell found nowhere in `sheet_default`, an error value in `sheet_error`; `sheet_changed` is the background of a cell the last commit worked out again ("Editing in the window"). All four are checked at 4.5 to 1 on the sheet's ground in both themes.
* **Cost, as counts** (design 6, `work`): the outline is made **once for each drawing generation, revision and object** (a tab brought forward after an edit makes its own again, a tab behind makes none), by one walk that visits each row once and resolves no cell; Show Sections and a fold **arrange** the outline the tab holds and make no outline again; a scroll that brings k new lines on view resolves their cells and no others (the lines far from the view are let go past 800); **a frame in which nothing changed resolves no cell, reads no line and makes no outline**; there is no timer anywhere in the sheet, so that a window with a sheet open comes to rest. The list is painted by the lines on view with **its own scroll bar** (`sheet/scroll.rs`: the position is a line number and a part of a line in integers, so that a list of a million lines keeps its place), and a column is as wide as its widest box on view, from 56 to 240 points.
* The window's spec, built in `diacraft_doc::DISPLAY_ORDER` by and in `sheetview/show.rs`. One fixed order for every sheet: Document Properties, Style Properties and the page's Page Properties, Page Layout and Ruler & Grid first, then 1-D Endpoints, Shape Transform, the sections of rows (User-defined Cells, Shape Data, Hyperlinks, Connection Points, Actions, Controls, each Geometry section by `IX`, Scratch), Layers and Print Properties, Protection and the other groups, the 2013 groups and the two gradients' stops, then MasterSelectors and Reviewer; a section the table does not list follows by name, and **Other Cells** (the cells directly under the sheet that no group lists) last. **A shape** shows every group of a shape but 1-D Endpoints (only when its four end cells are there, own or inherited), Alignment and Text Transform (only when one of their cells is there, own or inherited), Group Properties (only on a group), Foreign Image Info (only on a foreign object) and Layer Membership (only when it holds the cell); Glue Info and Image Properties show on every shape. **A page** shows Page Properties, Page Layout and Print Properties (Ruler & Grid on a page's sheet and not a master's) and every group it holds a cell of; **the document**, Document Properties and what it holds; **a style**, Style Properties, Group Properties and what it holds. A section of rows shows when it holds a row not deleted, or a cell of its own. `all: true` shows the groups of the sheet's own kind that the rules leave out; a head of another kind (Page Properties on a shape) shows only when the sheet holds one of its cells, and a cell of a group the rules hide is shown in no section. A section asked for by `sections` that the rules hide is refused with the way to see it (`all: true`).
* Our rule. **A line is what the window paints**: a section is a **header** line, for Geometry its five own cells (`NoFill`, `NoLine`, `NoShow`, `NoSnap`, `NoQuickDrag`) as **cell** lines, a line of column **titles**, a **row** line for each row and, when the rows are not all listed, a **note** line; a group is a header and one **cell** line for each cell the catalogue lists for it (Shape Transform's Width, Height and Angle first). The lines of the sheet are numbered from 0 through its sections in order, and `from` and `count` page through them (`line_at`, a binary search of the sections' first lines). A section's `label` is what the window titles it (`Geometry 2`, `Line Gradient Stops`, `Fill Gradient Stops`) and its `section` what a reference spells (`Geometry2`, `Prop`, `User`, `Char`) or the label of a group. A row's `key` is its name or its number as a reference spells it, its `label` the Row column (`Prop.Cost`; the number for an indexed row). **A row's cells are the cells it holds**, own or inherited, in the order of the section's `columns`, `col` naming the column: the cells the catalogue lists for the section (a column of a section is named as a formula names the cell: `Verify`, `XDyn`, where the window's images title them Ask and X Dynamics: R12, a question for the window) and any other cell a row holds at the end.
* Design 6. The outline is **built with no cell resolved** (`Resolver::effective_row_keys`: each row of each sheet the section is looked for on, once), listing at most 1,000,000 lines: a section past that lists the rows that fit and a note (`108 more rows are not listed here`), and a section after the budget is spent lists none and says how many it holds (`unlisted`), counted without a merge. **Counted, not timed** (`Counts`, `diacraft_doc::work`): the outline of a Geometry of 31,273 rows merges 31,273 rows once and resolves no cell, deciding which groups show costs at most 18 cells looked up, and a window of 50 lines resolves their cells and no others.
* A cell's `value` is the cached `V` in the unit it shows in (`U`; with none, a length is in inches and an angle in degrees, the implicit unit of its kind: the drawing's own unit is not read yet), the number cleaned of the noise of a conversion (twelve digits). `shown` is the **Values view**: four decimals with the trailing zeros kept and the unit (`44.5000 mm`, `0.0000 deg`, `25.0000%`); a number with no unit that is whole shows whole (`1`, an index or a code: the catalogue does not tell an index from a real number that is whole, so a whole real shows `0`, and not `0.0000`); true-false `TRUE` or `FALSE`; text as it is; a colour `RGB(0, 0, 0)`; an error its value (`#DIV/0!`); a formula that did not parse `not read` (its text is kept as the file has it and `parsed` is false); a formula that calls a function the evaluator does not have the saved value and a `?` (`worked_out` is false). `formula` is the **Formulas view**: the text the file holds, `No Formula`, or for a value with no formula its literal with at most four decimals and the zeros dropped (`2.5 mm`, `0.6667`), a text in quotation marks. A cell found nowhere reads its kind's default, or the formula its catalogue entry gives (the seven cells of Text Transform, the two picture sizes), worked out on the sheet.
* **Where a cell comes from.** `origin` is `local` (the sheet holds the formula, or a value with no formula, or `No Formula`), `inherited` (a master or a style gives the formula: `F="Inh"` is inherited, whatever value the sheet caches) or `default`; `from` names the master (`{kind: "master", id, name, shape}`) or the style (`{kind: "style", id, name, family}`) an inherited cell comes from. `guarded` is `GUARD(...)`.
* **Budgets, as counts** (`sheetview`): a read gives at most 2,000 lines (`count`), a text of a cell at most 4,096 characters (`truncated`; `sheet.cell` gives it whole, up to the parser's 1 MiB), an answer at most 8 MiB of text (it stops after the line that passes it, and `more` says there are lines after it), a dry run at most 200,000 steps, the section names of a read 256; every number is checked and an unknown key is refused by the registry. A hostile sheet is read within these: 8,192 sections, 320,000 rows in a section, a deleted section or row (shown as nothing), a formula of a megabyte.
* Design 7.5; the window's spec. **The text** is cut of white space at its ends and of one leading `=`, at most 65,536 bytes (no limit is published, and a file's formula may be up to 1 MiB and is kept). **An empty text clears the cell's own formula** (of the inventory): a cell the sheet holds of its own that can inherit one (a master or a style has the cell) goes back to inheriting, `F="Inh"` with **no value of its own**, since the value it had was the result of the formula that went, and what the inherited formula works out to on the sheet is written by the recalculation where it differs from the source's saved value; a cell with nothing to inherit reads `No Formula` and keeps its last value; **a cell the sheet does not hold of its own is not changed** (so no refusal by an inherited `GUARD`, and no step). **Any other text must parse**, and a fault is refused with its kind, its byte offset in the text as given and words (`the formula has an error: a value is due at character 5 (expected_operand, byte 4)`): the window marks the fault from them. A formula is written as typed, the cell keeps the value it had (or, a cell with none, the one it reads now, else the default of its kind) until the recalculation works it out, and a formula that fails keeps that last good value and records its `E` (`#DIV/0!`; a cell that reads a failing cell with a value reads that value); **a function the evaluator does not have is written** and the answer says `worked_out: false`. **The same text over the same cell is no change**: no write, no recalculation, no step. **Typed text in a cell that expects text** (a cell whose catalogue kind is `text`: labels, prompts, formats, menus, tips) **with no leading `=` is a string**: `Unit cost` in `Prop.Cost.Label` is written as the formula `"Unit cost"` with the value `Unit cost`, a quotation mark inside doubled (**ours**: R34 leaves it `unknown`), and **a text that is a string literal already is the formula as it stands** (**ours**: what a cell shows can be typed back, and a formula copied from one cell to another is not quoted twice); with a leading `=` it is a formula, and a text cell given an empty text is cleared and not set to an empty string.
* (inventory V1). **A number literal alone** (`3`, `3 in`, `-0.25 mm`, `25%`) is written **as a value with no formula** (`V` and `U`), as a file holds a plain value. **A bare number is read in the unit the cell shows**: `3` in a cell showing `50 mm` is 3 mm (stored as its inches with `U` `MM`), in a cell showing `2 in` is 3 in, in a cell showing a percentage is 3%; a length cell that shows no unit takes the inch and an angle cell the degree (the default unit of its kind); a cell that shows no unit (a flag, an index) takes the number as it is. **A number typed with its unit keeps it for display** (`U` is the typed unit), and a unit of another measure than the cell's (`3 deg` in a length) makes the text a formula like any other, which the recalculation fits as calc fits a result (`cells.rs`). The cell the sheet shows is the cell of the master or style where the sheet has none, so a cell written on an instance carries the unit its master shows. The two rules of a bare number differ in units other than inches (calc's fitting keeps the stored number and changes only the unit): the design's risk 2.
* Design 7.2. **A cell must be there**: the sheet holds it, or it is inherited from a master or a style, or the catalogue lists it at that place for that kind of sheet (a direct cell of the page-sheet class on a page and on a master's page sheet, a style flag on a style, the others on any sheet; a cell the catalogue lists for a section, in a section and a row that are there). Any other is refused in words and nothing is made: `the sheet has no cell User.Total.Value: add the row first (sheet.add_row)`, `the sheet has no cell Geometry2.NoFill: add the section first (sheet.add_section)`, `the sheet has no cell PageWidth: a shape sheet does not hold it`, `the sheet has no cell NoSuchCell: no batch of the catalogue lists it, and the sheet does not hold it`. A program cannot make a cell no reader of a file would know; the cells of the protection, events and review batches are written only where a sheet holds them until their batches are catalogued (the design's risk 9). A row's name matches in any letter case and the cell written is the row the sheet holds.
* Design 8. **A formula typed in the sheet replaces a guarded one, and a program says so**: a guarded cell (its own `GUARD`, or one inherited) is refused without `force: true` in the words `the cell Width is guarded by GUARD(): send force: true to replace it`, and written with it (`WriteOrigin::AutomationForce`); the window sends `force: true`. A program may write **any cell of any sheet the drawing holds** (a shape, a group's member, a master's shape, a page, a master's page sheet, a style, the document), under these rules: the guard, the locked layer, a cell that must be there, a formula that is data (parsed and worked out, never run: an action cell is never evaluated, and a `SETF` in a cell that is worked out writes only), and **every write one undo step, journaled with its params**.
* Of 2026-11-17, documented behaviour wins, over. **A `SETF` writes when its cell is worked out.** The call is 0 and asks for a write: the cell it names (`GETREF(cell)`, or a string that reads as one reference; any other first argument is `#VALUE!`, a cell found nowhere is `#REF!` and no row is made) and the formula it gives (a string as it is, a number as a formula that reads back as that number; a text that does not parse is `#VALUE!` and leaves the target as it was; a blank one writes nothing). **The commit that worked the cell out makes the writes** (`calc`'s `commit`, `commit_in` and `commit_changed`, so every editing command's recalculation and `sheet.set_cell`'s), once its cells are all worked out, as cell writes of origin `Setf` (the formula becomes the cell's own; no guard stops it), in the order the calls were reached, **the last call that names a cell winning**, and a call whose target holds its text already writes nothing. The cells the writes changed and what reads them are then worked out again in the same commit, so a call comes to rest once the cell it wrote holds its text. **The loop budget and the work budget:** at most **64 formulas** are written by one commit and at most **16 rounds** of working out again are made (the 64; **ours**), at most 4,096 calls are queued by one working-out, a commit whose budget ran out makes none, and every round is charged to the commit's own budget; what is past a cap is dropped and counted in the commit's report (`setf_dropped`, with `setf_written`, `setf_same`, `setf_refused` and `setf_rounds`), so a call that sets itself off (a counter, two cells that write each other, a chain of cells that each write the next) ends at the caps and not at the budget. **When a call is worked out**. A `SETF` is worked out as any formula is: when an edit changes a cell its text reads (the width in `Width*2`, the counter a counter adds to) and in a pass over every cell of the document or a page (`commit`, `commit_in`, and the pass over a whole page that answers a theme or a style); it is **not** one of the calls that are worked out after every edit that changes anything (`SETF` was in `calc`'s `DYNAMIC_FUNCTIONS`, so a counter moved by sixteen on every edit, whatever the edit, and an idempotent call asked for its write each time). Nothing in says a call is worked out on an edit that changes nothing it reads. A `SETF` that sits with a call that is worked out after every edit (`EVALCELL`, `LISTSHEETREF()!Width`) is worked out when that call is. **A `GETREF` or `GETVAL` argument is no read**. The reference that is itself the argument of `GETREF` or `GETVAL` names a cell and is not a link of the dependency graph: a change to that cell does not work out the formula that holds the call. So a person's write to the cell a `SETF` names (`GETREF(Scratch.A1)`) leaves the call alone and the person's value stands, a `SETF` that names its target by a string is no read of it either, and one that also reads its own target by a reference of its own (`SETF(GETREF(N),IF(N<3,N+1,N))`) is worked out when `N` changes, because that reference is a read; a cell named by `GETVAL(PinX)` or `GetRef(User.Q)*22` does not work the cell that holds the call out when it changes. Only the reference that is the argument is an address: what a sum or a branch under the call reads is read. The cells are still **worked out first** when the formula is, so nothing reads a stale value inside one recalculation: two cells that read each other's value by `GETVAL` are a loop for the evaluator as before, and a `SETF` that names a cell through `GETREF` alone reads nothing of it, so two calls that name each other are no circular reference. **A cell that reads a `SETF` cell's value does not make the call write**. A call's write is asked for by **the `SETF` cell worked out as itself**: because an input it reads changed (it is dirty), because a pass works every cell out, or because a dynamic call (`EVALCELL`) works its formula out (the cell that holds the `EVALCELL` asks for the writes of the calls that formula reaches). A formula that reads the cell's value (the call is 0, or the cell's cached value) takes that value and queues nothing: the cell is worked out in place for its value and its calls are not asked for. So a cell worked out for some other input (`Reader` = `Go + Width`, after `Width` changed) does not make `Go` write over a person's value at its target. A `SETF` cell that is dirty is worked out once whichever of it and its readers comes first in the sheet, and its call is queued once (the last call that names a cell still wins, and a cell worked out as itself twice in one pass asks once); the caps and the dropped count are as before. **Where nothing is written:** opening a file recalculates nothing, an action cell is never worked out (so an action's `SETF` is not reached; the build runs no action yet), the dry run of a typed formula (`sheet.evaluate`) writes nothing and says what a commit would make of the cell, and the comparison with a file's saved values (the oracle) and the work of the document before an edit take the old reading. **That reading is kept as a setting** (`EvalOptions::setf`, `SetfMode::Inert`: the call is 0 whatever it names and nothing is queued; the default is `Perform`). A `SETF` can also be reached by an `EVALCELL` of an action cell's formula, which works the formula out, as the pages say `EVALCELL` does.
* `cmd/locked.rs`. **A shape on a locked layer is refused by the registry's rule**, in its words, as for every command; a `sheet.*` call that names a `master` names a master's shape, which no page's layer locks (the rule learns that), and **each write of a `sheet.set_cells` call that names a shape of a page is judged**, one on a locked layer refusing the call whole. A page's own sheet, a master, a style and the document are no shapes.
* **The recalculation, by kind of sheet** (design 7.5 step 7; `draw/sheet.rs`). The cells written and every cell that reads them are worked out (calc's commit of what changed, `settle`), and the connectors they moved are routed again, **once for each page the call touched, at the end**: **a shape of a page** and **a page's own sheet** on that page, the shape as touched; **a master's cell** (a master's shape or its page sheet) on every page that holds an instance of the master, each as a whole page (`Changes::whole_page`, as `theme.apply` does); **the document's cell and a style's cell** on every page, each as a whole page. **The cells of other pages that read a cell worked out** (gap F40): a cell that names a cell of another page through `Pages[..]` (`Pages[Page-1]!Sheet.10!Width`, a page by its name or its number, a cell of the page's own sheet too) is worked out in the same commit as the cell it reads, whatever page it is on, and the cells that read it in turn (on its page, or on a third), so a write on page 1 reaches a chain through every later page, each cell once, and the answer's `recalculated` lists those cells with the others; a pass over a whole page (a master, a style) goes after them in one more commit, which a call that works every page out whole (the document's cell and a style's) leaves out, its pass over each page working them out where they stand. Every step is counted in the budget the pages of the call share. **The connectors glued to a shape of such a page that moved are routed again by the settle step** (`settle::commit`, which every command that writes a cell goes through, compares each page the commit worked cells out on with the page as it was and routes what the shapes whose pose, size or outline cells changed are glued to, as after a change made to the shape itself), so `sheet.set_cell`, `sheet.set_cells`, `shape.move`, `shape.resize`, a data edit, a format and the page commands all do it, and in one place; **the commits a refit of a group and the placing of a glued end make route the pages they reach as well** (each takes its steps from the budget of the commit that made it, and a routing or a refresh of fields that is a commit in its turn reaches pages again, to at most 8 recalculations one inside another, a deeper chain being refused in words with nothing changed), and **the fields in the text of those pages are refreshed**: the shapes of a reached page whose cells the commit worked out have the text of their fields worked out again, for at most 256 shapes in an edit and within the evaluator's budget, the others left to `text.update_fields`; the commit that works out what reads each text, and the routing of the pages that commit reaches, take their steps off the same budget, and a budget that runs out refuses the call in words, as the routing does. **The sheets no page works out** (`draw/unpaged.rs`): the document's sheet, a style's, a master's page sheet and the shapes of a master that no page holds an instance of are worked out **first**, before the pages: the cells of them that differ from what the call began with (written, added, rewritten by a renumber, or taken away with their row or section) and the cells of the same sheet that read those, by calc's commit of what changed, so that a formula typed into the document's sheet reads the value it gives (it kept the 0 it was written with before) and the cells that read it follow it, whether the call writes cells or adds or deletes a row or a section (a `REF()` left by a deleted row has its `#REF!` recorded there as on a page); a sheet that holds no formula is left out, **except for the cells the call wrote on a master when some sheet names a master** (a number written to a master's shape that no page holds an instance of is read by the pages that name the master, `Masters[Meter]!Sheet.5!Width`, which no pass over the pages that hold an instance reaches, so the cells a call wrote there are worked out as changed, the cells that read them on any page follow in the one commit, and the connectors glued to the shapes they moved are routed again; a drawing in which no sheet names a master costs the listing, which the next commit finds kept; a write to the document's sheet or a style works every page out whole and is not asked), and a master's shape that a page holds an instance of is worked out by that page. **The budget is the call's**: the evaluator's 20 million steps are shared by every sheet and page the call works out (`calc_index::SharedSteps`), each taking what is left and taking off what it used, since the budget is derived as that of a whole document and a drawing of many pages that each passed little less than it was worked out in as many budgets, which a file made for it holds for hours; **the call is refused whole when a page passes what is left** (`the page 3 is too large to work out again after this edit, with the pages the edit reaches before it (they share 20000000 steps of the evaluator): nothing was changed`). The work grows with what the pages hold: a write to the document's sheet costs the sum of its pages (`the_steps_of_a_write_to_the_documents_sheet_are_the_sum_of_what_its_pages_cost`), and 64 pages of 2,000 shapes cost a fifth of the budget. **A call that puts every cell it wrote back as it was is no step** (a batch that writes a cell and writes its old formula again stood a value there until the recalculation gave it back). After a whole page the connectors glued to a shape whose pose, size or outline cells changed are routed again, as after a move (by the settle step of each page, where a pass of the call's own did before). The shapes a call names are found **in one walk of each page that holds them** (and of each master), not a search for each write (a count: 4,096 writes on a page of 30,000 shapes walk it a few times, `draw/loops_cost.rs`).
* **What the answer says of the recalculation** (`recalculated`). The cells that changed besides the ones written, on the pages the call worked out and the pages its recalculation reached through a cell that names a page (`Pages[..]`): `cells` their number, `listed` the first 256 (`{sheet, cell}`, `sheet` in the form of `sheet`, `cell` the reference or `null` where none can be spelled), `more` when there are others or a page could not be compared cell by cell. A call that changed no cell says `recalculated: {cells: 0, listed: [], more: false}`.
* **Budgets, as counts**: a formula 65,536 bytes (the 65,537th is refused), a call 4,096 writes (`writes holds at most 4096 writes`), 4,194,304 bytes of formula text in all (`the formulas of one call are at most 4194304 bytes in all`) and 262,144 parts of formulas in all (**ours**: the trees a call parses are held to about 32 MB; `the formulas of one call have too many parts: at most 262144 in all`), and 256 cells and 256 results in an answer. Each is checked before anything is written. An unknown key is refused by the registry, a number outside a whole number from 0 to 4,294,967,295 and a key of the wrong kind in words, and the parser's own limits (1 MiB, 131,072 nodes, 512 levels) hold as ever.
* Design 7.6; the window's spec. **Which sections take what.** Rows of Geometry, Connection Points, Controls, Scratch, Shape Data, User-defined Cells, Hyperlinks, Actions and Action Tag are added and deleted, and so are the stops of the two gradients (a row past the tenth is ignored by whatever reads the stops, and the answer's `note` says so). The section is inserted and deleted: Geometry (and **Ellipse** and **Infinite Line**, as `variant`), Connection Points and Controls on a shape only, the others on any sheet (a page, the document, a style, a master), and Text Transform and Layer Membership on a shape. **Something else makes the rows** of Character, Paragraph, Tabs and Text Fields (`text.format`, `text.insert_field`), of Layers (`layer.add` and `layer.delete`, which keep the members' numbers right) and of Reviewer and Annotation (`comment.add`), and each refusal names it; Shape Transform cannot be inserted or deleted, a group of cells has no rows, and a section no spec lists takes none. A section other than Geometry is there once (`the shape already has User-defined Cells: a section other than Geometry is there once`), a Geometry section takes the next number, and a section the sheet dropped from what a master gives is not added again (`undo that delete to have it again`). MS-VSDX forbids any other row in the section of an Ellipse or an Infinite Line: **a Geometry section that holds an Ellipse or an Infinite Line row, its master's too, holds that row alone**, so no row is added to it (`Geometry2 holds an Ellipse row, and a Geometry section that holds an Ellipse or an Infinite Line row holds that row alone: add the row to another Geometry section (sheet.add_section)`), and **such a row is added only to an empty section** (`an Ellipse or an Infinite Line row can only be added to an empty section: Geometry1 holds other rows, and such a row is the only one of its section: add a Geometry section with the variant Ellipse (sheet.add_section)`) or made with a new one, `sheet.add_section`'s `variant`; a section whose rows were all deleted is empty. No command changes a row's type (`sheet.set_cell` writes cells, and the type `T` is no cell), so there is no change of type to refuse.
* Our rule (observed in the reference application on the project's test PC, so under the owner's standing rule ("do what the reference application does") it replaces the reading of a reference to `WIDTH` as a cell no shape holds; nothing of the case of a reference to a cell directly under a sheet). In the application, `User.Score = WIDTH/1 in*12` with a Width of 4 in was 48; DiaCraft read `WIDTH` as a cell that is not there and gave 0, and nothing worked the formula out again when `Width` changed, since the cell it read had another name. **A cell directly under the sheet that the catalogue lists is named in any letter case in a reference** (`diacraft_doc::direct_cell_spelling`, used by the one reader of a reference's path in `diacraft_calc` (`refs.rs`) that the evaluator, the dependency walk and `cell_address` all go through): `WIDTH`, `width` and `wIdTh` are `Width`, `PINX` is `PinX`, in a formula, after a sheet (`Sheet.4!HEIGHT`) and in the `cell` of the `sheet.*` commands, where a write to `WIDTH` goes to `Width` and makes no cell of that name. **The formula is kept as it was typed** (`WIDTH/1 in*12`), and **a name the catalogue does not list** (a cell of an extension, a name of a file's own) **is read as it is spelled**, as are the names inside a section (`Char.Size`, `Geometry1.X2`): the application was seen with `WIDTH` only, so the section's name and the cells in its rows stay exact (a row's name is). **What a file holds is unchanged**: a cell written `pinx` in a file is an unknown cell, kept verbatim, though a formula that names `pinx` now reads `PinX`. The arithmetic was not the cause: `Width/1 in*12` was 48 already (a quotient of two lengths is a number, and the product after it, `*` and `/` ranking alike and running left to right). Tests: `crates/calc/tests/it/unit_divide.rs`, `crates/engine/tests/it/formula_case.rs`, `crates/doc/tests/it/catalogue.rs`.
* **A row given by name is read as a formula reads a name: the row of that exact spelling first, and only when no row spells it so the row that spells it in another letter case.** Where two rows of a section differ only in case (no drawing of ours makes them, and a command refuses to add one, but a file from another program can hold them), the exact spelling wins, so `sheet.delete_row` of `ROW_5` takes `ROW_5` and not `Row_5` whichever comes first, an `after` or a `before` of `ROW_5` goes by that row, `sheet.cell` and `sheet.set_cell` of `Prop.ROW_5.Value` address that row's cell and a formula that names `Prop.ROW_5` reads it. A name that no row spells exactly and that more than one row spells in other cases is the row of the nearer sheet, then of the lower `IX`, then of the earlier place, the row a formula reads (`diacraft_calc::spell_row`, which the evaluator's own index of a section's rows ranks by too: one rule for the commands and the formulas). A row of the exact spelling that is deleted here (`Del`) is that row and is not there: the name is not read as its live twin (`the section has no row Row_5`), as the evaluator reads it as nothing. A name no row has in any case is `the section has no row <name>`. A name for a **new** row is still refused when any row of the section has it in any letter case.
* **ours** where those say `unknown`. **What is new.** A new row holds every cell the catalogue lists for its section, at its default as a value (a length `0 in`, an angle `0 deg`, text empty). A Geometry row's `X` and `Y` are those of the row before it (when both rows are lengths, or both are shares of the size), so that the drawing does not change until the row is edited, and its other cells are those its type uses (the table of the 15 row types), at 0: a `PolylineTo` holds `POLYLINE(1,1)` and a `NURBSTo` `NURBS(1,1,1,1)` with its weights 1, a straight run, which a person then edits. The first row of a Geometry section must begin a path (`MoveTo`, `RelMoveTo`, `Ellipse` or `InfiniteLine`). **An unnamed row of a named section is `Row_1`, `Row_2` and on**, the first number no row holds in any letter case, a deleted row counting (in Shape Data too, `Property<n>` staying the Define Shape Data dialog's rule); a name given is letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit, at most 256 characters and not a row of the section in any letter case (`the section already has a row Cost`). **A new section holds one row**, a Geometry section a `MoveTo` and a `LineTo`, an Ellipse or an Infinite Line section its one row; Text Transform holds the seven cells with the formulas of `TxtAngle` 0 and Layer Membership an empty `LayerMember`.
* (**R29 is a project rule: no public page says whether a formula follows a row that moves**). An indexed row's `IX` is its key and a reference names it by its number (`Geometry1.X4` is the row of `IX` 4, `Scratch.A3` the row of `IX` 2). An insert goes after the row `after` names or before the row `before` names (the ribbon's Insert is `after`, the right-click menu's Insert Row `before` and Insert Row After `after`), and at the end with neither: it takes the next number, or the number of the row it goes before. **A number nobody holds is taken and nothing moves** (a gap a file left), **a number a row holds is taken by that row and by the run of rows after it, which move one up** (the run ends at the first number nobody holds), and a delete closes the run after it up by one. **Every formula that names a row that moved names it still, and one that named a row that went reads `#REF!`** (the call `REF()`): the formulas of the sheet's page and of the document's sheet, for the document's own rows every style and master (`TheDoc!`), and those of another page that reach the sheet through `Pages[..]`. Each reference is read **by the evaluator's own reading** (`diacraft_calc::Locator`, so `Sheet.20!Connections.X3`, `ThePage!`, a peer's name and a row's name in any letter case are found), and the bytes of its number are all that change (`diacraft_formula::reference_spans` says where they are: the spacing, the strings and every other reference of the formula are kept as typed). A reference with a call before it (`LISTSHEETREF()!Width`), a string worked out as a formula (`EVALTEXT`) and a formula that did not parse are not followed. **The `Connect` rows** of a connection point that moves follow it (`ToPart` 100 plus the `IX`, `ToCell` `Connections.X3`) and a row glued to a point that went is dropped. A name does not move, so a named row that goes leaves the formulas that name it, which read `#REF!` as the evaluator reads any row nothing supplies. **A master's own rows and a style's own rows keep their numbers** (a master's shape or page sheet, a style and the root are read by number by the sheets that inherit from them): a delete there leaves the others as they are, **and the formulas that name the row or the section that went read `REF()` all the same** (the formulas of the style, of the master's page sheet and of its shapes, which the scan of a section of a master or a style visits: a formula left naming a number read the row that took the number later), and an insert that would move a row is refused in words (`rows of Scratch after row 1 are numbered by the instances of this master: add the row at the end`, `... by the shapes that use this style ...`). **A sheet that inherits the section takes a copy first** (below), and then the rows move as in a section the sheet holds itself. A row cannot be numbered past 4,294,967,295 (a Geometry row's `IX`, any other's plus one: `no room for a row after row 4294967295: row numbers end at 4294967295`).
* **R56 for what a renumber writes** (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-26: calc's R56 over the design's V4; MS-VSDX). A formula that now reads `REF()` and had a value keeps that last good value and records `#REF!`, and a cell that reads it reads that value with no error; a formula that had no value to keep records no error (calc's commit leaves a cell with no value to keep alone) and a cell that reads it errors (`crates/engine/tests/it/sheet_rows.rs`).
* **Rows and sections a master or a style gives**. A row the sheet holds and no master or style gives is taken out (`how: removed`); a row a master or a style gives is dropped by a **local `Del` row** with its key and no cell (`how: marked`), the numbers of the other rows staying, and undo brings it back; a section likewise by a `Del` section with its name and `IX`. **A master's own rows and sections keep their numbers** and are removed, not marked (its instances hold rows by number), and an insert at the end is the way to add one. **Copy, then insert** (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-26, `draw/sheet_copy.rs`). **A middle insert into a section a sheet inherits** (a dropped Process shape's Geometry, its Connection Points, the stops a shape gets from its style) **is allowed: the sheet first takes its own copy of the rows, then the insert goes as it goes into a section the sheet holds itself** (the rows after it move up one, and the formulas and `Connect` rows that name them follow), all in **one undo step**, with no `Del` row left dangling. The copy writes every row the sheet reads (its master's and its own, merged, a row it dropped staying dropped) as a row of the sheet's own: **a formula is copied as its text**, with its cached value and unit, and so are the cells of the section itself (Geometry's `NoFill` and the rest); a copied formula that names another row is found and followed with the rest. It is not `F="Inh"` as the copy of a group member's geometry is: an inherited cell reads the master's cell at its own number, which after the rows move is another row's. **The master's cells are kept from showing through**: the row at each number the master holds is given every cell the master's row there holds that it lacks, at its default, as a cell of its own (an arc's `A` is not read on the line that now stands at the arc's number). **What this does to a later edit of the master: the sheet's rows are its own now**, so a number or a formula the master's rows later get no longer reaches this instance (it still reaches every instance that holds no copy), and a row the master later adds at a number the instance has used shows through there; this is expected. A row of the master that names one of the master's shapes by its `ID` (`Sheet.5!Width`) is bound by the instance when it is the master's and would name another shape as the sheet's own, so such a row cannot be copied: the insert is refused in words (`row 1 of Scratch names a shape of the master (Sheet.5) in A: the instance cannot take a copy of it ...: add the row at the end`) and the end is still the place. A copy is held to 2,000,000 cells (refused in words, before anything is written). A **named** row an instance's master gives comes first among the instance's rows whatever the instance does, so a row cannot be put by it and the end is the place (a named row has no number to move). **A Geometry section that goes numbers the later ones again** (Geometry sections have no gaps), and the formulas that name them follow (`Geometry3.X2` is `Geometry2.X2`); a section removed whole turns every reference to its rows to `REF()`. Text Transform and Layer Membership are deleted by taking their cells out (`removed_cells`), and the block reads the defaults of again.
* **Rows and sections, as counts** (`renumbered.work`). The formulas looked at (`visited`: every local formula of the sheets a reference to the section can be on), those whose text holds the section's name and were read for their references (`parsed`: a drawing whose formulas do not name the section costs a pass over their text), and the references located (`located`). A copy costs the cells of the rows it takes (`copied.cells`: one pass over the section, 31,273 rows copied in one call by `an_instance_of_a_master_of_31273_rows_copies_them_once_for_an_insert_in_the_middle`). The evaluator's budget holds the locating, and a drawing too large for it refuses the call whole (`nothing was changed`); at most 200,000 formulas and 1,048,576 parts of formulas are written again in one call; a section holds at most 320,000 rows (`a section holds at most 320000 rows`). Held by `crates/engine/tests/it/sheet_rows.rs`: a section of 31,273 rows is numbered again in one pass over its rows, a renumber that touches 30,000 shapes (each reads a row) writes each formula once, a chain of 10,000 cells that each read the row before is followed in one call, a formula of 6,500 references is read once, and a fixed sequence of 120 inserts and deletes over rows that formulas point at keeps every reference on its row (three sequences, checked against a model); the two timed runs are `#[ignore]`d. **Holds the rest** (`crates/engine/tests/it/sheet_hostile.rs`, every case counted by `diacraft_calc::work`, a timed twin of each `#[ignore]`d): a write to a cell that 100,000 cells read is one commit of 17 steps each, a chain of 10,000 cells one commit of 18 each, 4,096 writes read by 100 cells each (409,600 readers) one commit of 24 each, 64 pages of 2,000 shapes cost 33 steps a shape and one commit a page, formulas at the caps (65,536 bytes nested to the parser's limit, 512 levels, 32,000 arguments) are written or refused in words, a page that passes the budget and pages that pass it together are refused whole, a storm of 60 inserts and deletes over 600 formulas follows every row and is undone a step at a time, and loops of `SETF` end within the budget whichever way the evaluator performs `SETF`. And the **property test** (`sheet_model.rs`): random sequences of the six commands on every kind of sheet, with undo, redo and a save in `.vsdx` and `.diacraft` between them, checked against a model (a refusal changes nothing, a change is one step, the rows and the text of the cells are the model's, **a full recalculation finds the drawing settled**, undo and redo are exact, every writer saves and every `ref` maps back). **One recalculation for each page** the call touched, at the end, as a write is (`settle`).
* **Editing in the window** (`sheet/edit.rs`, `keys.rs`, `bar.rs`, `grid.rs`; design 5.8 to 5.11). **The window edits only through `sheet.set_cell`**, one undo step each. An edit is **begun** by a double click or F2 (the formula's own text, the caret at its end, the arrows move the caret), by a printable key (that character replaces the formula, **typing mode**: the arrows commit and move) or by Delete and Backspace (an empty text), by a press in the bar's text, or by `window.sheetEdit`; a cell that reads `No Formula` is edited from an empty text, and a formula past 65,536 bytes is shown and cannot be edited (`This formula is longer than 65,536 characters: it is kept as it is and cannot be edited here.`). It is **committed** by Enter (down), Tab (right), Shift+Enter and Shift+Tab (up and left), an arrow in typing mode, the accept button, a press on another cell or the paste of a formula (Ctrl+V on a selected cell), as one `sheet.set_cell` with the tab's object, the cell's reference, the text and `force: true`; a text equal to the one the edit began with sends nothing (no command, no step, no revision), and Escape and the cancel button send nothing. **A refusal keeps the edit open** with the command's words (the footer, in the error colour, and a line under the bar), and for a formula that does not parse the fault is **underlined from the byte `sheet.evaluate` gives to the end of the token there, or the last character when the text ended early**; the mark and the words go when the text changes. Each change of the text asks `sheet.evaluate` once (`work.evaluations`) and the bar shows the value, the error or the fault at the right of the text; a cell that expects text takes what is typed as a string, so its live value is the text. **What a commit worked out again** is read from the answer's `recalculated.listed`: those cells of the sheet on view have the `sheet_changed` background **until the next commit** (an undo or any other change of the drawing takes the marks away; no timer), and the footer says `Worked out again: 12 cells changed, 3 on this sheet.`, names the written cell and up to eight of the listed ones that now read an error (`Width now reads #DIV/0!`), says `Nothing changed` for a text the cell held, and says that a function the evaluator does not have was written (`worked_out: false`). While the sheet has the focus its keys are its own and the drawing's Delete, arrows and clipboard keys wait; Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y are the drawing's undo and redo. A display group is **name and value pairs in columns**, a column's edge is dragged (`DRAG_MIN` 24 to 2,000 points) and a double click on it fits it again, a cell's text is **cut at its box's edge with no ellipsis**, and a named row's name is right-aligned and red for an error.
* **Saved and opened again** (`crates/engine/tests/it/sheet_files.rs` with its drawing in `sheet_files_world.rs`, `crates/sheetxml/tests/it/patch_moved.rs`, `crates/vsdx/tests/it/sheet_edits.rs`). **Every edit of the commands above survives a save and a reopen** in each of the six types of a VSDX file and in `.diacraft` (a drawing, a template and a stencil), and in a Save As from one to the other: a cell written (a formula, a value, a clear, a text that holds the characters of markup, a guarded cell forced) on a shape, an instance, a group member, a page, a style, the document and a master's shape, a row added or deleted in every section that takes rows (at the end, in the middle with the rows after it numbered again, into a gap, in a section whose rows have no `IX`), a section added or deleted (a Geometry section numbered again, an Ellipse, Text Transform and Layer Membership), a copy of an instance's inherited rows and the `Del` row or section a delete of an inherited one writes, a batch of writes and a chain of every kind in one save. **The file reads back every sheet cell by cell and row by row** (`IX`, `N`, `T`, `Del`, the units, the formulas as typed, the unknown attributes and elements), `sheet.read` of the edited sheets gives the same lines, **the parts (entries) that hold no edited sheet are the same bytes, and in the one that does only the elements the edit reaches differ, in the same order**; a save with no edit after a save writes the same bytes. A file of the namespace the standard states, one of no namespace and one whose elements carry a prefix are held the same. **A VSDX save into the file patches its tree**: a row, or a Geometry section, that an insert or a delete **numbered again goes on being the element that held it**, with its unknown attribute, unknown element and comment (matched by what it holds that the model has no field for and not by its number: `diacraft_sheetxml::patch::match_items_with`, at most 64 comparisons for each item and then the number as before), and a row that took the number of one that was deleted is a new row, the old row's unknown nodes going with it. **A second save in the same session is no refusal** after an insert before an unknown node: the count of typed children before such a node is the count of the read, which an insert leaves as it was and the file read back counts again, so the patcher compares the nodes and their order and never the count (`same_unknown_nodes`; until a later change that save said `saving does not yet write this change: a change to the unknown elements of a shape` (or a section, or a row)). The model writers write each unknown node after as many typed children as its count says, so **every writer of a cell, a row, a section or a shape keeps the count in step** (`crates/doc/src/places.rs` and the writers of `crates/doc/src/sheet.rs` with `diacraft_doc::Passthrough::children_inserted`, `children_removed`, `children_followed` and `children_followed_by`, `crates/doc/tests/it/places.rs`, and in the engine `crates/engine/tests/it/sheet_places.rs`, `sheet_places_writers.rs`, `shape_places.rs`, `rebuilt_places.rs` and the ratchet `places_guard.rs`; the matrix above compares the counts exactly for the cell commands too): a row, a section or a cell that a command puts in, or takes out, moves the count of every node that stood after it, in each list that counts it (a section's nodes count its cells and then its rows, a row's its cells, a sheet's its cells and then its sections, and so do those of the shape or the style that holds the sheet, whose `Text` and members come after), and **a node goes on following the child it followed**: ahead of a row put in right after that child (a row at the end of a section too, and a section put in after the last), behind a node that stood before the first row, and with the child before it when its own is taken out. **The writers of the model do it themselves**, so none that goes through them can forget: `Sheet::set_cell`, `remove_cell`, `section_mut` and `row_mut`, `Row::put_cell`, `Section::put_cell` and `Row::replace_cells`, `Section::insert_row`, `remove_rows`, `retain_rows`, `sort_rows_by_key` and `replace_rows`, `Sheet::insert_section` and `remove_sections` (the nodes of the sheet, the section and the row), `Counted` from `Document::counted_mut`, `Shape::counted_sheet` and `Style::counted_sheet` (the same, with the nodes of the shape or the style that holds the sheet), and `Page::push_shape`, `insert_shape`, `remove_shape` and `edit_shapes` with their kin for a master and a group (**the unknown nodes of a `Shapes` list follow the shapes they followed**: a shape deleted, drawn, pasted, put in front or behind, grouped or ungrouped moves the nodes the same way). The cell commands (`sheet.set_cell`, `sheet.set_cells`, and every write of a cell through the document, a calculation's cached result among them), `shapedata.define`, `hyperlink.set`, `text.format`, `layer.delete`, the container and swimlane settings, the shape operations and the rest of the commands that make or take out a row or a section on a shape are held to it. So a drawing from a `.diacraft` file saved as a VSDX file, and any Save As across the formats, puts a comment or a foreign element after the same row that a save into the VSDX file does; an undo and a redo give the counts back with the rest of the document (the history holds whole snapshots); and a copy of an inherited section into an instance (copy, then insert) moves the nodes of the instance's section in one merge of the rows. A local section whose rows are out of the order of their numbers (a row a cell write made for an instance goes after the rows it holds, and another program may list them so) is put in order by a stable sort when it is copied into an instance, **and each node goes with the row it followed** (`Section::sort_rows_by_key`); it used to be put in order whole with the nodes at their counts. **No write of a list of cells is left without a reason**: the writers that put a cell straight into a list of cells (`cells.insert`: the four cells of a picture's box in a Save As to VSDX, a drop's pin and scale cell, the pin a drop fixes) go through `Sheet::set_cell` and `Counted`, and the ratchet `places_guard.rs` holds the lists of cells of every crate as it holds the rows, the sections and the shapes of the engine: a write of one by the list's own methods is a count on a list with its reason (a sheet, a section or a row that is new and nobody holds a node in, a plan of a row that `Row::replace_cells` writes, a file being read, the sheet an `.odg` writer compares, another list of the name). **A list made again keeps each node with the child it followed** (`crates/engine/tests/it/rebuilt_places.rs`, counted by `work::places_read` and `work::follow_keys`: the nodes and the keys are read once each, and nothing for a list that holds no node): the rows of a connector's route and of a path a tool carries on or closes replace those of the `Geometry` section whole, and each node stays after the row of the same `IX` it followed (`Section::replace_rows`; a node whose row is gone goes with the row before it, and the rows put in go ahead of the node that trailed the route); the sheet of a shape changed to another master takes the nodes of the old one (`Sheet::take_places_of_where` and `owner_places_after_where`: the sections the new master gives are new, whatever the old ones were called); and the copy a Save As an `.odg` is given (the frame and the style as constants, the sections merged with the master's, the rows the master gives the text) takes the nodes of the shape's sheet, of its sections and of the shape (`Sheet::take_places_of`, `Section::take_places_of` and `owner_places_after`), so a node among the cells, the rows or the sections of a shape stands after the same cell, row or section in the VSDX file that comes back from the `.odg`; a list a Save As across the formats rebuilds one shape for one (a shape given back as itself or as the shape it was) keeps the counts it had, which a test holds. **What is left:** the unknown nodes inside a `Geometry` or a `Connection` section are not carried through an `.odg`, which builds those sections again from what the shape resolves to (as it did), and a cell the `.odg` reader does not give back (a guide's `Angle` of 0) leaves the counts that ride in the file one place off in the VSDX file that comes back. A section of 31,273 rows numbered again is saved in about a second, the cost of the patcher's matching held to counts (`patch_moved.rs`). The `.odg` carries the edits.
* **Rows and sections in the window** (`sheet/rows.rs`, `cards.rs`, `menu.rs`; design 5.12 and 5.13). **The window adds and deletes rows and sections only through `sheet.add_row`, `sheet.delete_row`, `sheet.add_section` and `sheet.delete_section`**, one undo step each, and says in the footer and in the window state's `sheet.last` what the engine answered or why it refused; **an edit that is open is committed first**, as a press on another cell commits it, and a text the engine refuses stays in the editor and stops the command. **The Sections group**: **Insert** opens the Insert Section card (every section some sheet takes, in the window's order, in two columns where the card is wide enough), and OK sends one `command.batch` of `sheet.add_section` for the boxes ticked, with the first section added selected; **Delete** sends `sheet.delete_section` for the section of the selected cell and is greyed on Shape Transform. **The Rows group**: **Insert** sends `sheet.add_row` **after** the selected row and **Delete** `sheet.delete_row` for it; a cell of a row is in its row, a header selected adds at the end, and the footer says how many rows were numbered again and how many formulas followed them and that the sheet took its own copy of the rows it inherits first (the owner's ruling). **A control is greyed, with the engine's words in its tooltip, for what the window knows before it asks**: the rows the text, the layers and the comments make (`rows_refusal`), a section that cannot go (`section_refusal`) and a Geometry section that holds an Ellipse or an Infinite Line row holds that row alone, so Insert is greyed on it; what it cannot know, an insert in the middle of a master's own rows, the engine refuses and the footer says. **The sheet's right-click menu** (a cell, a row's number, a section's header, or Shift+F10) holds **Insert Row** (before the selected row), **Insert Row After** (Geometry only), **Delete Row**, **Insert Section...** and **Delete Section**, each the command its control sends, then Formulas and Values. **The Editing group**: **Shape Data** adds a row to the Shape Data section, **Link** to Hyperlinks and **Shape Action** to the selected Actions section (greyed until one is selected), each by `window.sheetAddRow`; the design (5.13) had Shape Data and Link open the Define Shape Data and Hyperlinks dialogs, and the specification's later answer wins (the owner's rule of 2026-11-17). **Edit Formula** and **Ctrl+E** open the Edit Formula card: Enter adds a line, Ctrl+Enter is OK and Escape is Cancel. What the window state says: `card` (`insertSection` with its `items`, or `editFormula` with the cell, its text and the engine's refusal) and `ops` (`{ok, reason}` for `insertRow`, `deleteRow`, `insertSection`, `deleteSection`, `editFormula`, `shapeData`, `link` and `shapeAction`, the reasons being the words of the tooltips). Tests: `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/sheet_rows.rs`.
* **Not here yet.** AutoComplete, reference by click and the same-window option (UI4) and the `.odg` round trip are later tasks of the plan; Change Row Type and Expand Row, which the right-click menu would also hold, stay later work. The cells of the protection, events and review batches have the kind `scalar` and no default of their own until the catalogue lists them (the design's risk 9).

## Closing the P0 rows

The rules that closed fourteen of the seventeen P0 rows still scored partial (`parity-checklist.md`): what the engine and the window gained, and what the rows said that was stale. Each is ours, and each is on the list of what to compare with the reference application (the check list).

* Our rule ("a group acts as one shape for resize, rotate and align"). `shape.size` takes a group: `Width` and `Height` of the group are written and **its members follow by the stretch of its frame** (`draw/scale.rs`, `scale_members_of`), the same stretch `shape.resize` gives it, so each member stays at the same place of the group's box; the group keeps its pin (`LocPinX` and `LocPinY` follow when they are formulas of the size) and the whole is one undo step. A member on a locked layer refuses it in words ("resized"), and a shape named together with a group it is in is refused too ("shape N is in group M, which is sized in the same command"), since the group's size would carry it a second time. The members one command carries are bounded (`MAX_SCALED_MEMBERS`, 20,000), as for a resize.
