  **The connector's right-click menu** (`CONNECTOR_MENU` of `ribbon/spec.rs`, when every shape selected is a connector; a menu of the shapes selected otherwise): Cut, Copy, Paste (at the click), Delete (which takes the connectors glued to the selection along, as the key does), Bring to Front and Send to Back (their two rows each), **Right-Angle Connector**, **Straight Connector** and **Curved Connector** (each is `connector.style` of the connectors selected, which routes them again, one undo step; their place above Reset Connector and their words are ours, the design call), **Reverse Ends** (`arrange.reverseEnds`, after Curved Connector, with its key Ctrl+Alt+R at the right of the row; ours), **Reset Connector** (`connector.reset` of the connectors selected: it is on a connector's right-click menu) and **Reroute**, a menu of four check boxes (Reroute Freely, Reroute As Needed, Never Reroute, Reroute on Crossover: the one the connectors selected agree on is ticked), each one `connector.reroute` of the connectors selected, one undo step
  (the reroute setting is an ordinary edit: it is not a View setting). The Reroute rows' place is **ours** (the specifications list the four commands among those that are on no tab and say the Behavior dialog's Connector tab has the list, which this build does not have; Q2 of the report). **Edit Text is not a row**, for want of a command that opens the box (F2 and a double click do). `ui.inspect` tells `legs` (`{connector, handles: [{leg, level, at}], reroute, dragging: {leg, to, raw, snap}}`, `null` with none) and the names `connector.leg.<n>`
  are the handles' press areas; `DiacraftApp::connector_leg_point` is where a client takes hold. The drag is **not built for**: Shift with an arrow key moving the handle by a pixel (Support), a handle on a straight or curved connector, and a leg that is shorter than 24 points.
* **Line jumps**. A jump is rows of the connector that carries it, written
  when connectors are routed, **never at open** and never drawn by the renderer. *Who takes part*: top-level connectors (made by DiaCraft or glued at an end, with `MoveTo`, `LineTo`, `ArcTo`
  and `PolylineTo` rows only, at most 256 legs); a curved connector takes none and gets none, and a line that is not a connector takes no part; at most 2,000 take part and 100,000 points
  between them, past which a page has no jumps made. *What a rebuild reads*: the routes of those connectors and the old routes of the ones routed, within 400,000 rows for the rebuild (`draw::MAX_JUMP_ROWS`), counted before any is merged; a route of more than 4,096 rows takes no part and is not read, and a page whose routes hold more rows than the rebuild may read has no jumps made, as a page of too many connectors has none (the routes were read whole whenever a connector was routed: 16 million rows beside 10,000 routes of 4,000 rows, for the move of one). *When*: after a command routes connectors, the routed ones are rebuilt, and so is every connector whose legs cross their old or their new route **that has a hop to make or take away**: one
  that has no hop and needs none (its rows and its new path are a `MoveTo` and `LineTo` rows only) keeps the rows it has, however they are written, **the rows the router has just written and a rebuild of every connector included** (the rows worked out again from the points they give are snapped and rounded again, a unit in the ninth place from the router's: a page of 48 right-angle connectors that cross nothing had 32 of them written again after the router, and more at each rebuild after that); the same after a delete, for the connectors a deleted one
  crossed; no other connector is touched; `connector.line_jumps` rebuilds every connector. Each is rebuilt from the route it has with its jumps
  taken out (the rows' ends with the points on a leg dropped), and a connector whose rows come out as they are is not written: the rows are the same when each cell is, a number being the same number however it is spelled (`-0` is `0`: a route a file holds with a `-0` is not written again for rows the rebuild has with a `0`, and keeps the file's own text), and the text of the numbers the editing commands write (nine places, `stencil::number_text`: the rows of routes, labels, glue and shape operations, and the cells of the others) has no `-0`, a zero being `0` whichever way it came (a point of a route carried into the connector's own frame and out again is a hair either side of 0, and the router wrote one sign where the rebuild worked out the other, and wrote the route again). A paste, group or ungroup makes no jumps. *Which connector carries it*:
  the page's `LineJumpCode`, read as 1 where nothing sets it, as the root of every file holds it: 0 none, 1 the flatter leg of the two crossing, 2 the steeper, 3 and 4 the connector
  higher in the page's drawing order (3, the last routed, stands in the order), 5 the lower, 6 and the rest none; equally steep goes to the higher. A connector's own `ConLineJumpCode` overrides
  1 never carries, 2 carries where the page gives the crossing to nobody, 3 never carries and the connector it crosses does instead, 4 neither carries; the page's choice wins a
  conflict. *Size*: a chord of `LineToLineX` times `LineJumpFactorX` on a level or slanted leg and `LineToLineY` times `LineJumpFactorY` on an upright one, in drawing units, 0.125 and 2/3
  where nothing sets them; none for a size of 0. *Room*: at least half a chord from both ends of the leg, and a second jump closer than a chord to the first is not made. *Look*
  (`LineJumpStyle`, `ConLineJumpStyle` when it is not 0): an arc (0, 1, and 5 to 9 by the project rule), a gap (2: a `MoveTo` to the far end of the chord), a square (3: a `PolylineTo` with a control
  point half a chord off each end of the chord), two sides (4: a `PolylineTo` with one control point half a chord off the crossing). *Side*: up on a level or slanted leg and left on an upright one
  by default; `PageLineJumpDirX` or `ConLineJumpDirX` 2 puts it down, `PageLineJumpDirY` or `ConLineJumpDirY` 2 puts it to the right. An arc's `A` is the half chord, **negative to the left of the way the leg
  runs** and carried into the connector's own frame (a mirrored connector has the other sign): a level leg running toward +x bulges up with `-0.0416...`, toward -x with `+`; the cells are plain
  numbers, `U` `DL` on `A`. `connector.line_jumps` takes `show` (the Connectors menu's Show Line Jumps: on makes the page's code 1 where it is 0 and leaves another code alone, off makes it 0 —
  ours, says Support does not say), `code` 0 to 5, `style` 0 to 9, `dir_x` and `dir_y` 0 to 2, `factor_x` and `factor_y` 0 to 10 (the page only); with `ids` it sets the own code, style
  and sides of those connectors (0 gives the page's back). **The work is bounded**: one rebuild tests at most 4,000,000 pairs of legs and writes nothing when that is not enough.

### What a route goes round

The first piece of the connector routing feature, which is designed and built in tasks (the design's section 1.2): **which shapes a route will go round**, the cells that say it, and the commands that set them.
**No route goes round any of them yet**: above still takes only the two shapes a connector is glued to, and the router that uses what is below is a later task. The reference app was never taken apart: every rule below is **ours**, built, and the owner's rulings of 2026-11-25
(of the design), and is listed for the check list. The code is `draw/obstacle.rs`, `draw/behavior.rs` and `cmd/behavior.rs`; the tests are `tests/it/route_behavior.rs` and the unit tests of the two modules.

* Our rule. For a connector at the top level of a page, an **obstacle** is a shape of the page's top level that is (1) **two-dimensional**, not a guide, not deleted from its master, with a box of finite numbers inside
  `MAX_COORD` that has an area; (2) **placeable**: its effective `ObjType`, read by mask (1 placeable, 2 routable, 4 neither and outranking both, 8 a group of members, values add up), has flag 1 and not 4, **or** holds none of
  1, 2 and 4 and a connector has an end glued to it (the *Let the application decide*: placeable once a connector is glued to it); **a group that holds 8 and not 1 is no obstacle itself, glued or not, and its members are taken by the same rule**, down to eight levels
  (`obstacle::MAX_MEMBER_DEPTH`; a group of 9 is one obstacle, and its members are not looked at); (3) **not hidden**: on no layer, or on at least one layer that is shown (the *hidden*, read from the shape's own `LayerMember`). **An obstacle is its box on the page**, level and
  upright: the box round the four corners of its frame, so a turned shape is the box that holds it and an ellipse is its box. A shape whose `ShapePermeableX` reads 1 lets level legs through, and one whose `ShapePermeableY` reads 1 upright legs (read through
  masters and styles; a guide reads 1 and is no obstacle anyway). The exemption (a shape whose box holds an end of the connector is no obstacle for that connector) needs the ends, and is the router's. `shape.behavior` says for each shape whether it
  is an obstacle now and, when it is not, why: a connector or a line, a guide, deleted from its master, a box that is empty or beyond `MAX_COORD`, placement behavior *Do not lay out and route around*, a group of members (8 without 1), marked routable and not placeable (2),
  *Let the application decide* with no connector glued to it, or every layer hidden.
* **Gluing makes a shape placeable** (owner 2026-11-25). A connector glued to a two-dimensional shape that reads none of the flags 1, 2 and 4 writes a **local `ObjType` of the flags it holds and 1** (a group's 8 becomes 9), **in the same undo step as the glue** (`connector.add`,
  `connector.reconnect`, AutoConnect, Change Shape's glue again, and a Re-Layout that glues the ends again): one batch of writes, each shape once. A shape that reads 1, 2 or 4, a connector or a line, a guide, a deleted shape, and a shape whose `ObjType` a `GUARD` protects are not written (and the
  glue is made all the same); a free end writes nothing; and no connector is routed again because of the write (the write is no cause: is the cause of a route made again). Undo takes the cell back with the glue.
* **The masters people join hold `ObjType` 1, and the cross-functional parts hold 4** (owner 2026-11-25): every two-dimensional master of Basic Shapes, the Basic Flowchart, the Gane-Sarson shapes and the Organization Chart Shapes (each says so in its dress, `Dress::obj_type`, and the master's shape holds the cell), so a shape dropped on a
  route is placeable at once. **The Swimlane and the Separator of the Cross-Functional Flowchart stencil hold `ObjType` 4** (`More::NEITHER`: neither placeable nor routable, as the reference's 76 swimlane and 77 separator masters hold it), **and so do the lane, the phase, the list of lanes and the list of phases** that `swimlane.create`, `swimlane.insert`, `swimlane.insert_phase` and the Swimlane and Separator drops make with no master (`stencil/swimlane.rs`), **while the frame of the cross-functional flowchart holds 1**, as the reference's outer container does. By 4 outranks 1 and 2: no route goes round a lane or a phase, a glue to one writes nothing on it (a glue writes only on a shape that reads none of 1, 2 and 4), and `shape.set_behavior` can still give one another placement. **The decorative shapes, the arrows and what the window makes with no master outside the cross-functional parts (a container, a callout, a text box) hold none**, and become placeable when a connector is glued to them or when told to be.
  A drawing saved before this change holds the older masters, which a drop finds again by their GUID and which hold none: a shape dropped from them reads 0 until a connector is glued to it. **A file keeps its own values:** the lanes, the phases, the lists and the frame an earlier build made hold none, and a save changes none of them, in any format; only the shapes DiaCraft makes now hold the cells. A group made by `shape.group` holds none either.
* Our rule: `shape.set_behavior` sets the Placement tab's boxes, `shape.behavior` reads them. *Placement* is `ObjType`: `auto` 0, `route_around` 1, `none` 4, **the flags outside 1, 2 and 4 kept** (a
  group's 8: `route_around` on a shape that holds 28 writes 25, and `auto` 24). `do_not_move` is flag 1 of `ShapeFixedCode`, **the other flags kept** (2, 4, 32, 64 and 128 are not this box's; the tab's box *Do not allow other shapes to move this shape away on drop*, which `ShapeFixedCode` also holds,
  has no key yet, and the cell is read and kept as it is). `allow_on_top` is `ShapePermeablePlace`, `plow` is `ShapePlowCode` (`as_page` 0, `never` 1, `always` 2; another number reads as the page's), `route_through_x` and `route_through_y` are `ShapePermeableX` and `ShapePermeableY`.
  Only what is given is written, **each cell locally and only where the shape reads something else** (`auto` on a shape whose master holds 1 writes a local 0; `route_through_y: false` on a shape that reads 0 writes nothing), as one undo step, `Shape behavior`, and **no step when nothing is written**.
  **All or nothing**: a shape that is not on the page, a connector or a line (`connector.reroute` and `connector.style` set how those are routed) or a guide refuses the call in words. A shape on a locked layer is refused first, as every edit is. **It routes nothing**: it is a setting, as `connector.reroute` is, and a route that goes round a
  shape that stops being an obstacle, or through one that starts to be, is made again when something asks (a later task).
* **Files.** Every cell above is an ordinary cell, written by the VSDX writer and kept by the splice as the shape's own, and it is in the model of a `.diacraft` file; in an `.odg` none has an attribute of ODF: a shape's ride in the `diacraft:cells` attribute of its own automatic style, and a master's in the document file
  (`file-format-parity.md`), in a new drawing and in the splice of a file that was opened, and come back as the same cells (`tests/it/route_behavior.rs`, in the three formats). **A connector no edit reached keeps its rows byte for byte**: the VSDX element of a connector, the `draw:connector` markup of an `.odg` and the shape of a `.diacraft` are as the file had them
  when a second connector is glued to other shapes and the file is saved in place.
* **What it costs.** A call is **one walk of the page** for all the shapes it names (`scan::named`, the same count whether it names one or 4,096; counted by `draw/behavior.rs`), then a read of a fixed number of cells for each; a walk of a group's members is charged one for each shape looked at to a budget the caller gives
  (`obstacle::obstacles_of`), and stops when it is spent and says so; the layers are read once for a call; the shapes a connector is glued to are found by one pass over the page's `Connect` rows; and the shapes a Re-Layout glues are made placeable in **one batch**, with no search for each (counted by `draw/obstacle.rs`).

## The page's routing settings

The commands `page.routing` and `page.set_routing`, the routing styles with a direction in `connector.style`, and `connector.path`: the engine's side of the Page Setup dialog's Layout and
Routing tab, its Spacing dialog and the Connector tab of the Behavior dialog (the first of the connector routing design's tasks: sections 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 and 5 of the design). The reference app was never taken apart: every rule below is **ours**,
built on and
And is listed for the check list. The code is `draw/routing.rs` and `draw/style.rs`; the commands are in `cmd/routing.rs` and `cmd/path.rs`. **No cell here changes
a route by itself** but the style: a route is still the right-angle route of and the straight and curved ones, and the spacing, Separate, Overlap and lean cells are written and kept for the
router that follows.

* Our rule, extends. A page's `RouteStyle` and a connector's `ShapeRouteStyle` hold one of the 22 codes of the table, and a 0 that is the default, right angle.
  `draw::RouteStyle` is the code with its direction: right angle 1, straight 2, **organization chart** 3, 4, 10 and 11, **flowchart** 5, 6, 12 and 13, **tree** 7, 8, 14 and 15 (top to bottom, left to right, bottom to top and right to
  left, in that order), network 9, centre to centre 16, **simple** 17 to 20 (the same four directions) and 21 (level, then upright) and 22 (upright, then level). `draw::route_style_of(code)` reads a cell (the code nearest the number; **a 0, a
  number between two codes, one outside 0 to 22 and one that is no number read as right angle**), `RouteStyle::code` writes one (right angle is 1), and `RouteStyle::family` and `RouteStyle::direction` give its words (`right_angle`,
  `straight`, `org_chart`, `flowchart`, `tree`, `network`, `centre_to_centre`, `simple`; `top_to_bottom`, `left_to_right`, `bottom_to_top`, `right_to_left`, and `level_first` and `upright_first` for the simple style, `null` for a style with none).
  **What a connector follows** is its own `ShapeRouteStyle` or, where that is 0, the page's `RouteStyle` (`draw::connector_style`). **What it draws is as before**: a directional style, the network and the simple styles
  draw right-angle routes, 2 is straight and 16 centre to centre, and a connector whose appearance is 2 is curved. `draw::lean_of(style)` is the way a directional style leans ("a router should prefer the direction and
  may leave it"): top to bottom is down the page, left to right is right, and so on, for the codes 3 to 8, 10 to 15 and 17 to 20, and none for any other; the router takes it up later.
* Our rule: the tab's mapping of controls to cells is "our reading from the cells' definitions". `page.set_routing` writes the cells the call names, **each once, in one write and one undo
  step**, and only those that read differently now (a call that finds them as they are is no undo step): `style` and `direction` the page's `RouteStyle` (a style that takes a direction and is given none flows `top_to_bottom`; a
  `direction` alone turns the style the page has; the words are read in any case with `-` or a space for `_`, and `Organization Chart` and `Center to Center` are taken); `separate` `LineAdjustFrom` (`unrelated` 0, `all` 1, `none` 2,
  `by_style` 3); `overlap` `LineAdjustTo` (`by_style` 0, `all` 1, `none` 2, `related` 3); `appearance` `LineRouteExt` (`straight` 1, `curved` 2); `plow` `PlowCode` and `split` `PageShapeSplit` (0 or 1, **written and kept, not acted on yet**: no
  shape is moved away and no connector split); and the four spacing groups, each `{x, y}` (either alone) in **paper inches, written in drawing units** (a paper length times the page's drawing scale, `units_per_inch`; a cell of 1.1 on a
  page of a scale of 10 is 0.11 inch on paper): `between_shapes` `AvenueSizeX` and `AvenueSizeY`, `shape_size` `BlockSizeX` and `BlockSizeY`, `connector_to_connector` `LineToLineX` and `LineToLineY`, `connector_to_shape` `LineToNodeX` and
  `LineToNodeY` (the four groups). A length must be a number of inches more than 0 and within a million drawing units. A direction the style does not take (`right_angle`, `straight`, `network` and `centre_to_centre` take none), `level_first` and
  `upright_first` given to a style other than `simple`, a word that is none of the words there are and a call that names nothing are **refused in words** and change nothing. The answer is what `page.routing` says, and `routed`.
* **`page.routing`** (query; `page`?) answers `{page, style, direction, style_code, separate, overlap, appearance, line_jumps, plow, split, between_shapes, shape_size, connector_to_connector, connector_to_shape, held}`: `style` and `direction`
  (`null` for a style with none) are the words of `page.set_routing`, `style_code` is the code of right angle is 1 whether the cell reads 0 or 1, `line_jumps` is `{code, style, factor_x, factor_y, dir_x, dir_y}` as `connector.line_jumps` sets
  them, each spacing group is `{x, y}` in paper inches, and `held` has a flag for each setting (`style`, `separate`, `overlap`, `appearance`, `line_jumps`, `plow`, `split` and the four groups) that says whether **the page holds it itself** (a cell of its own sheet)
  **or the root style or the default gives it**. **What a page reads where it holds nothing** (the root holds every one in a file): `LineAdjustFrom`, `LineAdjustTo`, `LineRouteExt`, `PlowCode` and `PageShapeSplit` 0 (the project rule:
  a page with no cell does not split) and a number outside a list's range as 0; a spacing cell found nowhere, no number or below 0 as the root's US value in the page's drawing units, as the jump size takes its own (`jumps.rs`): 1/8 inch for the
  two connector gaps, 3/8 for the space between shapes and 1/4 for the shape size (a connector gap of 0 is 0, and the other two must be more than 0, as the layout reads them).
* ours, a design call: the project rule follows the reading that a change of the page's routing policy asks for a reroute, and says the tab changes only dynamic connectors; research need N2.
  A `page.set_routing` that gives the page **another routing style** (not the same style again, and not a 0 made a 1, which is the same right angle) asks a new route, as a command about the connector does (`settle_forced`), of every connector of
  the page that **follows the page** (its own `ShapeRouteStyle` is 0), **is set to reroute freely** (`ConFixedCode` reads as freely: 0, and the 4, 5 and 6 of whole-shape glue) and is not on a locked layer, in the edit's limit of routes (the others are
  said in `groups_left`). **A connector with a style of its own, one set to 1, 2 or 3 (a 3 is also the mark of a hand edit) and one on a locked layer are left as they are.** The new route is the style's: a straight page makes the followers one leg, any
  right-angle style the right-angle route. **Nothing else asks a route:** not the appearance (it "concerns new connectors", and a connector takes it at its next route), not the spacing cells ("the next route keeps the new gap, and paths
  already saved stay as they are"), not Separate or Overlap, and **not the Connectors menu with nothing selected** (`connector.style` without `ids`, today's rule kept: it "sets the default for new connectors", which also holds for the
  new styles). The `routed` of the answer is how many connectors were asked.
* **`connector.style`** takes the other six words too, `org_chart`, `flowchart`, `tree`, `network`, `centre_to_centre` and `simple`, with `direction`: with `ids` it writes on each connector `ShapeRouteStyle` the style's code and `ConLineRouteExt` 1 (straight
  legs, as `right_angle` and `straight` write 1), undoes a hand edit and routes it again, as for the three of the menu; with none it writes the page's `RouteStyle` and `LineRouteExt` 1 and routes nothing. The answer has `direction` for a style that has one.
  `right_angle`, `straight` and `curved` take no direction and refuse one in words. **A directional style on a connector DiaCraft made is saved as `.odg` with the default connector type, and the cells that say the style ride in DiaCraft's data** (the format has a `draw:type` for a standard, a straight and a curved connector, and no place for a flowchart's direction; the save used to refuse it in words),
  and the style comes back from the file; `.diacraft` and VSDX keep it whole too, and the page's own style is kept by all three (the page's cells ride in the `.odg`'s own document file).
* **`connector.path`** (query; `id`, `page`?) answers `{page, id, points, style, route_style, reroute, hand_edited, editable}`: `points` are the corners of the route on the page, the begin first, **in paper inches** (`[x, y]` each: what `draw::connector_path`
  gives a window, divided by the page's drawing scale), and `null` for a connector whose rows are no path of lines (a curve); `style` is what it draws (`right_angle`, `straight`, `curved` or `centre_to_centre`); `route_style` is
  `{style, direction, code, own}`, the routing style it follows and whether it is the connector's own; `reroute` is its setting (`freely`, `as_needed`, `never` or `on_crossover`); `hand_edited` is whether its `ConFixedCode` is 3, and `editable`
  whether `connector.edit_path` can move its legs. A shape that is not a connector, one that is not there and a page that is not there are refused in words. It reads and changes nothing, and is no undo step.
* **In the files.** Every cell is a cell of the page (or of the connector), so it is kept whole by `.diacraft`, by the VSDX writer and by a save into a VSDX file, and by the `.odg` writer and a save into an `.odg` file, where the page's cells that the markup cannot say ride in DiaCraft's
  own document file (`tests/it/route_settings.rs` saves and reopens each in the three).
* **The window's Layout and Routing tab** (ours: name what it shows and none says how it works; the code is `crates/ui-egui/src/page_setup/routing.rs`, `routing_spacing.rs` and `routing_preview.rs`).
  The Page Setup dialog's sixth tab (the Design tab's Layout launcher opens it, and `window.pageSetup {tab: "Layout and Routing"}`) **reads `page.routing`** when the dialog opens and works on the dialog's draft like the other tabs.
  * **Routing:** Style (Right Angle, Straight, Organization Chart, Flowchart, Tree, Network, Center to Center, Simple), **Direction** (Top to Bottom, Left to Right, Bottom to Top and Right to Left, and for Simple also Level First and Upright
    First; **greyed for Right Angle, Straight, Network and Center to Center**, which take none, and a style that takes one starts from the top), Separate (Unrelated lines, All lines, No lines, Using routing style), Overlap (Related lines,
    All lines, No lines, Using routing style) and Appearance (Straight, Curved).
  * **Line jumps:** Add line jumps to (None, Horizontal Lines, Vertical Lines, Last Routed Line, Last Displayed Line, First Displayed Line: the codes 0 to 5), Line jump style (Arc, Gap, Square, 2 to 7 Sides) and **Vertical size and Horizontal
    size**, each a slider and a number box that hold one number from 0 to 10 (`LineJumpFactorY` and `LineJumpFactorX`; a box that is no number from 0 to 10 is refused in words).
  * **Other:** Move other shapes away on drop (`PlowCode`) and Enable connector splitting (`PageShapeSplit`) write their cells; **DiaCraft acts on neither yet**, and the group says so in a line under the boxes and in each box's tip.
  * **OK sends one `command.batch` labelled Page setup**, **always a batch** (even for one command), holding what the other tabs changed and then a `page.set_routing` and a `connector.line_jumps`, **each with only what the person changed** (a
    list set to the value it has, a box that still says what it said, and a tab nobody touched send nothing, so no cell nobody touched is written; `connector.line_jumps` is left out unless a jump list or size changed, as it writes the page's
    jump cells even for the values they hold): one undo step. Cancel and Escape send nothing, and an Escape that closes an open list closes only the list. A refusal (a size that is no number from 0 to 10, a page taken away, a length the engine
    refuses) is told in the dialog, which stays. A new Style routes again the connectors that follow the page and are set to reroute freely; Appearance, Separate, Overlap and the spacing route nothing.
  * **Spacing... opens the Layout and Routing Spacing dialog** (a modal over the Page Setup dialog, which leaves it Escape and Enter): four groups, Space between shapes, Average shape size, Connector to connector and Connector to shape, each a
    Horizontal and a Vertical box (`AvenueSizeX` and `Y`, `BlockSizeX` and `Y`, `LineToLineX` and `Y`, `LineToNodeX` and `Y`), a box taking a number in the unit shown or a length with a unit (`1 cm`: `measure.rs`). **OK puts the four groups in the
    tab's draft** (the Page Setup dialog's OK sends them as `page.set_routing`'s groups, each axis that changed, in paper inches); Cancel drops what was typed. **A box the person changed that is no length more than 0 is told in words and the dialog
    stays; a box that still says what it said is not looked at** (a file may hold a gap of 0). **Defaults** fills both boxes of each group with **the root style's values**: 3/8, 1/4, 1/8 and 1/8 inch, or 7.5, 5, 2.5 and 2.5 mm in the order of
    the groups.
  * **Lengths are lengths on paper** (the unit `page.set_routing` takes), **shown in millimetres where the page's scale is given in a metric unit on paper** (a drawing in millimetres, centimetres or metres) and in inches otherwise. **On
    a scaled page the window shows two things that differ**, and says nothing about it: a cell the page does not hold is read by the engine as 0.125 drawing inch (§1.4 of the design, as the jump size takes its own), so on a page of 1 inch to 10 inches
    the tab shows an absent `LineToNodeX` as 0.0125 inch, the paper length that is; **Defaults** fills 0.125, the root's paper value, and OK writes 1.25 drawing inches (`tests/it/routing_tab.rs`,
    `on_a_scaled_page_defaults_are_paper_lengths_written_as_drawing_lengths`). To flip: the engine's default read as paper lengths too, or Defaults in drawing units.
  * **The preview** is two boxes with a third between them, joined by a connector **that `diacraft-route` routes** (the engine's router, in paper inches) with the style, direction, appearance and clearance (Connector to shape) of the draft: a
    right-angle, network or directional style goes round the third box at the clearance, a straight connector and a centre-to-centre one are one leg through it (item 1), a directional style turns the picture to its flow, and a curved
    connector is drawn through the route's corners. **A second line crosses the connector once and the jump the page would make is drawn on it** (Add line jumps to chooses which of the two carries it, the style gives its look, and its chord is
    the spacing between connectors times the size of its direction; a curved connector has none), **drawn four times as large as it is** so that one look can be told from another. It is drawn again only when something it shows changes
    (a counter in the window state), and drawn last in a frame, so that it shows what the controls of the frame chose.
  * **`ui.inspect`** reports the tab as `pageSetup` ("Layout and Routing") and the draft, the Spacing dialog and the preview as `pageSetupRouting` (`null` while the dialog is closed): `style`, `direction`, `directionEnabled`, `separate`,
    `overlap`, `appearance`, `jumps {to, style, vertical, horizontal}`, `other {plow, split}`, `unit`, `spacing` and `spacingDialog` (each group as its two texts), and `preview {computed, outcome, boxes, route, curved, wire, crossing, jump}`;
    `ui.elements` names `pagesetup.routing.{style, direction, separate, overlap, appearance, jump_to, jump_style, vertical_size, vertical_size.box, horizontal_size, horizontal_size.box, plow, split, spacing, preview}` (the rows of an
    open list as `<list>.<word>`) and the Spacing dialog's `routingspacing.{between_shapes, shape_size, connector_to_connector, connector_to_shape}.{x, y}`, `routingspacing.defaults`, `.ok` and `.cancel`.
* **What is left** (the design's later tasks): the router and its use of the clearance and spacing cells, Separate, Overlap and the lean; the Behavior dialog's Connector tab; moving shapes away on drop and splitting connectors (the two boxes are written, nothing acts on them).

## What it costs

One `shape.move` of a shape with a connector on each side, on a page of 500 shapes and 300 connectors, measured by
`crates/engine/tests/it/edit_cost.rs` in the development profile: **about 4 ms**, where the page-wide recalculation it replaced is about 40 ms
on the same page (the test prints both; they move with the load of the machine, and across runs on a busy one a move was 2 to 4 times cheaper
than the whole page, and 10 times on a quiet one). The cost is mostly listing, for the page, the formulas that read other shapes (the glue
formulas, the frame functions and the `Connect` rows), which is done for each command and not kept. Moving 4,096 shapes in one command on a
page of 4,100 takes about 0.15 s, and deleting them about 0.05 s. The connector work added to a move the list of the connectors with a glued end (once for the
command), the `calc` test of each glued end of a connector of a file that follows (one evaluation), and the route of every connector of a file whose
end moved, which the test page's connectors, all ours, did not need.

**Connectors routed again**, counted by the unit tests of `crates/engine/src/draw/route_cost.rs` and timed by its ignored tests (run by hand, each case against a yardstick of plain content of the same size made just before it, in the development profile on a machine at a load of 37 to 47), on crafted pages of 10,000 copies of one connector, glued to box A and box B, which come after them in the page's order, the copies sharing one route section: a move of A that routes the 10,000 again visited 300 million shapes in searches of the page and passed over 200 million `Connect` rows (6.9 s with routes of 4,000 rows); it visits the edit's own two walks and passes over the rows once, and took 3.7 s against 3.9 s for the same move with the connectors set never to reroute (routes of six rows) and 4.3 s against 2.9 s (routes of 4,000 rows). **The floor of that move** (the connectors set never to reroute) grew with the rows of the route the copies share: the recalculation's walks of the sheets passed over 160 million cells and the pricing of the undo step looked at 80 million rows, 4.3 s against 1.1 s with routes of six rows; `calc` now lists a section's formula cells once for a commit and passes by a section that two versions of a sheet hold behind one pointer, and the step is charged a section once and never one that the next version holds (it was charged the route for each copy): 416,130 cells and 4,001 rows, 2.8 s against 2.9 s with six rows. **10,000 ends on a shape of 10,000 connection points** placed and routed by a move of the shape did not finish in a quarter of an hour (4.7 s with a shape of four points): they read the points once, 4.1 s against 3.9 s (glued to a point) and 3.4 s against 3.2 s (to the whole of the shape). **One connector routed beside 10,000 routes of 4,000 rows** read 16 million rows in the jump pass (19.3 s); it reads 400,008, 4.7 s against 3.0 s beside routes of six rows. **A move of the shape 20,000 connectors are glued to** routes 10,000 and says the others: 6.9 s against 6.1 s for the same move that routes none. The pages have no master, no text and no group; their connectors share one section, which is what a paste or a file's copies hold (connectors that each hold a route of their own of thousands of rows are walked once each, as their content is).

**The arrange commands**, measured by `crates/engine/tests/it/arrange.rs` in the development profile on the same page of 500 rectangles of the built-in stencil and 300 connectors
of ours, each glued at both ends by `PAR` formulas (no `_WALKGLUE`, no group, no text, one page; the numbers move with the load of the machine, and the page-wide recalculation is
about 40 ms on it): turning or flipping one shape that has a connector on each side **about 4 ms**; turning or flipping 100 shapes as one (the connectors between them
follow) **about 20 ms**; aligning 100 shapes, 99 of which move, **about 20 ms**; resizing a turned shape **about 4 ms**; reordering one shape or 100 **under 1 ms** (the order is
a list, and nothing is recalculated). At the most ids a command takes, 4,096 shapes on a page of 4,100 with no connectors: turning them as one 0.23 s, flipping 0.22 s, aligning
0.21 s, reordering 0.06 s. The page has no connector of a file glued to the whole of a shape (places those ends for each connector that follows a shape that was
turned), no group, no text and no master with a long list of connection points, and what they cost was not measured here.
**The format commands**, measured by `crates/engine/tests/it/format_cost.rs` in the development profile on the page of `edit_cost.rs` (500
rectangles of the built-in stencil, each an instance holding its pin, and 300 glued connectors) with a label of one run on each rectangle. Medians of
5 to 7 calls, on a quiet run and on one when the machine's load average was 26, both given since they move together with the page-wide recalculation
that is the yardstick: `shape.format` of one shape with a connector on each side (fill, line, weight and end arrow) **3.7 ms** and 9.7 ms, of all 500
shapes 8 ms and 20 ms; `text.format` of one shape (size, bold, colour) 3.7 ms and 9 to 11 ms, of a range (it splits a run) 3.7 ms and 11 ms, of all 500
labels 8.6 ms and 22 ms; `shape.formatting` of one shape 0.01 ms, of all 500 5 ms and 9 ms; the recalculation of every formula of the page, which a
format would cost if it worked out the page, 42 ms and 86 to 89 ms. So one shape is about a ninth of the page in both runs, and 500 shapes about a fifth.
The cost of one shape is the listing of the formulas of the page that `calc` does for each command, as for a move; the writes are a few cells each.
Formatting 4,096 shapes (the most `ids` takes) on a page of 4,100 labelled rectangles took 0.12 s for `shape.format`, 0.13 s for `text.format` and 0.10 s
for `shape.formatting`, and about twice that when loaded. **The fixture lacks** groups, fields, a second run, a theme part, a style chain beyond the
root and any formula that reads a format cell: a file whose line colour is a shade of its fill colour works out that cell too after a fill, and only
that one; the numbers are not claimed for it.

**A text of many runs and shapes named many times**, measured by `format_scale.rs`: the whole text of a label of 1,500 runs with five cells
changed for each run took 28 ms and of 12,000 runs 270 ms (9.6 times for 8 times the runs; the cells a shape plans are found by address, the rows of a
section are found once for a command and held by `IX`, and the rows a split names are held in sets, where a scan of the cells planned so far took 10.5 s
at 12,000 runs); a split in the first run of a text of 12,000 runs, which numbers every run again (a row written for each), 90 ms (9 ms at 1,500); 4,096
names of one group of 5,000 members took 76 ms (the group is walked once), and `shape.formatting` of a group of 25,000 named 4,096 times 40 ms. The fixture
is a label of runs of two letters with a row of its own for each run and no master, style row, field or theme; a text whose rows are partly a style's has
the other numbering (next free), which writes fewer rows. A split of a text whose runs name rows far apart (`cp` 0, then `cp` 40,000
and up) takes the rows it leaves behind out in one pass over the section: 3,000 rows took 17 ms and 24,000 rows 186 ms (11 times for 8 times the rows; a
pass for each row took 23 s at 24,000, a ratio of 62), and the unit tests count one pass for 3,000 rows. A text of 320,000 markers that name one row,
formatted over a range of 199,000 of them, plans two rows (a count, in the unit tests). The answer to "does a master or a style hold a row above 0" no
longer copies the document and builds a resolver: it reads the rows the command found already.

**`shape.formatting` over a range**, counted by the unit tests of `formatting/tests.rs` and timed by `format_scale.rs`, on a load average of about 12: a range over
every run of a text of 1,500 runs, each a row of its own that agrees with the others (so nothing ends the reading early), took 4 ms and of 12,000 runs 23 ms (5.6 times for 8
times the runs: a read of each row and a walk of the parts); a range of ten characters at the far end of the same texts 0.05 ms and 0.36 ms (the walk of the parts, which counts
characters). The worst case is a text of many distinct rows that all agree, nothing to stop the reading early: 30,000 rows that nobody holds read in 46 ms and 300,000 in 0.46 s
(1.5 microseconds a row, linear; measured once with a scratch test, not kept). The counts: 200,000 markers that name two rows read two rows, 100,000 runs with a range over the first three read three rows and walk seven parts, the same text
with a point in the middle reads one run and one paragraph, 16,000 rows that agree are read once each, and rows that differ in every character property stop the reading after
two. The fixture is runs of one letter and the page is the engine's alone: the paragraphs of a long text are found by a scan of its characters for line breaks (`paragraph_bounds`,
one test of a character each, as `text.format`'s `align` does), which was not timed apart.

**The clipboard, group and ungroup commands**, measured by `crates/engine/tests/it/edit_cost.rs` (the page above: 500 rectangles of the built-in stencil and 300 connectors of ours, each glued at both ends by `PAR`
formulas; no `_WALKGLUE`, no group to start with, no text, one page) and `clipboard_limits.rs`, in the development profile on a loaded machine (the numbers move with the load; two runs agreed to
within a tenth). On the 500-shape page, one shape with a connector on each side: copy **about 0.03 ms**, paste **3.5 ms**, duplicate **3.5 ms**, cut **4 ms** (the last three timed with the undo that restores the page, a pointer swap).
Four rows of shapes and their 96 connectors, 196 shapes in all: copy **1.4 ms**, paste **14 ms**, duplicate **15 ms**, cut **6 ms**, group **16 ms**, ungroup **15 ms**, a move of the group **19 ms**. At the most ids
a command takes (4,096) on a page of 4,100 boxes with no connector: copy 26 ms, paste 58 ms, duplicate 88 ms, group 102 ms, ungroup 97 ms, cut 337 ms; on a page of **100,000** boxes with 4,096
ids spread over it: copy 30 ms, paste 164 ms, group 214 ms (the page is walked once for all the ids, `draw/scan.rs`; a search for each id from the top of the page would be about 2e8 visits). The same id named 4,096
times costs what the shape costs (the ids are made distinct before anything is walked). A copy of a group of 50,000 shapes is pasted in 74 ms. One id naming a group of many members: an ungroup takes 0.2 s for 10,000 members, 1.3 s for 40,000 and 1.8 s at the cap of 50,000 (four times the members is about six times the time, which is the write of each member's pin, as for `shape.move`; the bookkeeping around it is one pass, and a test counts it). **What these fixtures lack**: no page holds a connector of a file
glued to the whole of a shape for these runs (`_WALKGLUE` ends are carried and not placed, so a paste or a group does not pay for them, but a later move does), no text with fields, no master with a long
list of connection points, and no page of 100,000 shapes with connectors (the 100,000-shape page has none, so the recalculation after the edit had few formulas to follow). A cut calls `delete_shapes`'s
rest unchanged. **Connectors glued to a shape that goes** (an ungroup, a cut, a delete) are found in one walk of the page (it was a search from the top of the page for each `Connect` row, 18.5 s for 100,000 connectors,
now 0.3 s), so an ungroup of a group with 20,000 connectors glued to it takes 0.3 s (4 times the connectors, about 5 times the time). **What a cut or a delete still pays**: `settle` looks each connector it routes up from the top of the page
(`connectors_to_route`, `refresh_route`, `label::place`), not changed here, so a delete of a shape with 5,000 connectors glued to it takes 0.27 s and with 10,000 about 1 s, and with 20,000 3.8 s (the product of the two).

**The connector commands**, counted, not timed (`crates/engine/tests/it/connect_cost.rs`, `diacraft_calc::work`) on the page of `edit_cost.rs` (500 rectangles and 300 connectors of ours, each
glued at both ends, all level, none crossing another; one page), against the **204,347 steps** of the recalculation of the whole page: `connector.autoconnect` of a copy beside a shape with a connector on each
side **3 commits of 88,447 steps** and of a master 2 commits of 88,991 (a drop, a move and a connector; the page is walked once for the place); `connector.style` of 100 connectors **1 commit of 54,006 steps** (53,606
back to right angle); `connector.reset` of 100 **1 commit of 44,201**; `connector.edit_path` of one **no commit** (it writes constants and cells nothing reads); `connector.line_jumps` on the page, which rebuilds
every connector and writes none that comes out as it was, **no commit**. **The jump pass adds no recalculation to the commands that route a connector** (a `shape.move` of a shape with a connector on each side is 1 commit of
about 45,000 steps, as before); it reads each connector's rows once, which a timing on a quiet run put at about 2 ms more for a move on this page (4.4 ms to 6.5 ms, measured once by hand, not held by a test).
**Crafted**, by the unit test of `draw/jumps.rs` that counts the pairs of legs tested (`spend`): 300 connectors of 200 slanted legs that all overlap (3.6e9 pairs) are given up by the budget of
**4,000,000 pairs** with nothing rewritten, and two such connectors test exactly 2 x 200 x 201 pairs; 2,100 connectors (past the 2,000 that take part) and 20 connectors of 1,000 legs (past the 256 of one that takes part)
make no commit and rewrite nothing. The fixture lacks crossing connectors on a large page (a move that rebuilds the jumps of many neighbours is about the jumps written, not the walk), a file's connectors inheriting
rows from a master, and curved connectors in numbers.

**Stencil files**, measured by `crates/engine/tests/it/stencil_hostile.rs` (crafted, timed; the times print with `--nocapture`; the development profile on a loaded machine, two runs each, and
the bound each test holds is 60 s, which asks whether it hangs and not how fast it is). Work is charged to what a file holds (a `Meter` of 3,000,000 shapes, rows, cells and styles for a copy, 32 MiB of icon
text for a listing, 2,048 masters listed), not to calls. **5,000 masters** (a 3.1 MB file): opening **0.23 to 0.33 s**, `stencil.list` 3 ms (a 252,533-byte answer: 2,048 masters listed), dropping the 4,999th master
0.2 to 0.4 ms, and 300 different masters into one drawing 0.11 to 0.14 s; **3,000 masters with one `UniqueID`**: opening 0.16 to 0.18 s; **a master part of 1.3 MB** (70,000 shapes in a group): opening
35 to 43 ms, a drop **0.6 to 0.9 ms** (past the 5,000 members an instance lists); **4,000 members each with four formulas**, listed: a drop **73 to 90 ms** (the recalculation of what reads the pin), 30,000 members left to
the master 15 to 17 ms; **40,000 members (3.9 MB) that all need a style link and a colour rewritten**: a drop **13 to 17 ms**, saving the drawing 0.11 s and reading it back 0.06 s; **a chain of 20,000 styles**: a first drop 8 to 13 ms and
the next 9 to 27 ms (the search of the drawing's styles by name is made again for each master that is not there already); **an icon of 12 MiB of text**: opening 22 to 26 ms, and refusing it 9 microseconds. A drop searches the drawing's masters
once (a few microseconds for each master it holds). What the fixtures lack: **no real stencil** (every package is built in code), formulas that read other members or are long, thousands of icons that each just fit,
styles that are large sheets, and a drawing of tens of thousands of masters. Reading is the reader's (`crates/vsdx`, whose own crafted tests hold it), and was not found slow on these.

The review's quadratic loops and the memory of open stencils; `stencil_hostile.rs`, `stencil_instances.rs`, `bring/tests.rs`. **The work of a copy is now counted by the tests** (`bring.rs` keeps two counters under `cfg(test)`):
a chain of 3,000 styles into a drawing that has all 3,000 of the name compares **3,000 sheets** (one for each), where a search of the drawing's styles of the name was about 4.5 million; a drawing of 6,000 alike-named styles
that differ from a chain of 6,000 compares **none**, and the time for 6,000 and for 12,000 is 10 and 18 ms (a doubling and not a quadrupling); 300,000 colour numbers against two tables of 4,096 examine **8,192 entries** (each table
once) and cost 34 ms. The whole drop of a chain of 20,000 alike-named styles into a drawing of 30,000 (the review's fixture, 6e8 comparisons by the old search) takes **19 to 26 ms**, and the next 20 to 37 ms; 4,000 masters of 64 shapes
open in 0.5 to 0.6 s (the listing sizes at most 8 shapes of a master and 10,000 of a stencil). **Open stencils are charged by their models**: five files of 4.6 MB each, each holding 96 MiB of XML, open and the sixth is refused (the old measure, the size of the file, took all sixteen, 1.5 GiB of XML). The meter now
also charges the hashing of the drawing's styles of a name (once for each name looked up), the two colour tables, and every kept element and attribute it looks at for a relationship.

`stencil_kept_text.rs`, `bring/tests/kept.rs`, `refs.rs`. **Kept text made to cost** (S7): an element of 60 declarations and 50,000 children pushes **60 bindings** (the first round pushed that for each child) in 5 ms; the review's 30,000 declarations and 30,000 children are refused **before anything is pushed** in 0.4 to 0.7 ms (the first round allocated about 29 GB); a shape that keeps 300,000 declarations and 300,000 prefixed attributes is refused in 7 to 13 ms (4.5e10 compares by a scan of the bindings for each attribute), through the reader and from a model built by hand. **The style search** now hashes every field `Sheet ==` compares (kept attributes and elements of the sheet, section, row and cell, a row's local name), charges each comparison, and counts no comparison for 2,000 styles of a name that differ from the chain's only in each of the ten fields; the re-review's fixture (a stencil of 20,000 styles called "Same" reached by 20,000 shapes against a drawing of 45,000 called "Same" that differ only in a kept cell attribute, 9e8 comparisons by the first hash) drops in **40 ms**, and the next drop 3 ms.

`stencil_line_pins.rs`, `bring/tests/kept.rs`, `refs.rs`. **A line's pin**: the dropped line's pin is `begin + (LocPinX / Width) * (end - begin)` and not always the middle of its ends (a line whose `LocPinX` is 0 has it at its begin, and one whose `LocPinX` is a quarter of its width a quarter along), set only where the master holds the pin as a number, then worked out again so that what reads `PinX` follows; tested for a single line and a line among the members of a dropped group, by cells and by pixels. **Kept text**: a declaration is taken back on leaving its element (each of the two `cut_back` calls is covered, for siblings in both orders, at the top and nested); the declarations of the elements above a kept node in its sheet (shape, sheet, section, row, cell) are in scope for it, in nesting order and taken back on leaving, and a sibling's is not seen (ten places for the owner, ten pairs of an enclosing element and a user, three levels of siblings); a node is charged before it is stacked (200,000 children against a budget of 1,000: 1 step stacked, and 996 of 200,000 at the top of a passthrough, where the first round stacked all of them). **The style search** charges a comparison, and the hash that finds it, a unit for 32 bytes of formula or kept text as well as its nodes (a 3.2 MB formula or kept attribute, equal in the drawing and the stencil, is refused by a budget that the nodes alone passed).

**Page setup and Auto Size**, measured by `crates/engine/tests/it/page_setup_cost.rs` (the times print with `--nocapture`; the development profile, run one test at a time on a machine whose load was moderate; two runs in parallel with other
tests were about three times slower). The page setup commands write a handful of cells and work out their readers (`settle_kept`, not the page): they are not timed. **The hook** (`draw::fit_page`) reads two cells when Auto Size is off. With it on it makes **one walk
of the page** for the shapes the command names (`scan`, not a search for each `ID`) and reads their boxes: a drop inside a page of **100,000** top-level shapes takes 0.74 ms with Auto Size off and 1.74 ms with it on, so the walk is about 1 ms for 100,000 shapes; one `shape.move`
on the page of 500 shapes and 300 connectors above takes 4.2 ms with it off and 4.1 ms with it on (no growth; the page was made wide enough to hold the fixture). **A growth** writes `PageWidth` and `PageHeight`: a drop that grew that page on the right (seven sheets) 3.7 ms.
**A growth on the left or the bottom carries every top-level shape** once (linear in the shapes and the `Connect` rows: the writes of the pins, the cached ends of glued connectors, and the recalculation of what reads a pose): 501 shapes and 300 connectors 23 ms, **19,999 shapes 206 ms**
(the most `MAX_SHIFT_SHAPES` carries, the new shape included); a page of 20,000 shapes is not carried (0.8 ms for the drop). What the fixtures lack: shapes with masters whose pin is a formula, groups with many members, and connectors of a file glued by `_WALKGLUE`
(`lift` carries their cached values); a hostile page of that kind was not timed.

**Starting a drawing from a template**, counted by `crates/engine/tests/it/template.rs` (`diacraft_calc::work`, `diacraft_doc::work`), in the development profile. Making a template
(a new drawing, its page size and turn, its theme, the writer, the reader) is **3 commits of the recalculation and 24 steps, with 17 resolvers built**, for Basic Flowchart, and fewer for Basic Diagram (no theme); `file.new {template}`
costs exactly that and **the same on an empty session and on the page of 500 shapes and 300 connectors it replaces** (a test compares the counts: nothing of the old drawing is touched). A start takes about **3 ms** (a hundred
in a row; printed by the test, not asserted). The package is made again each time and not kept: it is small and the cost is constant. A template **file** costs what `file.open` of it does (the reader's, bounded by its limits), plus a read
of its one cell: at most the first 4 KiB of the text and 64 entries (a test hands a cell of 800 KB, the most the reader allows an attribute, and gets at most 64 names counted). What the fixtures lack: a template file of
thousands of pages or masters (the reader's own tests hold that), and a Shapes window with a hundred open stencil files.

**The shapes a command names are found in one walk of the page** (for the format commands and the page a command works on, for the rest), counted, not timed, by the unit tests of `crates/engine/src/draw/loops_cost.rs`: the shapes `Document::find_shape` visited (`diacraft_doc::work`, a search of the page from its top for one `ID`) and the shapes the walks of `draw/scan.rs` visited, for the most ids each command takes spread from the first shape of a page of 30,000 to its last. The commands: `shape.rotate`, `shape.flip`, `shape.order`, `shape.align` and `shape.resize` of several shapes (`draw/arrange.rs::targets`), `shape.move` (`move_shapes_leaving`) and the moves the engine makes (`move_each`), `shape.delete`, `edit.copy`, `edit.cut` and `shape.duplicate` (`delete_shapes`, and `container::with_contents`, which asks whether a shape among them holds members), `shape.formatting` (`look_of_in`), `connector.reset` (each connector compared before and after), the snaps of `shape.move`, `shape.resize` and `shape.place` and `snap.at` with `ids`, on the 512 shapes a snap takes (`snap::bounds_each`, `box_of`, `own_points`, and `own_points_each` for the points of each shape a place moves by its own distance), `shape.change` on its 512 (the shapes named, and each new instance looked for at the end of the page's list, where the drop put it), `callout.insert` for 4,096 shapes on a page with a theme and an active layer (one pass makes the callouts follow the theme, `theme::follow_page_theme_refs`, and one write puts them on the layers, `layers::join_active_at`), and `fields::refresh` over named shapes (the command takes one). Each looked each shape up from the top of the page: **58.7 million** visits for 4,096 names, 117 million for `shape.delete` and `connector.reset` (two searches each), 263 million and 4,096 walks to make the new shapes follow the theme for `callout.insert`, and 7.6 to 23 million for the commands capped at 512. Now no shape is looked up from the top of the page, and each command walks the page **one to five times in all**, whatever the number named (the page the shapes are on, the shapes, and what follows them: an edit's settling, the callouts and members of a move, the containers of a delete). A shape that is not on the page is refused in the words and the order it was ("page 1 has no shape 99999", the first one named that is missing), and a page that is not there too. **Still a walk for each, of another kind:** `shape.change` finds the next free `ID` for each new instance by a walk of the page (`page_stats`, at most 512 of them), and the connector ends it glues again (at most 4,096) are each looked up and each rebuilds the page's `Connect` rows.

## What is left

* **Templates**: the built-in templates only (Basic Diagram, Basic Flowchart, Cross-Functional Flowchart, Organization Chart and Data Flow Model (Gane-Sarson), and the second stencil batch's as their stencils ship); no thumbnail; no choice of metric or US units when starting (the page is Letter; "Choose metric or US units when starting" is P1); no starter
  diagrams or samples (P2); no search (the window filters the list, which has the `category` of each); a template file is started from by its path, and the folders of templates (File Locations) and the recent templates list are
  the window's and the settings'. A built-in stencil cannot be closed (`stencil.close` refuses it, as before). Basic Diagram offers the Basic Shapes and the Arrow Shapes. A template names
  only built-in stencils; the stencil files open at the moment of a Save As are not kept. A drawing that came from a template opens the stencils its list names. A third
  save of a new drawing is gap F14, not this task's.
* **Snap, grid and guides** (gaps F16): writing the share form of glue to a guide, a single guide cell with no row and a line's end on a guide (read and kept), holding a turned shape or a member of a group to a guide, guide points, shape extension lines and isometric angle lines, a guide at an angle, the shapes of a background page and the members of a group as targets, a page's layers' own snap and glue, the window's own `SnapSettings` in the windows part, and the isometric angles in the Snap & Glue dialog (no setting holds them); the View tab's toggles are saved with the drawing (the dialog, the Visual Aids group and the switches are the window's, and so are the drags and the guides on the page). The flag values of `SnapSettings` (but flags 1 and 2), `GlueSettings` and `SnapExtensions` are not in a specification: the options that would need them are kept in DiaCraft's part until a source gives them.
* **Page setup**: Fit to Drawing, resizing the page by dragging its edge, "page size independent of printer paper" as a choice of its own, print margins and centring (the page breaks are drawn on the page), and background pages' own sizes (`page.size` works on any page, a background too, and nothing keeps a
  background the size of the pages that use it) are not here. Auto Size does not grow the page for a connector's route (only for the shapes a command names) or when it is turned on. A page deleted takes its `ID` with it; `Document::add_page`
  may hand the same `ID` out again. The drawing scales and the sizes of the gallery are ours (no specification lists them). A file's `PaperKind` that is not in the table (user-defined papers: 32767 on 34 page sheets of the census) is Letter for the sheets of a growth.
* A text box does not grow with its text (no cell of it reads `TEXTHEIGHT` or `TEXTWIDTH`). There is no tool that draws a vertical text box (Insert, Text Box, Vertical Text Box: a box is made across and Vertical Text turns its text) and no command for the text block's margins or
  background. The Text Block tool's change to a connector's label lasts until the connector is routed again. The net turn of the text of a member of a flipped group is the `Angle` - `TxtAngle` rule applied at every level
  (the specification gives it for a shape's own flip only, so it is ours and unverified).
* **Stencil files** (gaps F7): a master with a picture, an object, an embedded package or another relationship is refused (until the writer can copy related parts), and so is a master of none or of more than 5,000 top-level shapes (a master of several is dropped as a group, whose frame is ours); a stencil's theme part (left it for the writer to be able to add a theme part, which it can: a drop that put the stencil's part on `Document::themes` when no part there carries its number would now be saved, and what a master selects and which part to bring when the target holds another under that number is for a later task), the masters its formulas name by `USE()` and its data
  connections are not copied; a master is dropped at the size it has, whatever the target page's drawing scale; a master the drawing has changed is used as the drawing has it; a copied style keeps its name, so a drawing can hold two
  of one name; a master of more than 5,000 descendants is dropped without its members listed. The pages a stencil may hold (five of 488 in the census) are not offered: only masters are.

* What a function reads of a sheet that no reference and no frame names is not followed: the theme cells `THEMEVAL` reads, the text
  `TEXTWIDTH` reads. The commands change none of those. A formula that reads cells its text does not name (`LISTSHEETREF()!Width`, the container
  and callout functions, `EVALCELL`) is worked out after every command that changes anything, and a formula that names a sheet that is not
  there is worked out after a command that takes a shape out. A command that changed a master, a style or the document's own sheet would be
  worked out as the whole page (`Changes::whole_page`); the theme commands do, and no other.
* The list of what reads a cell **of its own sheet** (`Width` read by `LocPinX`) is found for a sheet when a change first reaches it, again for each command. The list of what reads a cell **through another sheet** (a qualified reference, a function that carries a point between frames, a `Connect` row), the cells that are worked out after every command (they read what their text does not name), and the cells whose reference finds no sheet are kept by the session from one command to the next (`calc::ReaderIndex`, held by the engine's session, `crates/engine/src/calc_index.rs`): a command that replaces a few shapes puts right what it read of those, by a comparison that skips every list and shape it did not write, so it costs what the command touched and not the formulas of the page (a move on a page of 12,000 shapes asked 168,000 formulas whether they read beyond their sheet before). A command that adds, takes out, moves, renames or gives another master to a shape, that changes a master, a style, the name of a page or the `Connect` rows, or that is an undo to a document the list was not made for, **makes the list again whole**, as every command did: it costs what it cost. The list of a page is kept for one page of the drawing at a time (the page of the command), so a drawing whose commands alternate between two pages makes it for each. **Across pages** (F40): the sheets of every page that hold a formula that names a page (`Pages[Site-2]`, `Pages[2]`) are listed once for the drawing and kept the same way, put right by what each command replaced (the first command in a drawing of two pages or more looks at the text of every formula, a step for 64 bytes of it, and the commands after it at the formulas of the shapes they replaced), and what such a formula reads is found when it is asked, against the drawing as it is then; the list of another page's readers is made when a change first reaches a cell of that page, and kept beside the command's own page, up to 256 pages. **What else reads a page**: the listing also holds the document's sheet, each style's, each master's page sheet and shapes, and an instance of a master shape whose formula names a page (the names are shared and each instance is charged for each name it inherits, and it is looked at only in a drawing in which some master shape names one; the cells found for the instances are charged to the commit, steps and memory, and the routing of the pages a commit reached shares one budget of the evaluator's steps, refused in words when spent); a sheet that calls `EVALTEXT` or `EVALCELL` is read as naming every page, so its cells that read at run time are worked out once after the first change to a cell of any page; and a page a change reaches has the cells of its own that read what their text does not name worked out, as the commit's page has (the commands that change the pages themselves are). **The sheets no page holds**: the listing also says which sheets name the document's sheet (`TheDoc!`), a style (`Styles!Name!`) and a master (`Masters[Name]!`), and a cell of one of those that a commit worked out is read by those sheets on every page, found as the cells that name a page are and classified when first asked, in the same commit; the sheets of the commit's own page are answered by its graph. **The sheets that name the document's sheet or a style are listed only when a chain can change it** (its document sheet, or a style, holds a formula that reads beyond its own sheet: the cells of a sheet that reads only itself change only by a write to it, which works every page out whole, and the text of a formula that names only `TheDoc!` is not even walked otherwise), and the masters always are. **A formula a shape inherits from a style** is listed and classified for the shape as one it inherits from a master is: a cell the shape holds as `Inh` whose formula the chain finds on a style is that formula, worked out on the shape, **and asked only of a shape a link of which (or of its master shape) names a style that holds a formula that names a page or another sheet, reads at run time or reads beyond its sheet** (a step for each style and for each cell asked, so a drawing whose styles hold none costs a step for each style and nothing for a shape); the listing of a page made before such a style changed is made again, and a shape given another style link is classified again. **Not followed:** a cell that reads a style's or a master's cell by inheriting its value (it holds no formula of the cell, takes the value from the style or the master shape, and a cell of its own sheet reads it by its plain name) is worked out when its own cell is and not because the style's or the master's was; a cell of a style, a master or the document's sheet that reads a number written to the document's sheet or to a style (`TheDoc!`, `Styles!`) is not worked out by that write while the sheet written holds no formula that reads beyond itself; a master or a style that is renamed is not a change to the names a formula finds it by; and a text a cell holds and another reads as a formula by converting it to a number is read where it is found.
* Full routing (avoiding every shape, spreading legs, the other route styles) replaces `draw::route`. A route here goes round the boxes of the two shapes it is glued to and
  **straight through any other shape that is in its way**; a curved connector cuts the corners of its route, so it can clip a shape the route passes close to; the flowchart, tree, network and simple styles are right angle.
* Group resize. An end glued to the whole of a shape goes to the box of the shape and not its drawn curve.
* Rotating and flipping the member of a turned or flipped group, and distributing shapes. A formula that reads the stacking order (`CONTAINERSHEETREF`, `LISTORDER`) is not worked out again after `shape.order`, which changes no cell; a flip of a file's connector with a bent route and no glued end keeps its rows (ROTATE-1D-1).
* `_WALKGLUE` is placed by the engine's rule and not the reference app's, which no source gives, so a file's dynamic glue may pick another
  point than the application that wrote it; `WalkPreference` is not read.
* A connector of a file that is centre to centre is left alone when a shape moves, and its rows follow only where they have formulas that read `Width`. One with `ConFixedCode` 1, 2 or 3 (a path edited by hand among them) is not
  routed again, but for a leg that would cross a shape it is glued to under 1 and 3: its interior corners stay where they are on the page and its end legs stretch along their own direction
  (above), where its bends stayed in the connector's frame; a curved route, one of more than `MAX_HAND_POINTS` points and one with no glued end keep their rows as they were. The values are the specification's.
* Line jumps are made when connectors are routed and when the page's jump cells are written; a paste, a group, an ungroup and a file's open make none, so a pasted connector keeps the jumps it had and does not make its
  neighbours jump. A connector in a group takes no part. The rows of 3 to 7 sides are an arc. The application's dynamic glue (`_WALKGLUE`) is written only for the whole of a shape that has no connection point (said never; the application drops such glue without the formulas): AutoConnect, like `connector.add`, glues such a shape to the whole of it, with the `_WALKGLUE` formulas in the end cells and a trigger that names the shape, and the engine places the ends.
* The shapes' clipboard is within one document: a drawing that is made or opened empties it, so a paste in another drawing is not done (the matching of a stencil's masters to a document's, is there); Paste Special and Paste as Hyperlink are not done, and the system clipboard gets the text of the labels and of every text field, where a paste in a text field takes text from it, while a paste of shapes stays within DiaCraft. A shape with a
  picture is pasted on its own page only (the writer does not add relationships to the page part). A member of a group that takes its cells from a master group is copied with its group only, and a group that is an
  instance of a master is not ungrouped (its members would lose the cells they take from it; making them local is not done). A connector cannot be carried out of a flipped group, copied or ungrouped. A group named with a group
  it is in is not taken apart in the same call. Pages of different scales are not compared on a paste (the cells are copied as they are). A paste does not carry layers, which are the page's.
* A member made from an instance holds `Width`, `Height`, `PinX` and `PinY` as formulas of its group and a local copy of its master's `Geometry` (gaps F8). A one-dimensional instance, the size of a member turned by other than a half turn, a cell with a formula of its own and a group with no extent keep their numbers (no count gives a form), `LocPinX` and `LocPinY` stay inherited, and `shape.resize` sizes a group and the formulas are what its members follow (`shape.size` still refuses a group), and a plain group inside a group and the shapes with no master follow it by their numbers (the stretch of the group's frame) and not by a formula.
* A connector of ours that is carried out of a turned group keeps the legs it was drawn with, slanted on the page (it draws where it did); a move of it, or of a shape it is glued to, routes it again.
* A group is sized by `shape.resize` as one shape and its members follow (`shape.size` still refuses a group, `shape.resize` refuses a member of a turned or flipped group, and `shape.size` does not). `shape_frame` of a
  member gives its box in its group's frame.
* Size & Position: a pin is not dragged (the window has no handle for it yet); the pin of a line or a connector is not set; several shapes are given one X or one Y by `shape.place`
  (the Size & Position pane sends one `shape.place`); a glued end is not typed into (`connector.reconnect` to a place takes the glue off first); a line of no length is not given a length of nothing.
* A text edit is plain characters: no choice of font, size or colour for the characters typed (they take the run they join; `text.format` changes
  them afterwards), no paragraph or tab markers added or taken away by an edit, and a field is not typed: `text.insert_field` puts one in (Insert, Text, Field).
* Formatting does not touch: the transparency of text (`ColorTrans`), `AsianFont` and `ComplexScriptFont`, `Pos`, `FontScale`, `Letterspace`, `DblUnderline`, `IndRight`,
  `IndFirst` but for a bullet's hanging form, line spacing, a bullet of one's own (`text.format`'s bullets are a table of seven marks) and tab stops. A shadow is `shape.shadow`,
  a gradient's stops `shape.gradient`, the fill's and the line's transparency, a line cap and the size of an arrowhead `shape.format`, and the left
  indent, the bullets, the case, the reading direction and vertical text `text.format`. In the case where a master or a style holds a row of `Character` or `Paragraph` at `IX` 1 or above (about 1 text in 100), a split numbers the
  new rows after the rows there are, so a reader that maps runs to rows by position shows a split in a run that has later
  runs wrong there. The rows a split does not write whole (a row left alone or changed in place) are not filled in for such a reader. The theme's marker
  in `Style` that the theme cannot answer reads as no bits.
* `shape.formatting` over a range reads the shape's **own** text, as the range of `text.format` and `shape.set_text` does: a shape that shows its master's
  text and has none of its own has no characters to range over, and the point `0` to `0` there reads row 0, which is the row the first character typed in it
  would take. A range of a group (name a member) and a range of several shapes (the window decides what a selection of several shows) are refused.
* The window's text box shows one face and size for all the characters, not the runs' (the picture of the page shows them), and the fields are shown
  under the characters, not where they stand. With a box open the Font group shows the characters selected, or the run before the caret (gap U19, settled); a caret
  still formats the whole text.
* A file's modified time can be set back to what it was by whatever changed it, and a change that keeps the size and the time (an edit within one
  tick of the file system's clock) is not seen: the check for a file changed on the disk is the size and the time, not the bytes.
